children.name: Information Technology Project Managers
children.description: Plan, initiate, and manage information technology (IT) projects. Lead and guide the work of technical staff. Serve as liaison between business and technical aspects of projects. Plan project stages and assess business implications for each stage. Monitor progress to assure deadlines, standards, and cost targets are met.

name: Architecture and Engineering Occupations
description: Involves designing, planning, and building structures, systems, and technologies. Includes architects, civil engineers, mechanical engineers, and others applying scientific and mathematical principles to solve technical challenges.

children.name: Architects, Surveyors, and Cartographers
children.description: Architects, Surveyors, and Cartographers are professionals who specialize in the design and mapping of structures, land, and geographical features. This category includes occupations such as architects, landscape architects, surveyors, and cartographers.

children.name: Architects, Except Naval
children.description: Plan and design structures—such as buildings and other physical environments—while considering functionality, aesthetics, safety, and regulatory requirements.

children.name: Architects, Except Landscape and Naval
children.description: Plan and design structures, such as private residences, office buildings, theaters, factories, and other structural property.

children.name: Landscape Architects
children.description: Plan and design land areas for projects such as parks and other recreational facilities, airports, highways, hospitals, schools, land subdivisions, and commercial, industrial, and residential sites.

children.name: Surveyors, Cartographers, and Photogrammetrists
children.description: Measure and map the Earth’s surface, establish property boundaries, and create detailed geographic data. May interpret aerial or satellite imagery for cartographic or photogrammetric purposes.

children.name: Cartographers and Photogrammetrists
children.description: Research, study, and prepare maps and other spatial data in digital or graphic form for one or more purposes, such as legal, social, political, educational, and design purposes. May work with Geographic Information Systems (GIS). May design and evaluate algorithms, data structures, and user interfaces for GIS and mapping systems. May collect, analyze, and interpret geographic information provided by geodetic surveys, aerial photographs, and satellite data.

children.name: Surveyors
children.description: Make exact measurements and determine property boundaries. Provide data relevant to the shape, contour, gravitation, location, elevation, or dimension of land or land features on or near the earth's surface for engineering, mapmaking, mining, land evaluation, construction, and other purposes.

children.name: Geodetic Surveyors
children.description: Measure large areas of the Earth's surface using satellite observations, global navigation satellite systems (GNSS), light detection and ranging (LIDAR), or related sources.

children.name: Engineers
children.description: Engineers are professionals who apply scientific and mathematical principles to design, develop, and improve various systems, structures, and technologies. This category includes a wide range of engineering occupations, such as civil engineers, mechanical engineers, electrical engineers, aerospace engineers, and chemical engineers, among others.

children.name: Aerospace Engineers
children.description: Design, develop, and test aircraft, spacecraft, or missiles, ensuring they meet engineering principles and regulatory requirements for performance, safety, and efficiency.

children.name: Aerospace Engineers
children.description: Perform engineering duties in designing, constructing, and testing aircraft, missiles, and spacecraft. May conduct basic and applied research to evaluate adaptability of materials and equipment to aircraft design and manufacture. May recommend improvements in testing equipment and techniques.

children.name: Agricultural Engineers
children.description: Apply engineering and biological principles to solve agricultural problems, such as designing improved machinery, irrigation systems, or pollution controls for farm operations.

children.name: Agricultural Engineers
children.description: Apply knowledge of engineering technology and biological science to agricultural problems concerned with power and machinery, electrification, structures, soil and water conservation, and processing of agricultural products.

children.name: Biomedical Engineers
children.description: Combine knowledge of engineering, biology, and biomechanics to design and improve medical devices and procedures that enhance healthcare.

children.name: Bioengineers and Biomedical Engineers
children.description: Apply knowledge of engineering, biology, chemistry, computer science, and biomechanical principles to the design, development, and evaluation of biological, agricultural, and health systems and products, such as artificial organs, prostheses, instrumentation, medical information systems, and health management and care delivery systems.

children.name: Chemical Engineers
children.description: Design and oversee processes for manufacturing chemicals and products, such as fuels, pharmaceuticals, and plastics, applying chemistry, physics, and engineering principles.

children.name: Chemical Engineers
children.description: Design chemical plant equipment and devise processes for manufacturing chemicals and products, such as gasoline, synthetic rubber, plastics, detergents, cement, paper, and pulp, by applying principles and technology of chemistry, physics, and engineering.

children.name: Civil Engineers
children.description: Plan, design, and supervise construction and maintenance of infrastructure such as roads, bridges, dams, water treatment systems, and other public works projects.

children.name: Civil Engineers
children.description: Perform engineering duties in planning, designing, and overseeing construction and maintenance of building structures and facilities, such as roads, railroads, airports, bridges, harbors, channels, dams, irrigation projects, pipelines, power plants, and water and sewage systems.

children.name: Transportation Engineers
children.description: Develop plans for surface transportation projects, according to established engineering standards and state or federal construction policy. Prepare designs, specifications, or estimates for transportation facilities. Plan modifications of existing streets, highways, or freeways to improve traffic flow.

children.name: Computer Hardware Engineers
children.description: Research, design, develop, and test computer hardware systems and components, ensuring seamless integration with software and user needs.

children.name: Computer Hardware Engineers
children.description: Research, design, develop, or test computer or computer-related equipment for commercial, industrial, military, or scientific use. May supervise the manufacturing and installation of computer or computer-related equipment and components.

children.name: Electrical and Electronics Engineers
children.description: Design, develop, and evaluate electronic or electrical systems and components, ranging from power generation equipment to consumer electronics and communications systems.

children.name: Electrical Engineers
children.description: Research, design, develop, test, or supervise the manufacturing and installation of electrical equipment, components, or systems for commercial, industrial, military, or scientific use.

children.name: Electronics Engineers, Except Computer
children.description: Research, design, develop, or test electronic components and systems for commercial, industrial, military, or scientific use employing knowledge of electronic theory and materials properties. Design electronic circuits and components for use in fields such as telecommunications, aerospace guidance and propulsion control, acoustics, or instruments and controls.

children.name: Radio Frequency Identification Device Specialists
children.description: Design and implement radio frequency identification device (RFID) systems used to track shipments or goods.

children.name: Environmental Engineers
children.description: Develop solutions to environmental problems using engineering, soil science, biology, and chemistry. Design systems to manage water, air, or soil quality, and reduce environmental impact.

children.name: Environmental Engineers
children.description: Research, design, plan, or perform engineering duties in the prevention, control, and remediation of environmental hazards using various engineering disciplines. Work may include waste treatment, site remediation, or pollution control technology.

children.name: Water/Wastewater Engineers
children.description: Design or oversee projects involving provision of potable water, disposal of wastewater and sewage, or prevention of flood-related damage. Prepare environmental documentation for water resources, regulatory program compliance, data management and analysis, and field work. Perform hydraulic modeling and pipeline design.

children.name: Industrial Engineers, Including Health and Safety
children.description: Design, optimize, and evaluate integrated systems for managing industrial production processes, often emphasizing efficiency, cost reduction, and worker safety.

children.name: Health and Safety Engineers, Except Mining Safety Engineers and Inspectors
children.description: Promote worksite or product safety by applying knowledge of industrial processes, mechanics, chemistry, psychology, and industrial health and safety laws. Includes industrial product safety engineers.

children.name: Industrial Safety and Health Engineers
children.description: Plan, implement, and coordinate safety programs, requiring application of engineering principles and technology, to prevent or correct unsafe environmental working conditions.

children.name: Fire-Prevention and Protection Engineers
children.description: Research causes of fires, determine fire protection methods, and design or recommend materials or equipment such as structural components or fire-detection equipment to assist organizations in safeguarding life and property against fire, explosion, and related hazards.

children.name: Product Safety Engineers
children.description: Develop and conduct tests to evaluate product safety levels and recommend measures to reduce or eliminate hazards.

children.name: Industrial Engineers
children.description: Design, develop, test, and evaluate integrated systems for managing industrial production processes, including human work factors, quality control, inventory control, logistics and material flow, cost analysis, and production coordination.

children.name: Human Factors Engineers and Ergonomists
children.description: Design objects, facilities, and environments to optimize human well-being and overall system performance, applying theory, principles, and data regarding the relationship between humans and respective technology. Investigate and analyze characteristics of human behavior and performance as it relates to the use of technology.

children.name: Marine Engineers and Naval Architects
children.description: Design, develop, and evaluate the construction, operation, and maintenance of ships, submarines, and other marine vessels. Analyze hulls, propulsion systems, and other components.

children.name: Marine Engineers and Naval Architects
children.description: Design, develop, and evaluate the operation of marine vessels, ship machinery, and related equipment, such as power supply and propulsion systems.

children.name: Marine Engineers
children.description: Design, develop, and take responsibility for the installation of ship machinery and related equipment including propulsion machines and power supply systems.

children.name: Marine Architects
children.description: Design and oversee construction and repair of marine craft and floating structures such as ships, barges, tugs, dredges, submarines, torpedoes, floats, and buoys. May confer with marine engineers.

children.name: Materials Engineers
children.description: Evaluate and develop materials for specific uses. Study and create new materials—like metals, polymers, and composites—to meet specialized performance requirements in products or systems.

children.name: Materials Engineers
children.description: Evaluate materials and develop machinery and processes to manufacture materials for use in products that must meet specialized design and performance specifications. Develop new uses for known materials. Includes those engineers working with composite materials or specializing in one type of material, such as graphite, metal and metal alloys, ceramics and glass, plastics and polymers, and naturally occurring materials. Includes metallurgists and metallurgical engineers, ceramic engineers, and welding engineers.

children.name: Mechanical Engineers
children.description: Research, design, develop, and test mechanical devices and systems, including engines, machines, and tools, focusing on improving efficiency and safety.

children.name: Mechanical Engineers
children.description: Perform engineering duties in planning and designing tools, engines, machines, and other mechanically functioning equipment. Oversee installation, operation, maintenance, and repair of equipment such as centralized heat, gas, water, and steam systems.

children.name: Fuel Cell Engineers
children.description: Design, evaluate, modify, or construct fuel cell components or systems for transportation, stationary, or portable applications.

children.name: Automotive Engineers
children.description: Develop new or improved designs for vehicle structural members, engines, transmissions, or other vehicle systems, using computer-assisted design technology. Direct building, modification, or testing of vehicle or components.

children.name: Mining and Geological Engineers, Including Mining Safety Engineers
children.description: Plan and oversee mining operations for safe, efficient extraction of minerals. Evaluate potential mine locations, design extraction processes, and implement safety measures.

children.name: Mining and Geological Engineers, Including Mining Safety Engineers
children.description: Conduct subsurface surveys to identify the characteristics of potential land or mining development sites. May specify the ground support systems, processes, and equipment for safe, economical, and environmentally sound extraction or underground construction activities. May inspect areas for unsafe geological conditions, equipment, and working conditions. May design, implement, and coordinate mine safety programs.

children.name: Nuclear Engineers
children.description: Research and apply nuclear science principles to problems involving nuclear energy, radiation, nuclear waste disposal, and related systems.

children.name: Nuclear Engineers
children.description: Conduct research on nuclear engineering projects or apply principles and theory of nuclear science to problems concerned with release, control, and use of nuclear energy and nuclear waste disposal.

children.name: Petroleum Engineers
children.description: Design methods for extracting oil and gas from deposits below the Earth’s surface. Oversee drilling and production operations and develop new techniques to enhance recovery.

children.name: Petroleum Engineers
children.description: Devise methods to improve oil and gas extraction and production and determine the need for new or modified tool designs. Oversee drilling and offer technical advice.

children.name: Miscellaneous Engineers
children.description: Perform specialized engineering duties not classified under other engineering roles, often in cutting-edge or highly specialized areas.

children.name: Engineers, All Other
children.description: All engineers not listed separately.

children.name: Biochemical Engineers
children.description: Develop usable, tangible products, using knowledge of biology, chemistry, or engineering. Solve problems related to materials, systems, or processes that interact with humans, plants, animals, microorganisms, or biological materials.

children.name: Validation Engineers
children.description: Design or plan protocols for equipment or processes to produce products meeting internal and external purity, safety, and quality requirements.

children.name: Energy Engineers, Except Wind and Solar
children.description: Design, develop, or evaluate energy-related projects or programs to reduce energy costs or improve energy efficiency during the designing, building, or remodeling stages of construction. May specialize in electrical systems; heating, ventilation, and air-conditioning (HVAC) systems; green buildings; lighting; air quality; or energy procurement.

children.name: Manufacturing Engineers
children.description: Design, integrate, or improve manufacturing systems or related processes. May work with commercial or industrial designers to refine product designs to increase producibility and decrease costs.

children.name: Mechatronics Engineers
children.description: Research, design, develop, or test automation, intelligent systems, smart devices, or industrial systems control.

children.name: Microsystems Engineers
children.description: Research, design, develop, or test microelectromechanical systems (MEMS) devices.

children.name: Photonics Engineers
children.description: Design technologies specializing in light information or light energy, such as laser or fiber optics technology.

children.name: Robotics Engineers
children.description: Research, design, develop, or test robotic applications.

children.name: Nanosystems Engineers
children.description: Design, develop, or supervise the production of materials, devices, or systems of unique molecular or macromolecular composition, applying principles of nanoscale physics and electrical, chemical, or biological engineering.

children.name: Wind Energy Engineers
children.description: Design underground or overhead wind farm collector systems and prepare and develop site specifications.

children.name: Solar Energy Systems Engineers
children.description: Perform site-specific engineering analysis or evaluation of energy efficiency and solar projects involving residential, commercial, or industrial customers. Design solar domestic hot water and space heating systems for new and existing structures, applying knowledge of structural energy requirements, local climates, solar technology, and thermodynamics.

children.name: Drafters, Engineering Technicians, and Mapping Technicians
children.description: Drafters, Engineering Technicians, and Mapping Technicians provide technical support and assist engineers, architects, and surveyors in various stages of design, development, and mapping processes.

children.name: Drafters
children.description: Create detailed technical drawings and plans for buildings, structures, or products using computer-aided design (CAD) software.

children.name: Architectural and Civil Drafters
children.description: Prepare detailed drawings of architectural and structural features of buildings or drawings and topographical relief maps used in civil engineering projects, such as highways, bridges, and public works. Use knowledge of building materials, engineering practices, and mathematics to complete drawings.

children.name: Architectural Drafters
children.description: Prepare detailed drawings of architectural designs and plans for buildings and structures according to specifications provided by architect.

children.name: Civil Drafters
children.description: Prepare drawings and topographical and relief maps used in civil engineering projects, such as highways, bridges, pipelines, flood control projects, and water and sewerage control systems.

children.name: Electrical and Electronics Drafters
children.description: Prepare wiring diagrams, circuit board assembly diagrams, and layout drawings used for the manufacture, installation, or repair of electrical equipment.

children.name: Electronic Drafters
children.description: Draw wiring diagrams, circuit board assembly diagrams, schematics, and layout drawings used for manufacture, installation, and repair of electronic equipment.

children.name: Electrical Drafters
children.description: Develop specifications and instructions for installation of voltage transformers, overhead or underground cables, and related electrical equipment used to conduct electrical energy from transmission lines or high-voltage distribution lines to consumers.

children.name: Mechanical Drafters
children.description: Prepare detailed working diagrams of machinery and mechanical devices, including dimensions, fastening methods, and other engineering information.

children.name: Drafters, All Other
children.description: All drafters not listed separately.

children.name: Engineering Technicians, Except Drafters
children.description: Support engineers in research, development, design, or production. Collect data, run tests, set up equipment, and help ensure quality in engineering processes.

children.name: Aerospace Engineering and Operations Technologists and Technicians
children.description: Operate, install, adjust, and maintain integrated computer/communications systems, consoles, simulators, and other data acquisition, test, and measurement instruments and equipment, which are used to launch, track, position, and evaluate air and space vehicles. May record and interpret test data.

children.name: Civil Engineering Technologists and Technicians
children.description: Apply theory and principles of civil engineering in planning, designing, and overseeing construction and maintenance of structures and facilities under the direction of engineering staff or physical scientists.

children.name: Electrical and Electronic Engineering Technologists and Technicians
children.description: Apply electrical and electronic theory and related knowledge, usually under the direction of engineering staff, to design, build, repair, adjust, and modify electrical components, circuitry, controls, and machinery for subsequent evaluation and use by engineering staff in making engineering design decisions.

children.name: Electronics Engineering Technicians
children.description: Lay out, build, test, troubleshoot, repair, and modify developmental and production electronic components, parts, equipment, and systems, such as computer equipment, missile control instrumentation, electron tubes, test equipment, and machine tool numerical controls, applying principles and theories of electronics, electrical circuitry, engineering mathematics, electronic and electrical testing, and physics. Usually work under direction of engineering staff.

children.name: Electrical Engineering Technicians
children.description: Test or modify developmental or operational electrical machinery or electrical control equipment and circuitry in industrial or commercial plants or laboratories. Usually work under direction of engineers or technologists.

children.name: Electro-Mechanical and Mechatronics Technologists and Technicians
children.description: Operate, test, maintain, or adjust unmanned, automated, servomechanical, or electromechanical equipment. May operate unmanned submarines, aircraft, or other equipment to observe or record visual information at sites such as oil rigs, crop fields, buildings, or for similar infrastructure, deep ocean exploration, or hazardous waste removal. May assist engineers in testing and designing robotics equipment.

children.name: Robotics Technicians
children.description: Build, install, test, or maintain robotic equipment or related automated production systems.

children.name: Environmental Engineering Technologists and Technicians
children.description: Apply theory and principles of environmental engineering to modify, test, and operate equipment and devices used in the prevention, control, and remediation of environmental problems, including waste treatment and site remediation, under the direction of engineering staff or scientists. May assist in the development of environmental remediation devices.

children.name: Industrial Engineering Technologists and Technicians
children.description: Apply engineering theory and principles to problems of industrial layout or manufacturing production, usually under the direction of engineering staff. May perform time and motion studies on worker operations in a variety of industries for purposes such as establishing standard production rates or improving efficiency.

children.name: Nanotechnology Engineering Technologists and Technicians
children.description: Implement production processes and operate commercial-scale production equipment to produce, test, or modify materials, devices, or systems of unique molecular or macromolecular composition. Operate advanced microscopy equipment to manipulate nanoscale objects. Work under the supervision of nanoengineering staff.

children.name: Mechanical Engineering Technologists and Technicians
children.description: Apply theory and principles of mechanical engineering to modify, develop, test, or adjust machinery and equipment under direction of engineering staff or physical scientists.

children.name: Automotive Engineering Technicians
children.description: Assist engineers in determining the practicality of proposed product design changes and plan and carry out tests on experimental test devices or equipment for performance, durability, or efficiency.

children.name: Calibration Technologists and Technicians
children.description: Execute or adapt procedures and techniques for calibrating measurement devices, by applying knowledge of measurement science, mathematics, physics, chemistry, and electronics, sometimes under the direction of engineering staff. Determine measurement standard suitability for calibrating measurement devices. May perform preventive maintenance on equipment. May perform corrective actions to address identified calibration problems.

children.name: Engineering Technologists and Technicians, Except Drafters, All Other
children.description: All engineering technologists and technicians, except drafters, not listed separately.

children.name: Non-Destructive Testing Specialists
children.description: Test the safety of structures, vehicles, or vessels using x-ray, ultrasound, fiber optic or related equipment.

children.name: Electrical Engineering Technologists
children.description: Assist electrical engineers in such activities as process control, electrical power distribution, or instrumentation design. May prepare layouts of electrical transmission or distribution systems, supervise the flow of work, estimate project costs, or participate in research studies.

children.name: Electromechanical Engineering Technologists
children.description: Assist electromechanical engineers in such activities as computer-based process control, instrumentation, or machine design. May prepare layouts of machinery or equipment, plan the flow of work, conduct statistical studies, or analyze production costs.

children.name: Electronics Engineering Technologists
children.description: Assist electronics engineers in such activities as electronics systems and instrumentation design or digital signal processing.

children.name: Industrial Engineering Technologists
children.description: Assist industrial engineers in such activities as quality control, inventory control, or material flow methods. May conduct statistical studies or analyze production costs.

children.name: Manufacturing Engineering Technologists
children.description: Develop tools, implement designs, or integrate machinery, equipment, or computer technologies to ensure effective manufacturing processes.

children.name: Mechanical Engineering Technologists
children.description: Assist mechanical engineers in such activities as generation, transmission, or use of mechanical or fluid energy. Prepare layouts of machinery or equipment or plan the flow of work. May conduct statistical studies or analyze production costs.

children.name: Photonics Technicians
children.description: Build, install, test, or maintain optical or fiber optic equipment, such as lasers, lenses, or mirrors, using spectrometers, interferometers, or related equipment.

children.name: Manufacturing Production Technicians
children.description: Set up, test, and adjust manufacturing machinery or equipment, using any combination of electrical, electronic, mechanical, hydraulic, pneumatic, or computer technologies.

children.name: Fuel Cell Technicians
children.description: Install, operate, or maintain integrated fuel cell systems in transportation, stationary, or portable applications.

children.name: Nanotechnology Engineering Technologists
children.description: Implement production processes for nanoscale designs to produce or modify materials, devices, or systems of unique molecular or macromolecular composition. Operate advanced microscopy equipment to manipulate nanoscale objects. Work under the supervision of nanoengineering staff.

children.name: Nanotechnology Engineering Technicians
children.description: Operate commercial-scale production equipment to produce, test, or modify materials, devices, or systems of molecular or macromolecular composition. Work under the supervision of engineering staff.

children.name: Surveying and Mapping Technicians
children.description: Assist surveyors and cartographers by collecting data in the field, verifying measurements, drafting maps, and updating geographic information systems.

children.name: Surveying and Mapping Technicians
children.description: Perform surveying and mapping duties, usually under the direction of an engineer, surveyor, cartographer, or photogrammetrist, to obtain data used for construction, mapmaking, boundary location, mining, or other purposes. May calculate mapmaking information and create maps from source data, such as surveying notes, aerial photography, satellite data, or other maps to show topographical features, political boundaries, and other features. May verify accuracy and completeness of maps.

children.name: Surveying Technicians
children.description: Adjust and operate surveying instruments, such as the theodolite and electronic distance-measuring equipment, and compile notes, make sketches and enter data into computers.

children.name: Mapping Technicians
children.description: Calculate mapmaking information from field notes, and draw and verify accuracy of topographical maps.

name: Life, Physical, and Social Science Occupations
description: Includes scientists and researchers who study living organisms, physical phenomena, and social systems. Examples range from chemists and biologists to sociologists and economists, often working in labs, field settings, or academic institutions.

children.name: Life Scientists
children.description: Life Scientists are professionals who study living organisms and their interactions with the environment. This category includes various occupations related to biological and life sciences, such as biochemists, biophysicists, microbiologists, zoologists, and botanists, among others.

children.name: Agricultural and Food Scientists
children.description: Research ways to improve the efficiency and safety of agricultural establishments and food products. Study soil composition, pest control, breeding, or processing techniques.

children.name: Animal Scientists
children.description: Conduct research in the genetics, nutrition, reproduction, growth, and development of domestic farm animals.

children.name: Food Scientists and Technologists
children.description: Use chemistry, microbiology, engineering, and other sciences to study the principles underlying the processing and deterioration of foods; analyze food content to determine levels of vitamins, fat, sugar, and protein; discover new food sources; research ways to make processed foods safe, palatable, and healthful; and apply food science knowledge to determine best ways to process, package, preserve, store, and distribute food.

children.name: Soil and Plant Scientists
children.description: Conduct research in breeding, physiology, production, yield, and management of crops and agricultural plants or trees, shrubs, and nursery stock, their growth in soils, and control of pests; or study the chemical, physical, biological, and mineralogical composition of soils as they relate to plant or crop growth. May classify and map soils and investigate effects of alternative practices on soil and crop productivity.

children.name: Biological Scientists
children.description: Study living organisms and their relationship to the environment, potentially specializing in fields like microbiology, ecology, zoology, or genetics.

children.name: Biologists
children.description: Research or study basic principles of plant and animal life, such as origin, relationship, development, anatomy, and functions.

children.name: Biochemists and Biophysicists
children.description: Study the chemical composition or physical principles of living cells and organisms, their electrical and mechanical energy, and related phenomena. May conduct research to further understanding of the complex chemical combinations and reactions involved in metabolism, reproduction, growth, and heredity. May determine the effects of foods, drugs, serums, hormones, and other substances on tissues and vital processes of living organisms.

children.name: Microbiologists
children.description: Investigate the growth, structure, development, and other characteristics of microscopic organisms, such as bacteria, algae, or fungi. Includes medical microbiologists who study the relationship between organisms and disease or the effects of antibiotics on microorganisms.

children.name: Zoologists and Wildlife Biologists
children.description: Study the origins, behavior, diseases, genetics, and life processes of animals and wildlife. May specialize in wildlife research and management. May collect and analyze biological data to determine the environmental effects of present and potential use of land and water habitats.

children.name: Biological Scientists, All Other
children.description: All biological scientists not listed separately.

children.name: Bioinformatics Scientists
children.description: Conduct research using bioinformatics theory and methods in areas such as pharmaceuticals, medical technology, biotechnology, computational biology, proteomics, computer information science, biology and medical informatics. May design databases and develop algorithms for processing and analyzing genomic information, or other biological information.

children.name: Molecular and Cellular Biologists
children.description: Research and study cellular molecules and organelles to understand cell function and organization.

children.name: Geneticists
children.description: Research and study the inheritance of traits at the molecular, organism or population level. May evaluate or treat patients with genetic disorders.

children.name: Biologists
children.description: Research or study basic principles of plant and animal life, such as origin, relationship, development, anatomy, and functions.

children.name: Conservation Scientists and Foresters
children.description: Manage and protect natural resources by advising on forest management, soil conservation, and land-use planning. May develop sustainable resource management strategies.

children.name: Conservation Scientists
children.description: Manage, improve, and protect natural resources to maximize their use without damaging the environment. May conduct soil surveys and develop plans to eliminate soil erosion or to protect rangelands. May instruct farmers, agricultural production managers, or ranchers in best ways to use crop rotation, contour plowing, or terracing to conserve soil and water; in the number and kind of livestock and forage plants best suited to particular ranges; and in range and farm improvements, such as fencing and reservoirs for stock watering.

children.name: Soil and Water Conservationists
children.description: Plan or develop coordinated practices for soil erosion control, soil or water conservation, or sound land use.

children.name: Range Managers
children.description: Research or study range land management practices to provide sustained production of forage, livestock, and wildlife.

children.name: Park Naturalists
children.description: Plan, develop, and conduct programs to inform public of historical, natural, and scientific features of national, state, or local park.

children.name: Foresters
children.description: Manage public and private forested lands for economic, recreational, and conservation purposes. May inventory the type, amount, and location of standing timber, appraise the timber's worth, negotiate the purchase, and draw up contracts for procurement. May determine how to conserve wildlife habitats, creek beds, water quality, and soil stability, and how best to comply with environmental regulations. May devise plans for planting and growing new trees, monitor trees for healthy growth, and determine optimal harvesting schedules.

children.name: Medical Scientists
children.description: Conduct research aimed at improving overall human health. Investigate diseases or medical conditions, develop methods of prevention, and create or test medical devices or new treatments.

children.name: Epidemiologists
children.description: Investigate and describe the determinants and distribution of disease, disability, or health outcomes. May develop the means for prevention and control.

children.name: Medical Scientists, Except Epidemiologists
children.description: Conduct research dealing with the understanding of human diseases and the improvement of human health. Engage in clinical investigation, research and development, or other related activities.

children.name: Miscellaneous Life Scientists
children.description: Perform biological or life science work not classified under other roles, possibly in emerging or interdisciplinary fields such as genetics, bioinformatics, or synthetic biology.

children.name: Life Scientists, All Other
children.description: All life scientists not listed separately.

children.name: Physical Scientists
children.description: Physical Scientists are professionals who study the physical properties, composition, and behavior of matter and natural phenomena. This category includes various occupations related to physical sciences, such as physicists, astronomers, chemists, and geoscientists, among others.

children.name: Astronomers and Physicists
children.description: Investigate the fundamental principles of the universe, studying matter, energy, galaxies, and celestial phenomena. Conduct research, develop theories, and analyze observational or experimental data.

children.name: Astronomers
children.description: Observe, research, and interpret astronomical phenomena to increase basic knowledge or apply such information to practical problems.

children.name: Physicists
children.description: Conduct research into physical phenomena, develop theories on the basis of observation and experiments, and devise methods to apply physical laws and theories.

children.name: Atmospheric and Space Scientists
children.description: Examine weather, climate, and space conditions, often analyzing atmospheric data to forecast weather or understand broader climate phenomena.

children.name: Atmospheric and Space Scientists
children.description: Investigate atmospheric phenomena and interpret meteorological data, gathered by surface and air stations, satellites, and radar to prepare reports and forecasts for public and other uses. Includes weather analysts and forecasters whose functions require the detailed knowledge of meteorology.

children.name: Chemists and Materials Scientists
children.description: Research and analyze chemical compounds and materials, conducting experiments to develop new products or improve existing ones. Study properties, composition, and structure of substances.

children.name: Chemists
children.description: Conduct qualitative and quantitative chemical analyses or experiments in laboratories for quality or process control or to develop new products or knowledge.

children.name: Materials Scientists
children.description: Research and study the structures and chemical properties of various natural and synthetic or composite materials, including metals, alloys, rubber, ceramics, semiconductors, polymers, and glass. Determine ways to strengthen or combine materials or develop new materials with new or specific properties for use in a variety of products and applications. Includes glass scientists, ceramic scientists, metallurgical scientists, and polymer scientists.

children.name: Environmental Scientists and Geoscientists
children.description: Investigate environmental issues and Earth processes, including pollution, resource management, and geological phenomena. Assess and mitigate environmental hazards and advise on environmental policies.

children.name: Environmental Scientists and Specialists, Including Health
children.description: Conduct research or perform investigation for the purpose of identifying, abating, or eliminating sources of pollutants or hazards that affect either the environment or public health. Using knowledge of various scientific disciplines, may collect, synthesize, study, report, and recommend action based on data derived from measurements or observations of air, food, soil, water, and other sources.

children.name: Climate Change Policy Analysts
children.description: Research and analyze policy developments related to climate change. Make climate-related recommendations for actions such as legislation, awareness campaigns, or fundraising approaches.

children.name: Environmental Restoration Planners
children.description: Collaborate with field and biology staff to oversee the implementation of restoration projects and to develop new products. Process and synthesize complex scientific data into practical strategies for restoration, monitoring or management.

children.name: Industrial Ecologists
children.description: Apply principles and processes of natural ecosystems to develop models for efficient industrial systems. Use knowledge from the physical and social sciences to maximize effective use of natural resources in the production and use of goods and services. Examine societal issues and their relationship with both technical systems and the environment.

children.name: Geoscientists, Except Hydrologists and Geographers
children.description: Study the composition, structure, and other physical aspects of the Earth. May use geological, physics, and mathematics knowledge in exploration for oil, gas, minerals, or underground water; or in waste disposal, land reclamation, or other environmental problems. May study the Earth's internal composition, atmospheres, and oceans, and its magnetic, electrical, and gravitational forces. Includes mineralogists, paleontologists, stratigraphers, geodesists, and seismologists.

children.name: Hydrologists
children.description: Research the distribution, circulation, and physical properties of underground and surface waters; and study the form and intensity of precipitation and its rate of infiltration into the soil, movement through the earth, and return to the ocean and atmosphere.

children.name: Miscellaneous Physical Scientists
children.description: Occupations encompassing physical science roles not distinctly covered by standard categories, often involving specialized or emerging fields like remote sensing, polymer science, or science policy.

children.name: Physical Scientists, All Other
children.description: All physical scientists not listed separately.

children.name: Remote Sensing Scientists and Technologists
children.description: Apply remote sensing principles and methods to analyze data and solve problems in areas such as natural resource management, urban planning, or homeland security. May develop new sensor systems, analytical techniques, or new applications for existing systems.

children.name: Social Scientists and Related Workers
children.description: Social Scientists and Related Workers study various aspects of human society, behavior, and interactions. They conduct research, collect and analyze data, and interpret social patterns and trends. This category includes occupations such as sociologists, anthropologists, political scientists, economists, and market research analysts.

children.name: Economists
children.description: Study the production and distribution of resources, goods, and services. Collect and analyze economic data, interpret trends, and forecast future market behaviors.

children.name: Economists
children.description: Conduct research, prepare reports, or formulate plans to address economic problems related to the production and distribution of goods and services or monetary and fiscal policy. May collect and process economic and statistical data using sampling techniques and econometric methods.

children.name: Environmental Economists
children.description: Conduct economic analysis related to environmental protection and use of the natural environment, such as water, air, land, and renewable energy resources. Evaluate and quantify benefits, costs, incentives, and impacts of alternative options using economic principles and statistical techniques.

children.name: Survey Researchers
children.description: Develop and administer surveys, collect data, analyze results, and provide findings to inform decisions in business, government, or social sciences.

children.name: Survey Researchers
children.description: Plan, develop, or conduct surveys. May analyze and interpret the meaning of survey data, determine survey objectives, or suggest or test question wording. Includes social scientists who primarily design questionnaires or supervise survey teams.

children.name: Psychologists
children.description: Study mental processes and behavior. May provide therapy, conduct research, or apply psychological principles to organizational, educational, or clinical settings.

children.name: Clinical, Counseling, and School Psychologists
children.description: Diagnose and treat mental disorders; learning disabilities; and cognitive, behavioral, and emotional problems, using individual, child, family, and group therapies. May design and implement behavior modification programs.

children.name: School Psychologists
children.description: Investigate processes of learning and teaching and develop psychological principles and techniques applicable to educational problems.

children.name: Clinical Psychologists
children.description: Diagnose or evaluate mental and emotional disorders of individuals through observation, interview, and psychological tests, and formulate and administer programs of treatment.

children.name: Counseling Psychologists
children.description: Assess and evaluate individuals' problems through the use of case history, interview, and observation and provide individual or group counseling services to assist individuals in achieving more effective personal, social, educational, and vocational development and adjustment.

children.name: Industrial-Organizational Psychologists
children.description: Apply principles of psychology to human resources, administration, management, sales, and marketing problems. Activities may include policy planning; employee testing and selection, training, and development; and organizational development and analysis. May work with management to organize the work setting to improve worker productivity.

children.name: Clinical and Counseling Psychologists
children.description: Assess, diagnose, and treat mental and emotional disorders of individuals through observation, interview, and psychological tests. Help individuals with distress or maladjustment understand their problems through their knowledge of case history, interviews with patients, and theory. Provide individual or group counseling services to assist individuals in achieving more effective personal, social, educational, and vocational development and adjustment. May design behavior modification programs and consult with medical personnel regarding the best treatment for patients.

children.name: School Psychologists
children.description: Diagnose and implement individual or schoolwide interventions or strategies to address educational, behavioral, or developmental issues that adversely impact educational functioning in a school. May address student learning and behavioral problems and counsel students or families. May design and implement performance plans, and evaluate performance. May consult with other school-based personnel.

children.name: Psychologists, All Other
children.description: All psychologists not listed separately.

children.name: Neuropsychologists and Clinical Neuropsychologists
children.description: Apply theories and principles of neuropsychology to diagnose and treat disorders of higher cerebral functioning.

children.name: Neuropsychologists
children.description: Apply theories and principles of neuropsychology to evaluate and diagnose disorders of higher cerebral functioning, often in research and medical settings. Study the human brain and the effect of physiological states on human cognition and behavior. May formulate and administer programs of treatment.

children.name: Clinical Neuropsychologists
children.description: Assess and diagnose patients with neurobehavioral problems related to acquired or developmental disorders of the nervous system, such as neurodegenerative disorders, traumatic brain injury, seizure disorders, and learning disabilities. Recommend treatment after diagnosis, such as therapy, medication, or surgery. Assist with evaluation before and after neurosurgical procedures, such as deep brain stimulation.

children.name: Sociologists
children.description: Examine human society, social behavior, and cultural institutions by analyzing groups, social organizations, and structures.

children.name: Sociologists
children.description: Study human society and social behavior by examining the groups and social institutions that people form, as well as various social, religious, political, and business organizations. May study the behavior and interaction of groups, trace their origin and growth, and analyze the influence of group activities on individual members.

children.name: Urban and Regional Planners
children.description: Develop plans and programs for land use and facilities in towns, cities, or regions. Evaluate community needs, forecast population changes, and propose solutions to urban challenges.

children.name: Urban and Regional Planners
children.description: Develop comprehensive plans and programs for use of land and physical facilities of jurisdictions, such as towns, cities, counties, and metropolitan areas.

children.name: Miscellaneous Social Scientists and Related Workers
children.description: Engage in social science research or applications not covered by specific disciplines, often adopting multidisciplinary methods to address social or cultural issues.

children.name: Anthropologists and Archeologists
children.description: Study the origin, development, and behavior of human beings. May study the way of life, language, or physical characteristics of people in various parts of the world. May engage in systematic recovery and examination of material evidence, such as tools or pottery remaining from past human cultures, in order to determine the history, customs, and living habits of earlier civilizations.

children.name: Anthropologists
children.description: Research, evaluate, and establish public policy concerning the origins of humans; their physical, social, linguistic, and cultural development; and their behavior, as well as the cultures, organizations, and institutions they have created.

children.name: Archeologists
children.description: Conduct research to reconstruct record of past human life and culture from human remains, artifacts, architectural features, and structures recovered through excavation, underwater recovery, or other means of discovery.

children.name: Geographers
children.description: Study the nature and use of areas of the Earth's surface, relating and interpreting interactions of physical and cultural phenomena. Conduct research on physical aspects of a region, including land forms, climates, soils, plants, and animals, and conduct research on the spatial implications of human activities within a given area, including social characteristics, economic activities, and political organization, as well as researching interdependence between regions at scales ranging from local to global.

children.name: Historians
children.description: Research, analyze, record, and interpret the past as recorded in sources, such as government and institutional records, newspapers and other periodicals, photographs, interviews, films, electronic media, and unpublished manuscripts, such as personal diaries and letters.

children.name: Political Scientists
children.description: Study the origin, development, and operation of political systems. May study topics, such as public opinion, political decisionmaking, and ideology. May analyze the structure and operation of governments, as well as various political entities. May conduct public opinion surveys, analyze election results, or analyze public documents.

children.name: Social Scientists and Related Workers, All Other
children.description: All social scientists and related workers not listed separately.

children.name: Transportation Planners
children.description: Prepare studies for proposed transportation projects. Gather, compile, and analyze data. Study the use and operation of transportation systems. Develop transportation models or simulations.

children.name: Life, Physical, and Social Science Technicians
children.description: Life, Physical, and Social Science Technicians provide support to scientists and researchers in various scientific disciplines. They assist with laboratory work, data collection, experimentation, and analysis. This category includes occupations such as biological technicians, chemical technicians, geological and petroleum technicians, and social science research assistants.

children.name: Agricultural and Food Science Technicians
children.description: Assist scientists in research or production, conducting tests on food, soil, and other samples. Maintain laboratory equipment and collect data to help improve agricultural methods and food processing.

children.name: Agricultural and Food Science Technicians
children.description: Assist scientists or engineers in the use of electronic, sonic, or nuclear measuring instruments in both laboratory and production activities to obtain data indicating potential resources such as metallic ore, minerals, gas, coal, or petroleum. Analyze mud and drill cuttings. Chart pressure, temperature, and other characteristics of wells or bore holes. Investigate and collect information leading to the possible discovery of new metallic ore, minerals, gas, coal, or petroleum deposits.

children.name: Agricultural Technicians
children.description: Set up or maintain laboratory equipment and collect samples from crops or animals. Prepare specimens or record data to assist scientists in biology or related life science experiments.

children.name: Food Science Technicians
children.description: Perform standardized qualitative and quantitative tests to determine physical or chemical properties of food or beverage products.

children.name: Agricultural Technicians
children.description: Work with agricultural scientists in plant, fiber, and animal research, or assist with animal breeding and nutrition. Set up or maintain laboratory equipment and collect samples from crops or animals. Prepare specimens or record data to assist scientists in biology or related life science experiments. Conduct tests and experiments to improve yield and quality of crops or to increase the resistance of plants and animals to disease or insects.

children.name: Precision Agriculture Technicians
children.description: Apply geospatial technologies, including geographic information systems (GIS) and Global Positioning System (GPS), to agricultural production or management activities, such as pest scouting, site-specific pesticide application, yield mapping, or variable-rate irrigation. May use computers to develop or analyze maps or remote sensing images to compare physical topography with data on soils, fertilizer, pests, or weather.

children.name: Food Science Technicians
children.description: Work with food scientists or technologists to perform standardized qualitative and quantitative tests to determine physical or chemical properties of food or beverage products. Includes technicians who assist in research and development of production technology, quality control, packaging, processing, and use of foods.

children.name: Geophysical Data Technicians
children.description: Measure, record, or evaluate geological data, using sonic, electronic, electrical, seismic, or gravity-measuring instruments to prospect for oil or gas. May collect or evaluate core samples or cuttings.

children.name: Biological Technicians
children.description: Support biological or medical scientists by setting up, operating, and maintaining laboratory instruments and equipment, monitoring experiments, and recording results.

children.name: Biological Technicians
children.description: Assist biological and medical scientists. Set up, operate, and maintain laboratory instruments and equipment, monitor experiments, collect data and samples, make observations, and calculate and record results. May analyze organic substances, such as blood, food, and drugs.

children.name: Chemical Technicians
children.description: Conduct chemical and physical laboratory tests to assist scientists in the qualitative and quantitative analyses of substances for research and development.

children.name: Chemical Technicians
children.description: Conduct chemical and physical laboratory tests to assist scientists in making qualitative and quantitative analyses of solids, liquids, and gaseous materials for research and development of new products or processes, quality control, maintenance of environmental standards, and other work involving experimental, theoretical, or practical application of chemistry and related sciences.

children.name: Geological and Petroleum Technicians
children.description: Collect and analyze geologic samples, test well fluids, or assist in surveying and drilling operations. Help geologists and petroleum engineers explore and extract natural resources.

children.name: Geological and Petroleum Technicians
children.description: Assist scientists or engineers in the use of electronic, sonic, or nuclear measuring instruments in both laboratory and production activities to obtain data indicating potential resources such as metallic ore, minerals, gas, coal, or petroleum. Analyze mud and drill cuttings. Chart pressure, temperature, and other characteristics of wells or bore holes. Investigate and collect information leading to the possible discovery of new metallic ore, minerals, gas, coal, or petroleum deposits.

children.name: Geological Sample Test Technicians
children.description: Test or analyze geological samples, crude oil, or minerals to detect presence of petroleum, gas, or mineral deposits indicating potential for exploration or production or to determine physical or chemical properties to ensure that products meet quality standards.

children.name: Environmental Science and Protection Technicians, Including Health
children.description: Perform laboratory and field tests to monitor the environment and investigate sources of pollution, including those that affect health, under the direction of an environmental scientist, engineer, or other specialist. May collect samples of gases, soil, water, and other materials for testing.

children.name: Geological Technicians, Except Hydrologic Technicians
children.description: Assist scientists or engineers in the use of electronic, sonic, or nuclear measuring instruments in laboratory, exploration, and production activities to obtain data indicating resources such as metallic ore, minerals, gas, coal, or petroleum. Analyze mud and drill cuttings. Chart pressure, temperature, and other characteristics of wells or bore holes.

children.name: Hydrologic Technicians
children.description: Collect and organize data concerning the distribution and circulation of ground and surface water, and data on its physical, chemical, and biological properties. Measure and report on flow rates and ground water levels, maintain field equipment, collect water samples, install and collect sampling equipment, and process samples for shipment to testing laboratories. May collect data on behalf of hydrologists, engineers, developers, government agencies, or agriculture.

children.name: Nuclear Technicians
children.description: Operate and maintain equipment used in nuclear research and energy production. Monitor radiation levels, assist with radioactive material handling, and enforce safety protocols.

children.name: Nuclear Technicians
children.description: Assist nuclear physicists, nuclear engineers, or other scientists in laboratory, power generation, or electricity production activities. May operate, maintain, or provide quality control for nuclear testing and research equipment. May monitor radiation.

children.name: Nuclear Equipment Operation Technicians
children.description: Operate equipment used for the release, control, or utilization of nuclear energy to assist scientists in laboratory or production activities.

children.name: Nuclear Monitoring Technicians
children.description: Collect and test samples to monitor results of nuclear experiments and contamination of humans, facilities, and environment.

children.name: Social Science Research Assistants
children.description: Help social scientists in laboratory, survey, or other research. Prepare findings for publication, conduct literature reviews, and assist with data collection and analysis.

children.name: Social Science Research Assistants
children.description: Assist social scientists in laboratory, survey, and other social science research. May help prepare findings for publication and assist in laboratory analysis, quality control, or data management.

children.name: City and Regional Planning Aides
children.description: Compile data from various sources, such as maps, reports, and field and file investigations, for use by city planner in making planning studies.

children.name: Forest and Conservation Technicians
children.description: Forest and Conservation Technicians aid in forest management, conservation, and research. They often work for government agencies or consulting firms, needing a degree in related fields.

children.name: Forest and Conservation Technicians
children.description: Provide technical assistance regarding the conservation of soil, water, forests, or related natural resources. May compile data pertaining to size, content, condition, and other characteristics of forest tracts under the direction of foresters, or train and lead forest workers in forest propagation and fire prevention and suppression. May assist conservation scientists in managing, improving, and protecting rangelands and wildlife habitats.

children.name: Miscellaneous Life, Physical, and Social Science Technicians
children.description: Perform technical tasks to support scientific research or operations not covered by specialized technician roles, often requiring cross-disciplinary skills.

children.name: Environmental Science and Protection Technicians, Including Health
children.description: Perform laboratory and field tests to monitor the environment and investigate sources of pollution, including those that affect health, under the direction of an environmental scientist, engineer, or other specialist. May collect samples of gases, soil, water, and other materials for testing.

children.name: Forensic Science Technicians
children.description: Collect, identify, classify, and analyze physical evidence related to criminal investigations. Perform tests on weapons or substances, such as fiber, hair, and tissue to determine significance to investigation. May testify as expert witnesses on evidence or crime laboratory techniques. May serve as specialists in area of expertise, such as ballistics, fingerprinting, handwriting, or biochemistry.

children.name: Forest and Conservation Technicians
children.description: Provide technical assistance regarding the conservation of soil, water, forests, or related natural resources. May compile data pertaining to size, content, condition, and other characteristics of forest tracts, under the direction of foresters; or train and lead forest workers in forest propagation, fire prevention and suppression. May assist conservation scientists in managing, improving, and protecting rangelands and wildlife habitats.

children.name: Life, Physical, and Social Science Technicians, All Other
children.description: All life, physical, and social science technicians not listed separately.

children.name: Quality Control Analysts
children.description: Conduct tests to determine quality of raw materials, bulk intermediate and finished products. May conduct stability sample tests.

children.name: Precision Agriculture Technicians
children.description: Apply geospatial technologies, including geographic information systems (GIS) and Global Positioning System (GPS), to agricultural production or management activities, such as pest scouting, site-specific pesticide application, yield mapping, or variable-rate irrigation. May use computers to develop or analyze maps or remote sensing images to compare physical topography with data on soils, fertilizer, pests, or weather.

children.name: Remote Sensing Technicians
children.description: Apply remote sensing technologies to assist scientists in areas such as natural resources, urban planning, or homeland security. May prepare flight plans or sensor configurations for flight trips.

children.name: Occupational Health and Safety Specialists and Technicians
children.description: The SOC 19-5010 series is all about championing workplace safety by blending high-level strategy with hands-on vigilance. It covers Occupational Health and Safety Specialists, who design and manage safety programs, ensure regulatory compliance, and educate teams, with Occupational Health and Safety Technicians, who hit the field to monitor hazards, collect critical safety data, and implement the specialists' plans. Together, they form a dynamic duo dedicated to creating secure, healthy work environments—a true safety squad ready to tackle challenges with precision and care, ensuring everyone goes home with a smile (and intact!).

children.name: Occupational Health and Safety Specialists
children.description: Review, evaluate, and analyze work environments and design programs and procedures to control, eliminate, and prevent disease or injury caused by chemical, physical, and biological agents or ergonomic factors. May conduct inspections and enforce adherence to laws and regulations governing the health and safety of individuals. May be employed in the public or private sector.

children.name: Occupational Health and Safety Technicians
children.description: Collect data on work environments for analysis by occupational health and safety specialists. Implement and conduct evaluation of programs designed to limit chemical, physical, biological, and ergonomic risks to workers.

name: Community and Social Service Occupations
description: Focuses on helping people address personal and social problems. Roles include social workers, counselors, and others who provide support services, advocacy, and resources in community centers, clinics, or other settings.

children.name: Counselors, Social Workers, and Other Community and Social Service Specialists
children.description: This category includes various occupations that provide support and services to individuals and communities. It encompasses occupations such as substance abuse and behavioral disorder counselors, mental health counselors, school and career counselors, social workers, and community health workers. These professionals work with diverse populations and address a range of social and behavioral issues.

children.name: Counselors
children.description: Provide guidance, therapeutic support, and advice to individuals or groups facing personal, mental, or educational challenges. May design treatment plans, collaborate with other professionals, and track client progress.

children.name: Substance Abuse and Behavioral Disorder Counselors
children.description: Counsel and advise individuals with alcohol, tobacco, drug, or other problems, such as gambling and eating disorders. May counsel individuals, families, or groups or engage in prevention programs.

children.name: Educational, Guidance, and Career Counselors and Advisors
children.description: Advise and assist students and provide educational and vocational guidance services.

children.name: Marriage and Family Therapists
children.description: Diagnose and treat mental and emotional disorders, whether cognitive, affective, or behavioral, within the context of marriage and family systems. Apply psychotherapeutic and family systems theories and techniques in the delivery of services to individuals, couples, and families for the purpose of treating such diagnosed nervous and mental disorders.

children.name: Mental Health Counselors
children.description: Counsel and advise individuals and groups to promote optimum mental and emotional health, with an emphasis on prevention. May help individuals deal with a broad range of mental health issues, such as those associated with addictions and substance abuse; family, parenting, and marital problems; stress management; self-esteem; or aging.

children.name: Rehabilitation Counselors
children.description: Counsel individuals to maximize the independence and employability of persons coping with personal, social, and vocational difficulties that result from birth defects, illness, disease, accidents, aging, or the stress of daily life. Coordinate activities for residents of care and treatment facilities. Assess client needs and design and implement rehabilitation programs that may include personal and vocational counseling, training, and job placement.

children.name: Counselors, All Other
children.description: All counselors not listed separately.

children.name: Social Workers
children.description: Help individuals and families cope with challenges in their lives. Assess client needs, provide advocacy and counseling, connect clients with resources, and monitor progress.

children.name: Child, Family, and School Social Workers
children.description: Provide social services and assistance to improve the social and psychological functioning of children and their families and to maximize the family well-being and the academic functioning of children. May assist parents, arrange adoptions, and find foster homes for abandoned or abused children. In schools, they address such problems as teenage pregnancy, misbehavior, and truancy. May also advise teachers.

children.name: Healthcare Social Workers
children.description: Provide individuals, families, and groups with the psychosocial support needed to cope with chronic, acute, or terminal illnesses. Services include advising family caregivers. Provide patients with information and counseling, and make referrals for other services. May also provide case and care management or interventions designed to promote health, prevent disease, and address barriers to access to healthcare.

children.name: Mental Health and Substance Abuse Social Workers
children.description: Assess and treat individuals with mental, emotional, or substance abuse problems, including abuse of alcohol, tobacco, and/or other drugs. Activities may include individual and group therapy, crisis intervention, case management, client advocacy, prevention, and education.

children.name: Social Workers, All Other
children.description: All social workers not listed separately.

children.name: Miscellaneous Community and Social Service Specialists
children.description: Deliver social services in specialized areas not covered by other occupations, possibly focusing on community outreach, crisis intervention, or specific at-risk populations.

children.name: Health Education Specialists
children.description: Provide and manage health education programs that help individuals, families, and their communities maximize and maintain healthy lifestyles. Use data to identify community needs prior to planning, implementing, monitoring, and evaluating programs designed to encourage healthy lifestyles, policies, and environments. May link health systems, health providers, insurers, and patients to address individual and population health needs. May serve as resource to assist individuals, other health professionals, or the community, and may administer fiscal resources for health education programs.

children.name: Probation Officers and Correctional Treatment Specialists
children.description: Provide social services to assist in rehabilitation of law offenders in custody or on probation or parole. Make recommendations for actions involving formulation of rehabilitation plan and treatment of offender, including conditional release and education and employment stipulations.

children.name: Social and Human Service Assistants
children.description: Assist other social and human service providers in providing client services in a wide variety of fields, such as psychology, rehabilitation, or social work, including support for families. May assist clients in identifying and obtaining available benefits and social and community services. May assist social workers with developing, organizing, and conducting programs to prevent and resolve problems relevant to substance abuse, human relationships, rehabilitation, or dependent care.

children.name: Community Health Workers
children.description: Promote health within a community by assisting individuals to adopt healthy behaviors. Serve as an advocate for the health needs of individuals by assisting community residents in effectively communicating with healthcare providers or social service agencies. Act as liaison or advocate and implement programs that promote, maintain, and improve individual and overall community health. May deliver health-related preventive services such as blood pressure, glaucoma, and hearing screenings. May collect data to help identify community health needs.

children.name: Community and Social Service Specialists, All Other
children.description: All community and social service specialists not listed separately.

children.name: Religious Workers
children.description: Religious Workers encompass a variety of roles within religious organizations, including clergy members, religious directors, religious educators, and religious activities coordinators. They provide spiritual guidance, lead religious services, perform religious rituals, and offer support and counseling to individuals and communities.

children.name: Clergy
children.description: Conduct religious worship, provide spiritual or moral guidance, and lead religious education programs or community services within a faith tradition.

children.name: Clergy
children.description: Conduct religious worship and perform other spiritual functions associated with beliefs and practices of religious faith or denomination. Provide spiritual and moral guidance and assistance to members.

children.name: Directors, Religious Activities and Education
children.description: Plan and coordinate religious education and social activities within a faith community. May train volunteers, lead youth groups, or organize outreach.

children.name: Directors, Religious Activities and Education
children.description: Coordinate or design programs and conduct outreach to promote the religious education or activities of a denominational group. May provide counseling, guidance, and leadership relative to marital, health, financial, and religious problems.

children.name: Miscellaneous Religious Workers
children.description: Perform faith-based or spiritual duties not encompassed by other roles, such as music ministry, spiritual counseling, or specialized pastoral services.

children.name: Religious Workers, All Other
children.description: All religious workers not listed separately.

name: Legal Occupations
description: Encompasses lawyers, judges, and related legal support roles. Individuals in these occupations interpret laws, advise clients, resolve disputes, and uphold legal standards through courts or legal institutions.

children.name: Lawyers, Judges, and Related Workers
children.description: This category includes various occupations related to the legal profession, such as lawyers, judges, magistrates, judicial law clerks, and legal researchers. Lawyers provide legal advice, represent clients in court, and handle legal matters, while judges and magistrates preside over court proceedings and make legal decisions.

children.name: Lawyers and Judicial Law Clerks
children.description: Represent clients in legal proceedings, draft legal documents, and offer legal advice. Judicial law clerks assist judges by conducting research and writing opinions.

children.name: Lawyers
children.description: Represent clients in criminal and civil litigation and other legal proceedings, draw up legal documents, or manage or advise clients on legal transactions. May specialize in a single area or may practice broadly in many areas of law.

children.name: Judicial Law Clerks
children.description: Assist judges in court or by conducting research or preparing legal documents.

children.name: Judges, Magistrates, and Other Judicial Workers
children.description: Preside over court proceedings, interpret and apply laws, make rulings, and render judgments in legal cases.

children.name: Administrative Law Judges, Adjudicators, and Hearing Officers
children.description: Conduct hearings to recommend or make decisions on claims concerning government programs or other government-related matters. Determine liability, sanctions, or penalties, or recommend the acceptance or rejection of claims or settlements.

children.name: Arbitrators, Mediators, and Conciliators
children.description: Facilitate negotiation and conflict resolution through dialogue. Resolve conflicts outside of the court system by mutual consent of parties involved.

children.name: Judges, Magistrate Judges, and Magistrates
children.description: Arbitrate, advise, adjudicate, or administer justice in a court of law. May sentence defendant in criminal cases according to government statutes or sentencing guidelines. May determine liability of defendant in civil cases. May perform wedding ceremonies.

children.name: Legal Support Workers
children.description: Legal Support Workers provide various administrative and clerical support services to legal professionals and legal organizations. This category includes occupations such as paralegals, legal secretaries, legal assistants, and court reporters. They assist in preparing legal documents, conducting research, organizing case files, and providing administrative support.

children.name: Paralegals and Legal Assistants
