children.description: Support lawyers by conducting legal research, drafting documents, organizing case files, and investigating facts for hearings, trials, and corporate meetings.

children.name: Paralegals and Legal Assistants
children.description: Assist lawyers by investigating facts, preparing legal documents, or researching legal precedent. Conduct research to support a legal proceeding, to formulate a defense, or to initiate legal action.

children.name: Miscellaneous Legal Support Workers
children.description: Carry out specialized legal support tasks not covered in other categories, such as abstracting and title searching, legal transcription, or eDiscovery management.

children.name: Court Reporters
children.description: Use verbatim methods and equipment to capture, store, retrieve, and transcribe pretrial and trial proceedings or other information. Includes stenocaptioners who operate computerized stenographic captioning equipment to provide captions of live or prerecorded broadcasts for hearing-impaired viewers.

children.name: Title Examiners, Abstractors, and Searchers
children.description: Search real estate records, examine titles, or summarize pertinent legal or insurance documents or details for a variety of purposes. May compile lists of mortgages, contracts, and other instruments pertaining to titles by searching public and private records for law firms, real estate agencies, or title insurance companies.

children.name: Legal Support Workers, All Other
children.description: All legal support workers not listed separately.

name: Education, Training, and Library Occupations
description: Comprises teachers, professors, librarians, and instructors who facilitate learning, develop curricula, manage library resources, and support academic or vocational growth in schools, colleges, or community programs.

children.name: Postsecondary Teachers
children.description: Postsecondary Teachers, also known as professors or faculty members, work in colleges, universities, and other higher education institutions. They teach academic and vocational subjects to students pursuing higher education. This category includes a wide range of disciplines, such as English literature, mathematics, biology, psychology, history, business, and many others.

children.name: Business Teachers, Postsecondary
children.description: Teach courses in business administration or management at the college or university level. May conduct scholarly research, publish findings, and advise students.

children.name: Business Teachers, Postsecondary
children.description: Teach courses in business administration and management, such as accounting, finance, human resources, labor and industrial relations, marketing, and operations research. Includes both teachers primarily engaged in teaching and those who do a combination of teaching and research.

children.name: Math and Computer Teachers, Postsecondary
children.description: Instruct students in mathematical or computer science disciplines at the postsecondary level. Prepare and deliver lectures, evaluate student work, and may conduct research.

children.name: Computer Science Teachers, Postsecondary
children.description: Teach courses in computer science. May specialize in a field of computer science, such as the design and function of computers or operations and research analysis. Includes both teachers primarily engaged in teaching and those who do a combination of teaching and research.

children.name: Mathematical Science Teachers, Postsecondary
children.description: Teach courses pertaining to mathematical concepts, statistics, and actuarial science and to the application of original and standardized mathematical techniques in solving specific problems and situations. Includes both teachers primarily engaged in teaching and those who do a combination of teaching and research.

children.name: Engineering and Architecture Teachers, Postsecondary
children.description: Teach courses in engineering and architecture at the college level. Develop curricula, advise students, and engage in research or creative work within those fields.

children.name: Architecture Teachers, Postsecondary
children.description: Teach courses in architecture and architectural design, such as architectural environmental design, interior architecture/design, and landscape architecture. Includes both teachers primarily engaged in teaching and those who do a combination of teaching and research.

children.name: Engineering Teachers, Postsecondary
children.description: Teach courses pertaining to the application of physical laws and principles of engineering for the development of machines, materials, instruments, processes, and services. Includes teachers of subjects such as chemical, civil, electrical, industrial, mechanical, mineral, and petroleum engineering. Includes both teachers primarily engaged in teaching and those who do a combination of teaching and research.

children.name: Life Sciences Teachers, Postsecondary
children.description: Educate students in biological sciences at colleges or universities. Prepare and deliver lectures, evaluate student performance, and conduct scientific research.

children.name: Agricultural Sciences Teachers, Postsecondary
children.description: Teach courses in the agricultural sciences. Includes teachers of agronomy, dairy sciences, fisheries management, horticultural sciences, poultry sciences, range management, and agricultural soil conservation. Includes both teachers primarily engaged in teaching and those who do a combination of teaching and research.

children.name: Biological Science Teachers, Postsecondary
children.description: Teach courses in biological sciences. Includes both teachers primarily engaged in teaching and those who do a combination of teaching and research.

children.name: Forestry and Conservation Science Teachers, Postsecondary
children.description: Teach courses in forestry and conservation science. Includes both teachers primarily engaged in teaching and those who do a combination of teaching and research.

children.name: Physical Sciences Teachers, Postsecondary
children.description: Teach courses in physical science subjects—such as chemistry, physics, and geology—at the postsecondary level, conduct research, and publish findings.

children.name: Atmospheric, Earth, Marine, and Space Sciences Teachers, Postsecondary
children.description: Teach courses in the physical sciences, except chemistry and physics. Includes both teachers primarily engaged in teaching, and those who do a combination of teaching and research.

children.name: Chemistry Teachers, Postsecondary
children.description: Teach courses pertaining to the chemical and physical properties and compositional changes of substances. Work may include providing instruction in the methods of qualitative and quantitative chemical analysis. Includes both teachers primarily engaged in teaching, and those who do a combination of teaching and research.

children.name: Environmental Science Teachers, Postsecondary
children.description: Teach courses in environmental science. Includes both teachers primarily engaged in teaching and those who do a combination of teaching and research.

children.name: Physics Teachers, Postsecondary
children.description: Teach courses pertaining to the laws of matter and energy. Includes both teachers primarily engaged in teaching and those who do a combination of teaching and research.

children.name: Social Sciences Teachers, Postsecondary
children.description: Teach courses in sociology, political science, or other social sciences at the college or university level. May also conduct scholarly research and publish findings.

children.name: Anthropology and Archeology Teachers, Postsecondary
children.description: Teach courses in anthropology or archeology. Includes both teachers primarily engaged in teaching and those who do a combination of teaching and research.

children.name: Area, Ethnic, and Cultural Studies Teachers, Postsecondary
children.description: Teach courses pertaining to the culture and development of an area, an ethnic group, or any other group, such as Latin American studies, women's studies, or urban affairs. Includes both teachers primarily engaged in teaching and those who do a combination of teaching and research.

children.name: Economics Teachers, Postsecondary
children.description: Teach courses in economics. Includes both teachers primarily engaged in teaching and those who do a combination of teaching and research.

children.name: Geography Teachers, Postsecondary
children.description: Teach courses in geography. Includes both teachers primarily engaged in teaching and those who do a combination of teaching and research.

children.name: Political Science Teachers, Postsecondary
children.description: Teach courses in political science, international affairs, and international relations. Includes both teachers primarily engaged in teaching and those who do a combination of teaching and research.

children.name: Psychology Teachers, Postsecondary
children.description: Teach courses in psychology, such as child, clinical, and developmental psychology, and psychological counseling. Includes both teachers primarily engaged in teaching and those who do a combination of teaching and research.

children.name: Sociology Teachers, Postsecondary
children.description: Teach courses in sociology. Includes both teachers primarily engaged in teaching and those who do a combination of teaching and research.

children.name: Social Sciences Teachers, Postsecondary, All Other
children.description: All postsecondary social sciences teachers not listed separately.

children.name: Health Teachers, Postsecondary
children.description: Educate students on health-related subjects such as public health, nutrition, or health administration at postsecondary institutions. May conduct research and advise students.

children.name: Health Specialties Teachers, Postsecondary
children.description: Teach courses in health specialties, in fields such as dentistry, laboratory technology, medicine, pharmacy, public health, therapy, and veterinary medicine.

children.name: Nursing Instructors and Teachers, Postsecondary
children.description: Demonstrate and teach patient care in classroom and clinical units to nursing students. Includes both teachers primarily engaged in teaching and those who do a combination of teaching and research.

children.name: Education and Library Science Teachers, Postsecondary
children.description: Instruct future educators and librarians in teaching methods, curriculum development, and library management. May also supervise student teachers and conduct research.

children.name: Education Teachers, Postsecondary
children.description: Teach courses pertaining to education, such as counseling, curriculum, guidance, instruction, teacher education, and teaching English as a second language. Includes both teachers primarily engaged in teaching and those who do a combination of teaching and research.

children.name: Library Science Teachers, Postsecondary
children.description: Teach courses in library science. Includes both teachers primarily engaged in teaching and those who do a combination of teaching and research.

children.name: Law, Criminal Justice, and Social Work Teachers, Postsecondary
children.description: Provide instruction in legal studies, criminal justice, or social work at the college level. Develop course materials, deliver lectures, and may conduct specialized research.

children.name: Criminal Justice and Law Enforcement Teachers, Postsecondary
children.description: Teach courses in criminal justice, corrections, and law enforcement administration. Includes both teachers primarily engaged in teaching and those who do a combination of teaching and research.

children.name: Law Teachers, Postsecondary
children.description: Teach courses in law. Includes both teachers primarily engaged in teaching and those who do a combination of teaching and research.

children.name: Social Work Teachers, Postsecondary
children.description: Teach courses in social work. Includes both teachers primarily engaged in teaching and those who do a combination of teaching and research.

children.name: Arts, Communications, and Humanities Teachers, Postsecondary
children.description: Teach courses in subjects like literature, foreign languages, communication, or visual/performing arts at the college or university level, and may be engaged in related research or creative work.

children.name: Art, Drama, and Music Teachers, Postsecondary
children.description: Teach courses in drama, music, and the arts including fine and applied art, such as painting and sculpture, or design and crafts. Includes both teachers primarily engaged in teaching and those who do a combination of teaching and research.

children.name: Communications Teachers, Postsecondary
children.description: Teach courses in communications, such as organizational communications, public relations, radio/television broadcasting, and journalism. Includes both teachers primarily engaged in teaching and those who do a combination of teaching and research.

children.name: English Language and Literature Teachers, Postsecondary
children.description: Teach courses in English language and literature, including linguistics and comparative literature. Includes both teachers primarily engaged in teaching and those who do a combination of teaching and research.

children.name: Foreign Language and Literature Teachers, Postsecondary
children.description: Teach languages and literature courses in languages other than English. Includes teachers of American Sign Language (ASL). Includes both teachers primarily engaged in teaching and those who do a combination of teaching and research.

children.name: History Teachers, Postsecondary
children.description: Teach courses in human history and historiography. Includes both teachers primarily engaged in teaching and those who do a combination of teaching and research.

children.name: Philosophy and Religion Teachers, Postsecondary
children.description: Teach courses in philosophy, religion, and theology. Includes both teachers primarily engaged in teaching and those who do a combination of teaching and research.

children.name: Miscellaneous Postsecondary Teachers
children.description: Instruct in postsecondary subjects not classified under other standard teaching categories, often involving specialized or emerging disciplines.

children.name: Graduate Teaching Assistants
children.description: Assist faculty or other instructional staff in postsecondary institutions by performing teaching or teaching-related duties, such as teaching lower level courses, developing teaching materials, preparing and giving examinations, and grading examinations or papers. Graduate teaching assistants must be enrolled in a graduate school program. Graduate assistants who primarily perform non-teaching duties, such as research, should be reported in the occupational category related to the work performed.

children.name: Family and Consumer Sciences Teachers, Postsecondary
children.description: Teach courses in childcare, family relations, finance, nutrition, and related subjects pertaining to home management. Includes both teachers primarily engaged in teaching and those who do a combination of teaching and research.

children.name: Recreation and Fitness Studies Teachers, Postsecondary
children.description: Teach courses pertaining to recreation, leisure, and fitness studies, including exercise physiology and facilities management. Includes both teachers primarily engaged in teaching and those who do a combination of teaching and research.

children.name: Career/Technical Education Teachers, Postsecondary
children.description: Teach vocational courses intended to provide occupational training below the baccalaureate level in subjects such as construction, mechanics/repair, manufacturing, transportation, or cosmetology, primarily to students who have graduated from or left high school. Teaching takes place in public or private schools whose primary business is academic or vocational education.

children.name: Postsecondary Teachers, All Other
children.description: All postsecondary teachers not listed separately.

children.name: Preschool, Primary, Secondary, and Special Education School Teachers
children.description: This category includes teachers who work in various educational settings, such as preschools, elementary schools, middle schools, high schools, and special education programs. They provide instruction, create lesson plans, assess student progress, and support the overall development and well-being of students.

children.name: Preschool and Kindergarten Teachers
children.description: Teach young children basic skills and concepts to prepare them for primary school, focusing on social, motor, language, and foundational academic development.

children.name: Preschool Teachers, Except Special Education
children.description: Instruct preschool-aged students, following curricula or lesson plans, in activities designed to promote social, physical, and intellectual growth.

children.name: Kindergarten Teachers, Except Special Education
children.description: Teach academic and social skills to kindergarten students.

children.name: Elementary and Middle School Teachers
children.description: Instruct students in multiple academic and developmental areas, typically from first through eighth grade, fostering foundational skills and knowledge.

children.name: Elementary School Teachers, Except Special Education
children.description: Teach academic and social skills to students at the elementary school level.

children.name: Middle School Teachers, Except Special and Career/Technical Education
children.description: Teach one or more subjects to students at the middle, intermediate, or junior high school level.

children.name: Career/Technical Education Teachers, Middle School
children.description: Teach occupational, vocational, career, or technical subjects to students at the middle, intermediate, or junior high school level.

children.name: Secondary School Teachers
children.description: Teach one or more subjects to high school students, preparing them for postsecondary education, careers, or vocational training.

children.name: Secondary School Teachers, Except Special and Career/Technical Education
children.description: Teach one or more subjects to students at the secondary school level.

children.name: Career/Technical Education Teachers, Secondary School
children.description: Teach occupational, vocational, career, or technical subjects to students at the secondary school level.

children.name: Special Education Teachers
children.description: Work with students who have a wide range of learning, mental, emotional, or physical disabilities. Adapt general education lessons and teach various subjects.

children.name: Special Education Teachers, Preschool
children.description: Teach academic, social, and life skills to preschool-aged students with learning, emotional, or physical disabilities. Includes teachers who specialize and work with students who are blind or have visual impairments; students who are deaf or have hearing impairments; and students with intellectual disabilities.

children.name: Special Education Teachers, Kindergarten and Elementary School
children.description: Teach elementary school subjects to educationally and physically handicapped students. Includes teachers who specialize and work with audibly and visually handicapped students and those who teach basic academic and life processes skills to the mentally impaired.

children.name: Special Education Teachers, Middle School
children.description: Teach middle school subjects to educationally and physically handicapped students. Includes teachers who specialize and work with audibly and visually handicapped students and those who teach basic academic and life processes skills to the mentally impaired.

children.name: Special Education Teachers, Secondary School
children.description: Teach secondary school subjects to educationally and physically handicapped students. Includes teachers who specialize and work with audibly and visually handicapped students and those who teach basic academic and life processes skills to the mentally impaired.

children.name: Special Education Teachers, Kindergarten
children.description: Teach academic, social, and life skills to kindergarten students with learning, emotional, or physical disabilities. Includes teachers who specialize and work with students who are blind or have visual impairments; students who are deaf or have hearing impairments; and students with intellectual disabilities.

children.name: Special Education Teachers, Elementary School
children.description: Teach academic, social, and life skills to elementary school students with learning, emotional, or physical disabilities. Includes teachers who specialize and work with students who are blind or have visual impairments; students who are deaf or have hearing impairments; and students with intellectual disabilities.

children.name: Special Education Teachers, Middle School
children.description: Teach academic, social, and life skills to middle school students with learning, emotional, or physical disabilities. Includes teachers who specialize and work with students who are blind or have visual impairments; students who are deaf or have hearing impairments; and students with intellectual disabilities.

children.name: Special Education Teachers, Secondary School
children.description: Teach academic, social, and life skills to secondary school students with learning, emotional, or physical disabilities. Includes teachers who specialize and work with students who are blind or have visual impairments; students who are deaf or have hearing impairments; and students with intellectual disabilities.

children.name: Special Education Teachers, All Other
children.description: All special education teachers not listed separately.

children.name: Adapted Physical Education Specialists
children.description: Provide individualized physical education instruction or services to children, youth, or adults with exceptional physical needs due to gross motor developmental delays or other impairments.

children.name: Other Teachers and Instructors
children.description: This category includes a diverse range of instructional roles outside of traditional preschool, primary, secondary, and postsecondary education. It encompasses occupations such as fitness trainers and instructors, vocational instructors, language instructors, music instructors, and art teachers. These professionals provide specialized instruction in various settings, including fitness centers, community centers, language schools, and private studios.

children.name: Adult Basic and Secondary Education and Literacy Teachers and Instructors
children.description: Teach adults in basic skills such as reading, writing, math, or English as a Second Language (ESL). May also prepare learners for GED exams or workforce readiness.

children.name: Adult Basic Education, Adult Secondary Education, and English as a Second Language Instructors
children.description: Teach or instruct out-of-school youths and adults in basic education, literacy, or English as a Second Language classes, or in classes for earning a high school equivalency credential.

children.name: Self-Enrichment Education Teachers
children.description: Offer instruction in non-academic, leisure, or self-improvement subjects such as arts, crafts, music, language, or personal development.

children.name: Self-Enrichment Teachers
children.description: Teach or instruct individuals or groups for the primary purpose of self-enrichment or recreation, rather than for an occupational objective, educational attainment, competition, or fitness.

children.name: Part-time Teachers and Instructors, All Other
children.description: The 25-3030.00 series is essentially the umbrella for teaching roles that don’t neatly fit into the more traditional, permanent classroom positions. In this case, it specifically covers substitute teachers—those nimble educators who jump in on short notice to keep the learning train chugging along when regular teachers are absent. These professionals typically follow the established lesson plans to maintain continuity for students, ensuring that the educational process doesn’t miss a beat. So, in a nutshell, the 25-3030.00 series is all about keeping classrooms in session with the dynamic, adaptable talent of short-term substitute teachers!

children.name: Substitute Teachers, Short-Term
children.description: Teach students on a short-term basis as a temporary replacement for a regular classroom teacher, typically using the regular teacher's lesson plan.

children.name: Teacher Assistants
children.description: Teacher Assistants, often known as paraprofessionals. These essential classroom allies support teachers by helping with instructional tasks, managing classroom activities, and offering individualized attention to students who might need a little extra help. Whether it's preparing learning materials, supervising small groups, or assisting in special education settings, teacher assistants play a key role in creating a nurturing and effective learning environment. If you enjoy working closely with students, thrive in a collaborative setting, and have a passion for making education accessible and engaging, this might be the perfect role for you—think of it as being the secret ingredient in the recipe for classroom success!

children.name: Tutors
children.description: Instruct individual students or small groups of students in academic subjects to support formal class instruction or to prepare students for standardized or admissions tests.

children.name: Miscellaneous Teachers and Instructors
children.description: Teach or instruct in specialized subjects not outlined under standard categories, potentially including private tutoring or specialty workshops.

children.name: Teachers and Instructors, All Other
children.description: All teachers and instructors not listed separately.

children.name: Tutors
children.description: Provide non-classroom, academic instruction to students on an individual or small-group basis for proactive or remedial purposes.

children.name: Librarians, Curators, and Archivists
children.description: This category includes professionals who work in libraries, museums, archives, and similar institutions. Librarians manage library collections, assist patrons in accessing information, and provide research support. Curators oversee collections in museums and galleries, organize exhibitions, and conduct research. Archivists preserve and maintain records and historical documents.

children.name: Archivists, Curators, and Museum Technicians
children.description: Appraise, preserve, and catalog historical documents, artwork, and museum collections. Organize exhibitions, conduct research, and maintain public or academic archives.

children.name: Archivists
children.description: Appraise, edit, and direct safekeeping of permanent records and historically valuable documents. Participate in research activities based on archival materials.

children.name: Curators
children.description: Administer collections, such as artwork, collectibles, historic items, or scientific specimens of museums or other institutions. May conduct instructional, research, or public service activities of institution.

children.name: Museum Technicians and Conservators
children.description: Restore, maintain, or prepare objects in museum collections for storage, research, or exhibit. May work with specimens such as fossils, skeletal parts, or botanicals; or artifacts, textiles, or art. May identify and record objects or install and arrange them in exhibits. Includes book or document conservators.

children.name: Librarians
children.description: Manage library services, organize collections of books and digital media, assist patrons with research, and develop programs to encourage literacy and learning.

children.name: Librarians
children.description: Administer libraries and perform related library services. Work in a variety of settings, including public libraries, educational institutions, museums, corporations, government agencies, law firms, non-profit organizations, and healthcare providers. Tasks may include selecting, acquiring, cataloguing, classifying, circulating, and maintaining library materials; and furnishing reference, bibliographical, and readers' advisory services. May perform in-depth, strategic research, and synthesize, analyze, edit, and filter information. May set up or work with databases and information systems to catalogue and access information.

children.name: Librarians and Media Collections Specialists
children.description: Administer and maintain libraries or collections of information, for public or private access through reference or borrowing. Work in a variety of settings, such as educational institutions, museums, and corporations, and with various types of informational materials, such as books, periodicals, recordings, films, and databases. Tasks may include acquiring, cataloging, and circulating library materials, and user services such as locating and organizing information, providing instruction on how to access information, and setting up and operating a library's media equipment.

children.name: Library Technicians
children.description: Support librarians by organizing materials, assisting with circulation, maintaining records, and helping users locate information.

children.name: Library Technicians
children.description: Assist librarians by helping readers in the use of library catalogs, databases, and indexes to locate books and other materials; and by answering questions that require only brief consultation of standard reference. Compile records; sort and shelve books or other media; remove or repair damaged books or other media; register patrons; and check materials in and out of the circulation process. Replace materials in shelving area (stacks) or files. Includes bookmobile drivers who assist with providing services in mobile libraries.

children.name: Other Education, Training, and Library Occupations
children.description: This category includes a diverse range of occupations related to education, training, and library services that do not fall into the specific subcategories. It encompasses various roles such as instructional coordinators, teacher assistants, educational support professionals, library technicians, and educational counselors. These professionals provide support, assistance, and services in educational and library settings.

children.name: Audio-Visual and Multimedia Collections Specialists
children.description: Manage and operate multimedia collections and equipment. Select, install, and maintain audio-visual resources for libraries, schools, and other institutions.

children.name: Audio-Visual and Multimedia Collections Specialists
children.description: Prepare, plan, and operate multimedia teaching aids for use in education. May record, catalogue, and file materials.

children.name: Farm and Home Management Advisors
children.description: Advise and educate individuals or families on agriculture, horticulture, nutrition, and home management techniques to improve efficiency, health, and sustainability.

children.name: Farm and Home Management Educators
children.description: Instruct and advise individuals and families engaged in agriculture, agricultural-related processes, or home management activities. Demonstrate procedures and apply research findings to advance agricultural and home management activities. May develop educational outreach programs. May instruct on either agricultural issues such as agricultural processes and techniques, pest management, and food safety, or on home management issues such as budgeting, nutrition, and child development.

children.name: Instructional Coordinators
children.description: Develop educational materials, coordinate curriculum standards, and provide training for teachers. Assess program effectiveness to enhance learning outcomes.

children.name: Instructional Coordinators
children.description: Develop instructional material, coordinate educational content, and incorporate current technology into instruction in order to provide guidelines to educators and instructors for developing curricula and conducting courses. May train and coach teachers. Includes educational consultants and specialists, and instructional material directors.

children.name: Instructional Designers and Technologists
children.description: Develop instructional materials and products and assist in the technology-based redesign of courses. Assist faculty in learning about, becoming proficient in, and applying instructional technology.

children.name: Teacher Assistants
children.description: Assist classroom teachers by providing additional support to students, preparing materials, and supervising classroom activities.

children.name: Teacher Assistants
children.description: Perform duties that are instructional in nature or deliver direct services to students or parents. Serve in a position for which a teacher has ultimate responsibility for the design and implementation of educational programs and services.

children.name: Miscellaneous Education, Training, and Library Workers
children.description: Perform various educational or library-related roles not classified under other standard occupations, possibly involving specialized instructional support or resource management.

children.name: Educational Instruction and Library Workers, All Other
children.description: All educational instruction and library workers not listed separately.

name: Arts, Design, Entertainment, Sports, and Media Occupations
description: Covers creative and performance-based professions, including artists, designers, athletes, performers, writers, and media professionals responsible for cultural, artistic, and informational content.

children.name: Art and Design Workers
children.description: This category includes a diverse range of occupations related to art, design, and creative industries. It encompasses roles such as graphic designers, multimedia artists and animators, fine artists, craft artists, and fashion designers. These professionals work in various industries, including advertising, media, entertainment, fashion, and visual arts.

children.name: Artists and Related Workers
children.description: Create art to communicate ideas, thoughts, or feelings. May specialize in fine art, multimedia, or other creative mediums.

children.name: Art Directors
children.description: Formulate design concepts and presentation approaches for visual productions and media, such as print, broadcasting, video, and film. Direct workers engaged in artwork or layout design.

children.name: Craft Artists
children.description: Create or reproduce handmade objects for sale and exhibition using a variety of techniques, such as welding, weaving, pottery, and needlecraft.

children.name: Fine Artists, Including Painters, Sculptors, and Illustrators
children.description: Create original artwork using any of a wide variety of media and techniques.

children.name: Special Effects Artists and Animators
children.description: Create special effects or animations using film, video, computers, or other electronic tools and media for use in products, such as computer games, movies, music videos, and commercials.

children.name: Artists and Related Workers, All Other
children.description: All artists and related workers not listed separately.

children.name: Designers
children.description: Develop visual concepts and designs in fields such as fashion, graphics, interiors, or industrial products to meet client or organizational needs.

children.name: Commercial and Industrial Designers
children.description: Design and develop manufactured products, such as cars, home appliances, and children's toys. Combine artistic talent with research on product use, marketing, and materials to create the most functional and appealing product design.

children.name: Fashion Designers
children.description: Design clothing and accessories. Create original designs or adapt fashion trends.

children.name: Floral Designers
children.description: Design, cut, and arrange live, dried, or artificial flowers and foliage.

children.name: Graphic Designers
children.description: Design or create graphics to meet specific commercial or promotional needs, such as packaging, displays, or logos. May use a variety of mediums to achieve artistic or decorative effects.

children.name: Interior Designers
children.description: Plan, design, and furnish the internal space of rooms or buildings. Design interior environments or create physical layouts that are practical, aesthetic, and conducive to the intended purposes. May specialize in a particular field, style, or phase of interior design.

children.name: Merchandise Displayers and Window Trimmers
children.description: Plan and erect commercial displays, such as those in windows and interiors of retail stores and at trade exhibitions.

children.name: Set and Exhibit Designers
children.description: Design special exhibits and sets for film, video, television, and theater productions. May study scripts, confer with directors, and conduct research to determine appropriate architectural styles.

children.name: Designers, All Other
children.description: All designers not listed separately.

children.name: Entertainers and Performers, Sports and Related Workers
children.description: This category includes professionals involved in various forms of entertainment, performing arts, sports, and related fields. It encompasses occupations such as actors, dancers, musicians, athletes, coaches, and referees. These professionals work in industries such as theater, film and television, music, dance, sports, and recreation.

children.name: Actors, Producers, and Directors
children.description: Portray roles in productions, oversee performance projects, or direct the creative, technical, and administrative aspects of film, theater, TV, or other media.

children.name: Actors
children.description: Play parts in stage, television, radio, video, or film productions, or other settings for entertainment, information, or instruction. Interpret serious or comic role by speech, gesture, and body movement to entertain or inform audience. May dance and sing.

children.name: Producers and Directors
children.description: Produce or direct stage, television, radio, video, or film productions for entertainment, information, or instruction. Responsible for creative decisions, such as interpretation of script, choice of actors or guests, set design, sound, special effects, and choreography.

children.name: Producers
children.description: Plan and coordinate various aspects of radio, television, stage, or motion picture production, such as selecting script, coordinating writing, directing and editing, and arranging financing.

children.name: Directors- Stage, Motion Pictures, Television, and Radio
children.description: Interpret script, conduct rehearsals, and direct activities of cast and technical crew for stage, motion pictures, television, or radio programs.

children.name: Media Programming Directors
children.description: Direct and coordinate activities of personnel engaged in preparation of radio or television station program schedules and programs, such as sports or news.

children.name: Talent Directors
children.description: Audition and interview performers to select most appropriate talent for parts in stage, television, radio, or motion picture productions.

children.name: Media Technical Directors/Managers
children.description: Coordinate activities of technical departments, such as taping, editing, engineering, and maintenance, to produce radio or television programs.

children.name: Athletes, Coaches, Umpires, and Related Workers
children.description: Compete in athletic events, coach teams, or officiate sports. Train and condition athletes, analyze performance, and enforce rules during competitions.

children.name: Athletes and Sports Competitors
children.description: Compete in athletic events.

children.name: Coaches and Scouts
children.description: Instruct or coach groups or individuals in the fundamentals of sports for the primary purpose of competition. Demonstrate techniques and methods of participation. May evaluate athletes' strengths and weaknesses as possible recruits or to improve the athletes' technique to prepare them for competition. Those required to hold teaching certifications should be reported in the appropriate teaching category.

children.name: Umpires, Referees, and Other Sports Officials
children.description: Officiate at competitive athletic or sporting events. Detect infractions of rules and decide penalties according to established regulations. Includes all sporting officials, referees, and competition judges.

children.name: Dancers and Choreographers
children.description: Express ideas and stories through dance. May also create and direct dance routines for performances, competitions, or instructional purposes.

children.name: Dancers
children.description: Perform dances. May perform on stage, for broadcasting, or for video recording.

children.name: Choreographers
children.description: Create new dance routines. Rehearse performance of routines. May direct and stage presentations.

children.name: Musicians, Singers, and Related Workers
children.description: Perform music in live or recorded settings, compose or arrange songs, and practice to maintain and develop musical skills.

children.name: Music Directors and Composers
children.description: Conduct, direct, plan, and lead instrumental or vocal performances by musical artists or groups, such as orchestras, bands, choirs, and glee clubs; or create original works of music.

children.name: Music Directors
children.description: Direct and conduct instrumental or vocal performances by musical groups, such as orchestras or choirs.

children.name: Music Composers and Arrangers
children.description: Write and transcribe musical scores.

children.name: Musicians and Singers
children.description: Play one or more musical instruments or sing. May perform on stage, for broadcasting, or for sound or video recording.

children.name: Singers
children.description: Sing songs on stage, radio, television, or motion pictures.

children.name: Musicians, Instrumental
children.description: Play one or more musical instruments in recital, in accompaniment, or as members of an orchestra, band, or other musical group.

children.name: Miscellaneous Entertainers and Performers, Sports and Related Workers
children.description: Engage in entertainment or sports activities not elsewhere classified, including circus performers, stunt performers, or other unique roles in the sports and entertainment industry.

children.name: Disc Jockeys, Except Radio
children.description: Play prerecorded music for live audiences at venues or events such as clubs, parties, or wedding receptions. May use techniques such as mixing, cutting, or sampling to manipulate recordings. May also perform as emcee (master of ceremonies).

children.name: Entertainers and Performers, Sports and Related Workers, All Other
children.description: All entertainers and performers, sports and related workers not listed separately.

children.name: Media and Communication Workers
children.description: This category includes professionals involved in various aspects of media and communication, including journalism, broadcasting, public relations, advertising, and digital media. It encompasses occupations such as reporters, editors, broadcast technicians, public relations specialists, and advertising professionals.

children.name: Announcers
children.description: Present music, news, or sports over television, radio, or live events. May interview guests, operate studio equipment, or provide commentary on broadcasts.

children.name: Broadcast Announcers and Radio Disc Jockeys
children.description: Speak or read from scripted materials, such as news reports or commercial messages, on radio, television, or other communications media. May play and queue music, announce artist or title of performance, identify station, or interview guests.

children.name: Public Address System and Other Announcers
children.description: Make announcements over public address system at sporting or other public events. May act as master of ceremonies or disc jockey at weddings, parties, clubs, or other gathering places.

children.name: News Analysts, Reporters and Correspondents
children.description: Investigate, research, and report on current events and news stories. Gather information through interviews or records, and present findings via print, broadcast, or online media.

children.name: Broadcast News Analysts
children.description: Analyze, interpret, and broadcast news received from various sources.

children.name: Reporters and Correspondents
children.description: Collect and analyze facts about newsworthy events by interview, investigation, or observation. Report and write stories for newspaper, news magazine, radio, or television.

children.name: Public Relations Specialists
children.description: Build and maintain a positive public image for clients or organizations. Create media releases, develop communication strategies, and coordinate promotional events.

children.name: Public Relations Specialists
children.description: Promote or create an intended public image for individuals, groups, or organizations. May write or select material for release to various communications media. May specialize in using social media.

children.name: Writers and Editors
children.description: Originate written content for various media, revise and refine drafts for clarity and accuracy, and ensure final outputs meet editorial standards.

children.name: Editors
children.description: Plan, coordinate, revise, or edit written material. May review proposals and drafts for possible publication.

children.name: Technical Writers
children.description: Write technical materials, such as equipment manuals, appendices, or operating and maintenance instructions. May assist in layout work.

children.name: Writers and Authors
children.description: Originate and prepare written material, such as scripts, stories, advertisements, and other material.

children.name: Copy Writers
children.description: Write advertising copy for use by publication or broadcast media to promote sale of goods and services.

children.name: Poets, Lyricists and Creative Writers
children.description: Create original written works, such as scripts, essays, prose, poetry or song lyrics, for publication or performance.

children.name: Miscellaneous Media and Communication Workers
children.description: Perform communications functions not covered under other occupations, such as press agents, bloggers, or content creators using new media platforms.

children.name: Interpreters and Translators
children.description: Interpret oral or sign language, or translate written text from one language into another.

children.name: Media and Communication Workers, All Other
children.description: All media and communication workers not listed separately.

children.name: Media and Communication Equipment Workers
children.description: This category includes professionals who specialize in the installation, maintenance, and operation of equipment used in media production, broadcasting, telecommunications, and related fields. It encompasses occupations such as broadcast and sound engineering technicians, camera operators, audio and video equipment technicians, and telecommunications equipment installers.

children.name: Broadcast and Sound Engineering Technicians and Radio Operators
children.description: Set up, operate, and maintain equipment to broadcast radio or television programs and record or enhance audio. May also regulate volume and sound quality during broadcasts.

children.name: Audio and Video Technicians
children.description: Set up, maintain, and dismantle audio and video equipment, such as microphones, sound speakers, connecting wires and cables, sound and mixing boards, video cameras, video monitors and servers, and related electronic equipment for live or recorded events, such as concerts, meetings, conventions, presentations, podcasts, news conferences, and sporting events.

children.name: Broadcast Technicians
children.description: Set up, operate, and maintain the electronic equipment used to acquire, edit, and transmit audio and video for radio or television programs. Control and adjust incoming and outgoing broadcast signals to regulate sound volume, signal strength, and signal clarity. Operate satellite, microwave, or other transmitter equipment to broadcast radio or television programs.

children.name: Radio Operators
children.description: Receive and transmit communications using radiotelephone equipment in accordance with government regulations. May repair equipment.

children.name: Sound Engineering Technicians
children.description: Assemble and operate equipment to record, synchronize, mix, edit, or reproduce sound, including music, voices, or sound effects, for theater, video, film, television, podcasts, sporting events, and other productions.

children.name: Photographers
children.description: Capture images of people, events, or objects, using various photographic techniques and equipment. May edit and enhance images for final presentation.

children.name: Photographers
children.description: Photograph people, landscapes, merchandise, or other subjects. May use lighting equipment to enhance a subject's appearance. May use editing software to produce finished images and prints. Includes commercial and industrial photographers, scientific photographers, and photojournalists.

children.name: Television, Video, and Motion Picture Camera Operators and Editors
children.description: Operate cameras to record images or scenes for TV, film, or digital media. Edit raw footage into finished products that meet artistic or project goals.

children.name: Camera Operators, Television, Video, and Film
children.description: Operate television, video, or film camera to record images or scenes for television, video, or film productions.

children.name: Film and Video Editors
children.description: Edit moving images on film, video, or other media. May work with a producer or director to organize images for final production. May edit or synchronize soundtracks with images.

children.name: Miscellaneous Media and Communication Equipment Workers
children.description: Operate or manage specialized media or communication equipment not covered in other classifications, possibly including lighting techs, sound mixers, or satellite communications operators.

children.name: Media and Communication Equipment Workers, All Other
children.description: All media and communication equipment workers not listed separately.

name: Healthcare Practitioners and Technical Occupations
description: Involves diagnosing, treating, and caring for patients. Includes doctors, nurses, pharmacists, and technicians who use clinical knowledge and technical skills to promote and restore health.

children.name: Health Diagnosing and Treating Practitioners
children.description: This category includes a wide range of healthcare professionals involved in diagnosing and treating patients. It encompasses occupations such as physicians, surgeons, dentists, optometrists, podiatrists, chiropractors, and other specialized healthcare practitioners. These professionals work in various healthcare settings, including hospitals, clinics, private practices, and research institutions.

children.name: Chiropractors
children.description: Assess and treat neuromusculoskeletal conditions, focusing on spinal alignment and manipulation. May advise on exercise, lifestyle, and nutrition to promote overall wellness.

children.name: Chiropractors
children.description: Assess, treat, and care for patients by manipulation of spine and musculoskeletal system. May provide spinal adjustment or address sacral or pelvic misalignment.

children.name: Dentists
children.description: Diagnose and treat diseases, injuries, and malformations of the teeth and gums. Provide preventive care, perform dental surgeries, and educate patients on oral health.

children.name: Dentists, General
children.description: Examine, diagnose, and treat diseases, injuries, and malformations of teeth and gums. May treat diseases of nerve, pulp, and other dental tissues affecting oral hygiene and retention of teeth. May fit dental appliances or provide preventive care.

children.name: Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeons
children.description: Perform surgery and related procedures on the hard and soft tissues of the oral and maxillofacial regions to treat diseases, injuries, or defects. May diagnose problems of the oral and maxillofacial regions. May perform surgery to improve function or appearance.

children.name: Orthodontists
children.description: Examine, diagnose, and treat dental malocclusions and oral cavity anomalies. Design and fabricate appliances to realign teeth and jaws to produce and maintain normal function and to improve appearance.

children.name: Prosthodontists
children.description: Diagnose, treat, rehabilitate, design, and fit prostheses that maintain oral function, health, and appearance for patients with clinical conditions associated with teeth, oral and maxillofacial tissues, or the jaw.

children.name: Dentists, All Other Specialists
children.description: All dentists not listed separately.

children.name: Dietitians and Nutritionists
children.description: Advise individuals or groups on nutritional practices to maintain or improve health. May plan and implement meal programs, assess dietary needs, and promote healthy eating.

children.name: Dietitians and Nutritionists
children.description: Plan and conduct food service or nutritional programs to assist in the promotion of health and control of disease. May supervise activities of a department providing quantity food services, counsel individuals, or conduct nutritional research.

children.name: Optometrists
children.description: Examine eyes and visual systems, diagnose eye-related conditions, and prescribe lenses or other treatments to improve and protect vision.

children.name: Optometrists
children.description: Diagnose, manage, and treat conditions and diseases of the human eye and visual system. Examine eyes and visual system, diagnose problems or impairments, prescribe corrective lenses, and provide treatment. May prescribe therapeutic drugs to treat specific eye conditions.

children.name: Pharmacists
children.description: Dispense prescription medications, provide expertise in drug therapy, and counsel patients on medication usage, side effects, and interactions.

children.name: Pharmacists
children.description: Dispense drugs prescribed by physicians and other health practitioners and provide information to patients about medications and their use. May advise physicians and other health practitioners on the selection, dosage, interactions, and side effects of medications.

children.name: Physicians and Surgeons
children.description: Diagnose illnesses, prescribe treatments, and perform procedures or surgeries to restore patient health. May specialize in areas like cardiology, pediatrics, or surgery.

children.name: Anesthesiologists
children.description: Physicians who administer anesthetics prior to, during, or after surgery or other medical procedures.

children.name: Family and General Practitioners
children.description: Physicians who diagnose, treat, and help prevent diseases and injuries that commonly occur in the general population. May refer patients to specialists when needed for further diagnosis or treatment.

children.name: Internists, General
children.description: Physicians who diagnose and provide non-surgical treatment of diseases and injuries of internal organ systems. Provide care mainly for adults who have a wide range of problems associated with the internal organs.

children.name: Obstetricians and Gynecologists
children.description: Physicians who provide medical care related to pregnancy or childbirth and those who diagnose, treat, and help prevent diseases of women, particularly those affecting the reproductive system. May also provide general medical care to women.

children.name: Pediatricians, General
children.description: Physicians who diagnose, treat, and help prevent children's diseases and injuries.

children.name: Psychiatrists
children.description: Physicians who diagnose, treat, and help prevent disorders of the mind.

children.name: Surgeons
children.description: Physicians who treat diseases, injuries, and deformities by invasive, minimally-invasive, or non-invasive surgical methods, such as using instruments, appliances, or by manual manipulation.

children.name: Physicians and Surgeons, All Other
children.description: All physicians and surgeons not listed separately.

children.name: Allergists and Immunologists
children.description: Diagnose, treat, and help prevent allergic diseases and disease processes affecting the immune system.

children.name: Dermatologists
children.description: Diagnose, treat, and help prevent diseases or other conditions of the skin.

children.name: Hospitalists
children.description: Provide inpatient care predominantly in settings such as medical wards, acute care units, intensive care units, rehabilitation centers, or emergency rooms. Manage and coordinate patient care throughout treatment.

children.name: Neurologists
children.description: Diagnose, treat, and help prevent diseases and disorders of the nervous system.

children.name: Nuclear Medicine Physicians
children.description: Diagnose and treat diseases using radioactive materials and techniques. May monitor radionuclide preparation, administration, and disposition.

children.name: Ophthalmologists
children.description: Diagnose, treat, and help prevent diseases and injuries of the eyes and related structures.

children.name: Pathologists
children.description: Diagnose presence and stage of diseases using laboratory techniques and patient specimens. Study the nature, cause, and development of diseases. May perform autopsies.

children.name: Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation Physicians
children.description: Diagnose and treat disorders requiring physiotherapy to provide physical, mental, and occupational rehabilitation.

children.name: Preventive Medicine Physicians
children.description: Apply knowledge of general preventive medicine and public health issues to promote health care to groups or individuals, and aid in the prevention or reduction of risk of disease, injury, disability, or death. May practice population-based medicine or diagnose and treat patients in the context of clinical health promotion and disease prevention.

children.name: Radiologists
children.description: Examine and diagnose disorders and diseases using x-rays and radioactive materials. May treat patients.

children.name: Sports Medicine Physicians
children.description: Diagnose, treat, and help prevent injuries that occur during sporting events, athletic training, and physical activities.

children.name: Urologists
children.description: Diagnose, treat, and help prevent benign and malignant medical and surgical disorders of the genitourinary system and the renal glands.

children.name: Physician Assistants
children.description: Practice medicine under the supervision of physicians. Conduct examinations, diagnose conditions, provide treatment, and write prescriptions where legally permitted.

children.name: Physician Assistants
children.description: Provide healthcare services typically performed by a physician, under the supervision of a physician. Conduct complete physicals, provide treatment, and counsel patients. May, in some cases, prescribe medication. Must graduate from an accredited educational program for physician assistants.

children.name: Anesthesiologist Assistants
children.description: Assist anesthesiologists in the administration of anesthesia for surgical and non-surgical procedures. Monitor patient status and provide patient care during surgical treatment.

children.name: Podiatrists
children.description: Diagnose and treat diseases, deformities, and injuries of the foot, ankle, and lower leg. May perform surgeries, prescribe orthotics, or provide preventive care.

children.name: Podiatrists
children.description: Diagnose and treat diseases and deformities of the human foot.

children.name: Therapists
children.description: Provide rehabilitative, therapeutic services (e.g., physical, occupational, speech) to help patients overcome physical, mental, or developmental challenges.

children.name: Occupational Therapists
children.description: Assess, plan, and organize rehabilitative programs that help build or restore vocational, homemaking, and daily living skills, as well as general independence, to persons with disabilities or developmental delays. Use therapeutic techniques, adapt the individual's environment, teach skills, and modify specific tasks that present barriers to the individual.

children.name: Low Vision Therapists, Orientation and Mobility Specialists, and Vision Rehabilitation Therapists
children.description: Provide therapy to patients with visual impairments to improve their functioning in daily life activities. May train patients in activities such as computer use, communication skills, or home management skills.

children.name: Physical Therapists
children.description: Assess, plan, organize, and participate in rehabilitative programs that improve mobility, relieve pain, increase strength, and improve or correct disabling conditions resulting from disease or injury.

children.name: Radiation Therapists
children.description: Provide radiation therapy to patients as prescribed by a radiation oncologist according to established practices and standards. Duties may include reviewing prescription and diagnosis; acting as liaison with physician and supportive care personnel; preparing equipment, such as immobilization, treatment, and protection devices; and maintaining records, reports, and files. May assist in dosimetry procedures and tumor localization.

children.name: Recreational Therapists
children.description: Plan, direct, or coordinate medically-approved recreation programs for patients in hospitals, nursing homes, or other institutions. Activities include sports, trips, dramatics, social activities, and crafts. May assess a patient condition and recommend appropriate recreational activity.

children.name: Art Therapists
children.description: Plan or conduct art therapy sessions or programs to improve clients' physical, cognitive, or emotional well-being.

children.name: Music Therapists
children.description: Plan, organize, or direct medically prescribed music therapy activities designed to positively influence patients' psychological or behavioral status.

children.name: Respiratory Therapists
children.description: Assess, treat, and care for patients with breathing disorders. Assume primary responsibility for all respiratory care modalities, including the supervision of respiratory therapy technicians. Initiate and conduct therapeutic procedures; maintain patient records; and select, assemble, check, and operate equipment.

children.name: Speech-Language Pathologists
children.description: Assess and treat persons with speech, language, voice, and fluency disorders. May select alternative communication systems and teach their use. May perform research related to speech and language problems.

children.name: Exercise Physiologists
children.description: Assess, plan, or implement fitness programs that include exercise or physical activities such as those designed to improve cardiorespiratory function, body composition, muscular strength, muscular endurance, or flexibility.

children.name: Therapists, All Other
children.description: All therapists not listed separately.

children.name: Veterinarians
children.description: Diagnose and treat diseases and injuries in animals. May perform surgeries, vaccinate animals, prescribe medications, and advise on care and feeding.

children.name: Veterinarians
children.description: Diagnose, treat, or research diseases and injuries of animals. Includes veterinarians who conduct research and development, inspect livestock, or care for pets and companion animals.

children.name: Registered Nurses
children.description: Assess patients’ health problems, administer nursing care, educate patients and the public about health conditions, and maintain medical records.

children.name: Registered Nurses
children.description: Assess patient health problems and needs, develop and implement nursing care plans, and maintain medical records. Administer nursing care to ill, injured, convalescent, or disabled patients. May advise patients on health maintenance and disease prevention or provide case management. Licensing or registration required.

children.name: Acute Care Nurses
children.description: Provide advanced nursing care for patients with acute conditions such as heart attacks, respiratory distress syndrome, or shock. May care for pre- and post-operative patients or perform advanced, invasive diagnostic or therapeutic procedures.

children.name: Advanced Practice Psychiatric Nurses
children.description: Assess, diagnose, and treat individuals and families with mental health or substance use disorders or the potential for such disorders. Apply therapeutic activities, including the prescription of medication, per state regulations, and the administration of psychotherapy.

children.name: Critical Care Nurses
children.description: Provide specialized nursing care for patients in critical or coronary care units.

children.name: Clinical Nurse Specialists
children.description: Direct nursing staff in the provision of patient care in a clinical practice setting, such as a hospital, hospice, clinic, or home. Ensure adherence to established clinical policies, protocols, regulations, and standards.

children.name: Nurse Anesthetists
children.description: Administer anesthesia, monitor patients’ vital signs, and oversee patient recovery from anesthesia under the guidance of anesthesiologists or other physicians.

children.name: Nurse Anesthetists
children.description: Administer anesthesia, monitor patient's vital signs, and oversee patient recovery from anesthesia. May assist anesthesiologists, surgeons, other physicians, or dentists. Must be registered nurses who have specialized graduate education.

children.name: Nurse Midwives
children.description: Provide prenatal, childbirth, and postpartum care to women, manage low-risk pregnancies, and offer reproductive health education and counseling.

children.name: Nurse Midwives
children.description: Diagnose and coordinate all aspects of the birthing process, either independently or as part of a healthcare team. May provide well-woman gynecological care. Must have specialized, graduate nursing education.

children.name: Nurse Practitioners
children.description: Deliver advanced nursing services, including diagnosing and managing most common and chronic illnesses. Often focus on health promotion, disease prevention, and patient education.

children.name: Nurse Practitioners
children.description: Diagnose and treat acute, episodic, or chronic illness, independently or as part of a healthcare team. May focus on health promotion and disease prevention. May order, perform, or interpret diagnostic tests such as lab work and x rays. May prescribe medication. Must be registered nurses who have specialized graduate education.

children.name: Audiologists
children.description: Identify, assess, and manage disorders of hearing, balance, and related ear problems. May fit hearing aids and counsel patients on hearing loss adaptation.

children.name: Audiologists
children.description: Assess and treat persons with hearing and related disorders. May fit hearing aids and provide auditory training. May perform research related to hearing problems.

children.name: Miscellaneous Health Diagnosing and Treating Practitioners
children.description: Occupations providing health assessment and treatment services not classified under a specific healthcare role, potentially including naturopaths, acupuncturists, or other specialized practitioners.

children.name: Health Diagnosing and Treating Practitioners, All Other
children.description: All health diagnosing and treating practitioners not listed separately.

children.name: Acupuncturists
children.description: Provide treatment of symptoms and disorders using needles and small electrical currents. May provide massage treatment. May also provide preventive treatments.

children.name: Naturopathic Physicians
children.description: Diagnose, treat, and help prevent diseases using a system of practice that is based on the natural healing capacity of individuals. May use physiological, psychological or mechanical methods. May also use natural medicines, prescription or legend drugs, foods, herbs, or other natural remedies.

children.name: Orthoptists
children.description: Diagnose and treat visual system disorders such as binocular vision and eye movement impairments.

children.name: Health Technologists and Technicians
children.description: This category includes healthcare professionals who perform various technical and diagnostic procedures to support patient care. It encompasses occupations such as medical and clinical laboratory technologists, radiologic technologists, cardiovascular technologists, surgical technologists, and medical records and health information technicians. These professionals work in hospitals, clinics, diagnostic laboratories, and other healthcare settings.

children.name: Clinical Laboratory Technologists and Technicians
children.description: Perform complex medical laboratory tests for diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of disease. Analyze blood, tissue, and body fluids.

children.name: Medical and Clinical Laboratory Technologists
children.description: Perform complex medical laboratory tests for diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of disease. May train or supervise staff.

children.name: Cytogenetic Technologists
children.description: Analyze chromosomes or chromosome segments found in biological specimens, such as amniotic fluids, bone marrow, solid tumors, and blood to aid in the study, diagnosis, classification, or treatment of inherited or acquired genetic diseases. Conduct analyses through classical cytogenetic, fluorescent in situ hybridization (FISH) or array comparative genome hybridization (aCGH) techniques.

children.name: Cytotechnologists
children.description: Stain, mount, and study cells to detect evidence of cancer, hormonal abnormalities, and other pathological conditions following established standards and practices.

children.name: Histotechnologists and Histologic Technicians
children.description: Prepare histologic slides from tissue sections for microscopic examination and diagnosis by pathologists. May assist in research studies.

children.name: Medical and Clinical Laboratory Technicians
children.description: Perform routine medical laboratory tests for the diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of disease. May work under the supervision of a medical technologist.

children.name: Dental Hygienists
children.description: Clean teeth, examine patients for signs of oral disease, and provide preventative dental care. May educate patients on ways to improve oral health.

children.name: Dental Hygienists
children.description: Clean teeth and examine oral areas, head, and neck for signs of oral disease. May educate patients on oral hygiene, take and develop x rays, or apply fluoride or sealants.

children.name: Diagnostic Related Technologists and Technicians
children.description: Operate specialized diagnostic imaging equipment (e.g., X-rays, MRI) or perform tests to help healthcare providers diagnose diseases or injuries.

children.name: Cardiovascular Technologists and Technicians
children.description: Conduct tests on pulmonary or cardiovascular systems of patients for diagnostic, therapeutic, or research purposes. May conduct or assist in electrocardiograms, cardiac catheterizations, pulmonary functions, lung capacity, and similar tests.

children.name: Diagnostic Medical Sonographers
children.description: Produce ultrasonic recordings of internal organs for use by physicians. Includes vascular technologists.

children.name: Nuclear Medicine Technologists
children.description: Prepare, administer, and measure radioactive isotopes in therapeutic, diagnostic, and tracer studies using a variety of radioisotope equipment. Prepare stock solutions of radioactive materials and calculate doses to be administered by radiologists. Subject patients to radiation. Execute blood volume, red cell survival, and fat absorption studies following standard laboratory techniques.

children.name: Magnetic Resonance Imaging Technologists
children.description: Operate Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) scanners. Monitor patient safety and comfort, and view images of area being scanned to ensure quality of pictures. May administer gadolinium contrast dosage intravenously. May interview patient, explain MRI procedures, and position patient on examining table. May enter into the computer data such as patient history, anatomical area to be scanned, orientation specified, and position of entry.

children.name: Radiologic Technologists and Technicians*
children.description: Operate Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) scanners. Monitor patient safety and comfort, and view images of area being scanned to ensure quality of pictures. May administer gadolinium contrast dosage intravenously. May interview patient, explain MRI procedures, and position patient on examining table. May enter into the computer data such as patient history, anatomical area to be scanned, orientation specified, and position of entry.

children.name: Emergency Medical Technicians and Paramedics
children.description: Provide first-response medical care and transport for sick or injured individuals in emergency situations. Assess patient conditions, perform basic interventions, and communicate with hospital staff.

children.name: Emergency Medical Technicians and Paramedics
children.description: Assess injuries, administer emergency medical care, and extricate trapped individuals. Transport injured or sick persons to medical facilities.

children.name: Health Practitioner Support Technologists and Technicians
children.description: Assist practitioners in fields like surgery, pharmacy, or rehabilitation by preparing equipment, handling specimens, or aiding in procedures.

children.name: Dietetic Technicians
children.description: Assist in the provision of food service and nutritional programs, under the supervision of a dietitian. May plan and produce meals based on established guidelines, teach principles of food and nutrition, or counsel individuals.

children.name: Pharmacy Technicians
children.description: Prepare medications under the direction of a pharmacist. May measure, mix, count out, label, and record amounts and dosages of medications according to prescription orders.

children.name: Psychiatric Technicians
children.description: Care for individuals with mental or emotional conditions or disabilities, following the instructions of physicians or other health practitioners. Monitor patients' physical and emotional well-being and report to medical staff. May participate in rehabilitation and treatment programs, help with personal hygiene, and administer oral or injectable medications.

children.name: Respiratory Therapy Technicians
children.description: Provide respiratory care under the direction of respiratory therapists and physicians.

children.name: Surgical Technologists
children.description: Assist in operations, under the supervision of surgeons, registered nurses, or other surgical personnel. May help set up operating room, prepare and transport patients for surgery, adjust lights and equipment, pass instruments and other supplies to surgeons and surgeons' assistants, hold retractors, cut sutures, and help count sponges, needles, supplies, and instruments.

children.name: Veterinary Technologists and Technicians
children.description: Perform medical tests in a laboratory environment for use in the treatment and diagnosis of diseases in animals. Prepare vaccines and serums for prevention of diseases. Prepare tissue samples, take blood samples, and execute laboratory tests, such as urinalysis and blood counts. Clean and sterilize instruments and materials and maintain equipment and machines. May assist a veterinarian during surgery.

children.name: Ophthalmic Medical Technicians
children.description: Assist ophthalmologists by performing ophthalmic clinical functions. May administer eye exams, administer eye medications, and instruct the patient in care and use of corrective lenses.

children.name: Licensed Practical and Licensed Vocational Nurses
children.description: Provide basic nursing care under the direction of registered nurses and doctors. Monitor patients’ health, administer basic treatments, and keep records.

children.name: Licensed Practical and Licensed Vocational Nurses
children.description: Care for ill, injured, or convalescing patients or persons with disabilities in hospitals, nursing homes, clinics, private homes, group homes, and similar institutions. May work under the supervision of a registered nurse. Licensing required.

children.name: Medical Records and Health Information Technicians
children.description: Organize and manage health information data, ensuring accuracy, accessibility, and security in both paper and electronic systems.

children.name: Medical Records and Health Information Technicians
children.description: Compile, process, and maintain medical records of hospital and clinic patients in a manner consistent with medical, administrative, ethical, legal, and regulatory requirements of the health care system. Process, maintain, compile, and report patient information for health requirements and standards in a manner consistent with the healthcare industry's numerical coding system.

children.name: Opticians, Dispensing
children.description: Fit and adjust eyeglasses or contact lenses according to prescriptions from ophthalmologists or optometrists. Help customers select frames and educate on lens care.

children.name: Opticians, Dispensing
children.description: Design, measure, fit, and adapt lenses and frames for client according to written optical prescription or specification. Assist client with inserting, removing, and caring for contact lenses. Assist client with selecting frames. Measure customer for size of eyeglasses and coordinate frames with facial and eye measurements and optical prescription. Prepare work order for optical laboratory containing instructions for grinding and mounting lenses in frames. Verify exactness of finished lens spectacles. Adjust frame and lens position to fit client. May shape or reshape frames. Includes contact lens opticians.

children.name: Miscellaneous Health Technologists and Technicians
children.description: Support healthcare delivery by performing specialized technical tasks not covered by other defined roles, such as surgical technologists or neurodiagnostic technologists.
