children.name: Orthotists and Prosthetists
children.description: Design, measure, fit, and adapt orthopedic braces, appliances or prostheses, such as limbs or facial parts for patients with disabling conditions.

children.name: Hearing Aid Specialists
children.description: Select and fit hearing aids for customers. Administer and interpret tests of hearing. Assess hearing instrument efficacy. Take ear impressions and prepare, design, and modify ear molds.

children.name: Health Technologists and Technicians, All Other
children.description: All health technologists and technicians not listed separately.

children.name: Neurodiagnostic Technologists
children.description: Conduct electroneurodiagnostic (END) tests such as electroencephalograms, evoked potentials, polysomnograms, or electronystagmograms. May perform nerve conduction studies.

children.name: Ophthalmic Medical Technologists
children.description: Assist ophthalmologists by performing ophthalmic clinical functions and ophthalmic photography. Provide instruction and supervision to other ophthalmic personnel. Assist with minor surgical procedures, applying aseptic techniques and preparing instruments. May perform eye exams, administer eye medications, and instruct patients in care and use of corrective lenses.

children.name: Radiologic Technicians
children.description: Maintain and use equipment and supplies necessary to demonstrate portions of the human body on x-ray film or fluoroscopic screen for diagnostic purposes.

children.name: Surgical Assistants
children.description: Assist surgeons during surgery by performing duties such as tissue retraction, insertion of tubes and intravenous lines, or closure of surgical wounds. Perform preoperative and postoperative duties to facilitate patient care.

children.name: Other Healthcare Practitioners and Technical Occupations
children.description: This category includes a diverse range of healthcare professionals who perform specialized roles in patient care, diagnostics, therapy, and technical support. It encompasses occupations such as dental hygienists, nuclear medicine technologists, veterinary technologists and technicians, ophthalmic medical technicians, and pharmacy technicians.

children.name: Occupational Health and Safety Specialists and Technicians
children.description: Evaluate and analyze work environments to design programs and procedures that control, eliminate, and prevent disease or injury caused by chemical, physical, and biological agents.

children.name: Occupational Health and Safety Specialists
children.description: Review, evaluate, and analyze work environments and design programs and procedures to control, eliminate, and prevent disease or injury caused by chemical, physical, and biological agents or ergonomic factors. May conduct inspections and enforce adherence to laws and regulations governing the health and safety of individuals. May be employed in the public or private sector. Includes environmental protection officers.

children.name: Occupational Health and Safety Technicians
children.description: Collect data on work environments for analysis by occupational health and safety specialists. Implement and conduct evaluation of programs designed to limit chemical, physical, biological, and ergonomic risks to workers.

children.name: Miscellaneous Health Practitioners and Technical Workers
children.description: Engage in healthcare tasks not classified under other occupations. May involve emerging healthcare technologies or highly specialized medical support activities.

children.name: Athletic Trainers
children.description: Evaluate and treat musculoskeletal injuries or illnesses. Provide preventive, therapeutic, emergency, and rehabilitative care.

children.name: Genetic Counselors
children.description: Assess individual or family risk for a variety of inherited conditions, such as genetic disorders and birth defects. Provide information to other healthcare providers or to individuals and families concerned with the risk of inherited conditions. Advise individuals and families to support informed decisionmaking and coping methods for those at risk. May help conduct research related to genetic conditions or genetic counseling.

children.name: Healthcare Practitioners and Technical Workers, All Other
children.description: All healthcare practitioners and technical workers not listed separately.

children.name: Midwives
children.description: Provide prenatal care and childbirth assistance.

name: Healthcare Support Occupations
description: Provides assistance to healthcare practitioners, including aides and assistants who handle patient care tasks, administrative support, or routine clinical procedures under supervision of licensed professionals.

children.name: Nursing, Psychiatric, and Home Health Aides
children.description: This category includes healthcare professionals who provide essential care and assistance to patients in various settings. It encompasses occupations such as registered nurses, licensed practical and vocational nurses, psychiatric aides, home health aides, and personal care aides. These professionals work in hospitals, nursing homes, psychiatric facilities, home healthcare settings, and other healthcare institutions.

children.name: Nursing, Psychiatric, and Home Health Aides
children.description: Provide basic patient care in home, long-term care, or hospital settings. Monitor vital signs, assist with daily living activities, and report patient status to nursing staff.

children.name: Home Health Aides
children.description: Provide routine individualized healthcare such as changing bandages and dressing wounds, and applying topical medications to the elderly, convalescents, or persons with disabilities at the patient's home or in a care facility. Monitor or report changes in health status. May also provide personal care such as bathing, dressing, and grooming of patient.

children.name: Nursing Aides, Orderlies, and Attendants*
children.description: Provide basic patient care under direction of nursing staff. Perform duties such as feed, bathe, dress, groom, or move patients, or change linens. May transfer or transport patients. Includes nursing care attendants, nursing aides, and nursing attendants.

children.name: Psychiatric Aides
children.description: Assist mentally impaired or emotionally disturbed patients, working under direction of nursing and medical staff. May assist with daily living activities, lead patients in educational and recreational activities, or accompany patients to and from examinations and treatments. May restrain violent patients. Includes psychiatric orderlies.

children.name: Nursing Assistants
children.description: Provide basic patient care under direction of nursing staff. Perform duties such as feed, bathe, dress, groom, or move patients, or change linens. May transfer or transport patients. Includes nursing care attendants, nursing aides, and nursing attendants.

children.name: Orderlies
children.description: Transport patients to areas such as operating rooms or x-ray rooms using wheelchairs, stretchers, or moveable beds. May maintain stocks of supplies or clean and transport equipment.

children.name: Occupational Therapy and Physical Therapist Assistants and Aides
children.description: This category includes healthcare professionals who work under the guidance of occupational therapists and physical therapists to provide support and assistance to patients during therapy sessions. It encompasses occupations such as occupational therapy assistants, occupational therapy aides, physical therapist assistants, and physical therapist aides. These professionals assist patients in performing therapeutic exercises, prepare treatment areas, and provide support to therapists in delivering care.

children.name: Occupational Therapy Assistants and Aides
children.description: Help occupational therapists provide rehabilitative services to patients, assisting in treatments designed to improve mobility, coordination, and daily living skills.

children.name: Occupational Therapy Assistants
children.description: Assist occupational therapists in providing occupational therapy treatments and procedures. May, in accordance with state laws, assist in development of treatment plans, carry out routine functions, direct activity programs, and document the progress of treatments. Generally requires formal training.

children.name: Occupational Therapy Aides
children.description: Under close supervision of an occupational therapist or occupational therapy assistant, perform only delegated, selected, or routine tasks in specific situations. These duties include preparing patient and treatment room.

children.name: Physical Therapist Assistants and Aides
children.description: Assist physical therapists in providing treatments that improve patient mobility, relieve pain, and prevent or limit permanent physical disabilities.

children.name: Physical Therapist Assistants
children.description: Assist physical therapists in providing physical therapy treatments and procedures. May, in accordance with state laws, assist in the development of treatment plans, carry out routine functions, document the progress of treatment, and modify specific treatments in accordance with patient status and within the scope of treatment plans established by a physical therapist. Generally requires formal training.

children.name: Physical Therapist Aides
children.description: Under close supervision of a physical therapist or physical therapy assistant, perform only delegated, selected, or routine tasks in specific situations. These duties include preparing the patient and the treatment area.

children.name: Other Healthcare Support Occupations
children.description: This category includes a variety of healthcare support roles that provide assistance and support to healthcare professionals and patients. It encompasses occupations such as medical transcriptionists, pharmacy aides, veterinary assistants and laboratory animal caretakers, dietetic technicians, and medical equipment preparers. These professionals work in hospitals, clinics, laboratories, pharmacies, and other healthcare settings.

children.name: Massage Therapists
children.description: Use touch to manipulate soft-tissue muscles of the body, relieving pain, improving circulation, or promoting relaxation. May also advise clients on stretching, strengthening, and overall wellness.

children.name: Massage Therapists
children.description: Perform therapeutic massages of soft tissues and joints. May assist in the assessment of range of motion and muscle strength, or propose client therapy plans.

children.name: Miscellaneous Healthcare Support Occupations
children.description: Deliver allied health support services not classified under specific roles, including specialized therapeutic aides or other emerging support positions in healthcare settings.

children.name: Dental Assistants
children.description: Perform limited clinical duties under the direction of a dentist. Clinical duties may include equipment preparation and sterilization, preparing patients for treatment, assisting the dentist during treatment, and providing patients with instructions for oral healthcare procedures. May perform administrative duties such as scheduling appointments, maintaining medical records, billing, and coding information for insurance purposes.

children.name: Medical Assistants
children.description: Perform administrative and certain clinical duties under the direction of a physician. Administrative duties may include scheduling appointments, maintaining medical records, billing, and coding information for insurance purposes. Clinical duties may include taking and recording vital signs and medical histories, preparing patients for examination, drawing blood, and administering medications as directed by physician.

children.name: Medical Equipment Preparers
children.description: Prepare, sterilize, install, or clean laboratory or healthcare equipment. May perform routine laboratory tasks and operate or inspect equipment.

children.name: Medical Transcriptionists
children.description: Transcribe medical reports recorded by physicians and other healthcare practitioners using various electronic devices, covering office visits, emergency room visits, diagnostic imaging studies, operations, chart reviews, and final summaries. Transcribe dictated reports and translate abbreviations into fully understandable form. Edit as necessary and return reports in either printed or electronic form for review and signature, or correction.

children.name: Pharmacy Aides
children.description: Record drugs delivered to the pharmacy, store incoming merchandise, and inform the supervisor of stock needs. May operate cash register and accept prescriptions for filling.

children.name: Veterinary Assistants and Laboratory Animal Caretakers
children.description: Feed, water, and examine pets and other nonfarm animals for signs of illness, disease, or injury in laboratories and animal hospitals and clinics. Clean and disinfect cages and work areas, and sterilize laboratory and surgical equipment. May provide routine postoperative care, administer medication orally or topically, or prepare samples for laboratory examination under the supervision of veterinary or laboratory animal technologists or technicians, veterinarians, or scientists.

children.name: Phlebotomists
children.description: Draw blood for tests, transfusions, donations, or research. May explain the procedure to patients and assist in the recovery of patients with adverse reactions.

children.name: Healthcare Support Workers, All Other
children.description: All healthcare support workers not listed separately.

children.name: Speech-Language Pathology Assistants
children.description: Assist speech-language pathologists in the assessment and treatment of speech, language, voice, and fluency disorders. Implement speech and language programs or activities as planned and directed by speech-language pathologists. Monitor the use of alternative communication devices and systems.

children.name: Endoscopy Technicians
children.description: Maintain a sterile field to provide support for physicians and nurses during endoscopy procedures. Prepare and maintain instruments and equipment. May obtain specimens.

name: Protective Service Occupations
description: Responsible for safeguarding people, property, and institutions. Occupations include law enforcement officers, firefighters, corrections staff, and other roles ensuring public safety.

children.name: Supervisors of Protective Service Workers
children.description: This category includes supervisors who oversee and manage the activities of protective service workers in various industries. It encompasses occupations such as police supervisors, fire and emergency medical service supervisors, gaming supervisors, and transportation security screeners supervisors. These professionals ensure compliance with regulations, provide guidance to subordinates, and maintain the efficiency and effectiveness of protective service operations.

children.name: First-Line Supervisors of Law Enforcement Workers
children.description: Direct and coordinate activities of police officers or other law enforcement personnel. Oversee training, patrol, investigations, and administrative tasks.

children.name: First-Line Supervisors of Correctional Officers
children.description: Directly supervise and coordinate activities of correctional officers and jailers.

children.name: First-Line Supervisors of Police and Detectives
children.description: Directly supervise and coordinate activities of members of police force.

children.name: First-Line Supervisors of Fire Fighting and Prevention Workers
children.description: Supervise and coordinate firefighters or other staff responding to fires and other emergencies. Oversee rescue operations, equipment maintenance, and training.

children.name: First-Line Supervisors of Firefighting and Prevention Workers
children.description: Directly supervise and coordinate activities of workers engaged in firefighting and fire prevention and control.

children.name: Municipal Fire Fighting and Prevention Supervisors
children.description: Supervise fire fighters who control and extinguish municipal fires, protect life and property, and conduct rescue efforts.

children.name: Forest Fire Fighting and Prevention Supervisors
children.description: Supervise fire fighters who control and suppress fires in forests or vacant public land.

children.name: Miscellaneous First-Line Supervisors, Protective Service Workers
children.description: Provide oversight for protective service personnel not included in standard categories, such as lifeguard supervisors or security shift leaders.

children.name: First-Line Supervisors of Protective Service Workers, All Other
children.description: All protective service supervisors not listed separately above.

children.name: Fire Fighting and Prevention Workers
children.description: This category includes professionals who specialize in fire prevention, fire suppression, and emergency response. It encompasses occupations such as firefighters, fire inspectors, and fire investigators. Firefighters respond to emergency situations, extinguish fires, and provide medical assistance. Fire inspectors ensure compliance with fire codes and regulations, while fire investigators determine the cause and origin of fires.

children.name: Firefighters
children.description: Combat and extinguish fires, respond to emergencies, and safeguard life and property. Perform rescue operations, administer first aid, and maintain firefighting equipment.

children.name: Firefighters
children.description: Control and extinguish fires or respond to emergency situations where life, property, or the environment is at risk. Duties may include fire prevention, emergency medical service, hazardous material response, search and rescue, and disaster assistance.

children.name: Municipal Firefighters
children.description: Control and extinguish municipal fires, protect life and property and conduct rescue efforts.

children.name: Forest Firefighters
children.description: Control and suppress fires in forests or vacant public land.

children.name: Fire Inspectors
children.description: Inspect buildings to detect fire hazards and enforce local ordinances or state laws regulating fire safety. Investigate fire causes and origins.

children.name: Fire Inspectors and Investigators
children.description: Inspect buildings to detect fire hazards and enforce local ordinances and state laws, or investigate and gather facts to determine cause of fires and explosions.

children.name: Fire Inspectors
children.description: Inspect buildings and equipment to detect fire hazards and enforce state and local regulations.

children.name: Fire Investigators
children.description: Conduct investigations to determine causes of fires and explosions.

children.name: Forest Fire Inspectors and Prevention Specialists
children.description: Enforce fire regulations, inspect forest for fire hazards, and recommend forest fire prevention or control measures. May report forest fires and weather conditions.

children.name: Law Enforcement Workers
children.description: This category includes occupations such as police officers, detectives, and transit and railroad police. Law Enforcement Workers are responsible for maintaining public safety, enforcing laws, conducting investigations, and ensuring the security of individuals and property.

children.name: Bailiffs, Correctional Officers, and Jailers
children.description: Maintain order in courts or supervise correctional facility inmates. Enforce rules, conduct searches, and ensure safety and security.

children.name: Bailiffs
children.description: Maintain order in courts of law.

children.name: Correctional Officers and Jailers
children.description: Guard inmates in penal or rehabilitative institutions in accordance with established regulations and procedures. May guard prisoners in transit between jail, courtroom, prison, or other point. Includes deputy sheriffs and police who spend the majority of their time guarding prisoners in correctional institutions.

children.name: Detectives and Criminal Investigators
children.description: Gather facts and collect evidence for criminal cases. Conduct interviews, surveillance, and investigations to solve crimes.

children.name: Detectives and Criminal Investigators
children.description: Conduct investigations related to suspected violations of federal, state, or local laws to prevent or solve crimes.

children.name: Police Detectives
children.description: Conduct investigations to prevent crimes or solve criminal cases.

children.name: Police Identification and Records Officers
children.description: Collect evidence at crime scene, classify and identify fingerprints, and photograph evidence for use in criminal and civil cases.

children.name: Criminal Investigators and Special Agents
children.description: Investigate alleged or suspected criminal violations of Federal, state, or local laws to determine if evidence is sufficient to recommend prosecution.

children.name: Immigration and Customs Inspectors
children.description: Investigate and inspect persons, common carriers, goods, and merchandise, arriving in or departing from the United States or between states to detect violations of immigration and customs laws and regulations.

children.name: Intelligence Analysts
children.description: Gather, analyze, or evaluate information from a variety of sources, such as law enforcement databases, surveillance, intelligence networks or geographic information systems. Use intelligence data to anticipate and prevent organized crime activities, such as terrorism.

children.name: Fish and Game Wardens
children.description: Enforce fishing, hunting, and boating laws. Patrol wildlife areas, investigate complaints, and ensure protection of wildlife populations.

children.name: Fish and Game Wardens
children.description: Patrol assigned area to prevent fish and game law violations. Investigate reports of damage to crops or property by wildlife. Compile biological data.

children.name: Parking Enforcement Workers
children.description: Monitor parking regulations, issue tickets for violations, and direct vehicle or pedestrian traffic as needed.

children.name: Parking Enforcement Workers
children.description: Patrol assigned area, such as public parking lot or city streets to issue tickets to overtime parking violators and illegally parked vehicles.

children.name: Police Officers
children.description: Protect life and property, enforce laws, patrol assigned areas, respond to emergencies, and investigate crimes.

children.name: Police and Sheriff's Patrol Officers
children.description: Maintain order and protect life and property by enforcing local, tribal, state, or federal laws and ordinances. Perform a combination of the following duties: patrol a specific area; direct traffic; issue traffic summonses; investigate accidents; apprehend and arrest suspects, or serve legal processes of courts. Includes police officers working at educational institutions.

children.name: Police Patrol Officers
children.description: Patrol assigned area to enforce laws and ordinances, regulate traffic, control crowds, prevent crime, and arrest violators.

children.name: Sheriffs and Deputy Sheriffs
children.description: Enforce law and order in rural or unincorporated districts or serve legal processes of courts. May patrol courthouse, guard court or grand jury, or escort defendants.

children.name: Transit and Railroad Police
children.description: Protect and police railroad and transit property, employees, or passengers.

children.name: Other Protective Service Workers
children.description: This category includes occupations such as security guards, gaming surveillance officers, and transportation security screeners. Other Protective Service Workers are responsible for ensuring the safety and security of individuals, properties, and facilities in various settings.

children.name: Animal Control Workers
children.description: Handle situations involving stray, dangerous, or abused animals. Enforce animal licensing laws and investigate reports of animal mistreatment.

children.name: Animal Control Workers
children.description: Handle animals for the purpose of investigations of mistreatment, or control of abandoned, dangerous, or unattended animals.

children.name: Private Detectives and Investigators
children.description: Gather information for clients using interviews, surveillance, or research. May investigate financial, legal, or personal matters.

children.name: Private Detectives and Investigators
children.description: Gather, analyze, compile, and report information regarding individuals or organizations to clients, or detect occurrences of unlawful acts or infractions of rules in private establishment.

children.name: Security Guards and Gaming Surveillance Officers
children.description: Guard property against theft, vandalism, or illegal activity. Monitor premises, check identification, and use video surveillance in casinos and other facilities.

children.name: Gambling Surveillance Officers and Gambling Investigators
children.description: Observe gambling operation for irregular activities such as cheating or theft by either employees or patrons. Investigate potential threats to gambling assets such as money, chips, and gambling equipment. Act as oversight and security agent for management and customers.

children.name: Security Guards
children.description: Guard, patrol, or monitor premises to prevent theft, violence, or infractions of rules. May operate x-ray and metal detector equipment.

children.name: Miscellaneous Protective Service Workers
children.description: Engage in protective service roles not classified elsewhere, such as crossing guards, transportation security screeners, or school security.

children.name: Crossing Guards and Flaggers
children.description: Guide or control vehicular or pedestrian traffic at such places as streets, schools, railroad crossings, or construction sites.

children.name: Lifeguards, Ski Patrol, and Other Recreational Protective Service Workers
children.description: Monitor recreational areas, such as pools, beaches, or ski slopes, to provide assistance and protection to participants.

children.name: Transportation Security Screeners
children.description: Conduct screening of passengers, baggage, or cargo to ensure compliance with Transportation Security Administration (TSA) regulations. May operate basic security equipment such as x-ray machines and hand wands at screening checkpoints.

children.name: Protective Service Workers, All Other
children.description: All protective service workers not listed separately.

children.name: Retail Loss Prevention Specialists
children.description: Implement procedures and systems to prevent merchandise loss. Conduct audits and investigations of employee activity. May assist in developing policies, procedures, and systems for safeguarding assets.

name: Food Preparation and Serving Related Occupations
description: Involves preparing and serving food and beverages in restaurants, cafeterias, and other dining establishments. Includes cooks, waitstaff, bartenders, and related support staff.

children.name: Supervisors of Food Preparation and Serving Workers
children.description: This category includes supervisors and managers who oversee food preparation and serving workers in various establishments such as restaurants, cafeterias, and catering services. They are responsible for managing staff, ensuring food safety and quality, coordinating operations, and maintaining customer satisfaction.

children.name: Supervisors of Food Preparation and Serving Workers
children.description: Direct and coordinate activities of workers engaged in preparing and serving food. Schedule shifts, ensure quality standards, and handle customer complaints.

children.name: Chefs and Head Cooks
children.description: Direct and may participate in the preparation, seasoning, and cooking of salads, soups, fish, meats, vegetables, desserts, or other foods. May plan and price menu items, order supplies, and keep records and accounts.

children.name: First-Line Supervisors of Food Preparation and Serving Workers
children.description: Directly supervise and coordinate activities of workers engaged in preparing and serving food.

children.name: Cooks and Food Preparation Workers
children.description: Cooks and Food Preparation Workers are responsible for preparing ingredients, cooking meals, following recipes, and ensuring food safety and quality. They work under the guidance of chefs, supervisors, or kitchen managers, and their tasks may include chopping vegetables, seasoning dishes, operating cooking equipment, and maintaining cleanliness in the kitchen area.

children.name: Cooks
children.description: Prepare meals according to recipes and customer requests in restaurants or other food establishments. Monitor food quality, safety, and sanitation.

children.name: Cooks, Fast Food
children.description: Prepare and cook food in a fast food restaurant with a limited menu. Duties of these cooks are limited to preparation of a few basic items and normally involve operating large-volume single-purpose cooking equipment.

children.name: Cooks, Institution and Cafeteria
children.description: Prepare and cook large quantities of food for institutions, such as schools, hospitals, or cafeterias.

children.name: Cooks, Private Household
children.description: Prepare meals in private homes. Includes personal chefs.

children.name: Cooks, Restaurant
children.description: Prepare, season, and cook dishes such as soups, meats, vegetables, or desserts in restaurants. May order supplies, keep records and accounts, price items on menu, or plan menu.

children.name: Cooks, Short Order
children.description: Prepare and cook to order a variety of foods that require only a short preparation time. May take orders from customers and serve patrons at counters or tables.

children.name: Cooks, All Other
children.description: All cooks not listed separately.

children.name: Food Preparation Workers
children.description: Perform basic cooking tasks, such as chopping ingredients and preparing cold foods. Maintain kitchen cleanliness and adhere to food safety standards.

children.name: Food Preparation Workers
children.description: Perform a variety of food preparation duties other than cooking, such as preparing cold foods and shellfish, slicing meat, and brewing coffee or tea.

children.name: Food and Beverage Serving Workers
children.description: Food and Beverage Serving Workers encompass a range of positions in the food service industry, including waiters, waitresses, bartenders, hosts/hostesses, and counter attendants. They work in restaurants, bars, cafes, hotels, and other dining establishments. Their responsibilities include taking orders, serving food and beverages, ensuring customer satisfaction, and maintaining a clean and welcoming dining environment.

children.name: Bartenders
children.description: Mix and serve alcoholic and nonalcoholic beverages to patrons. May collect payments, manage bar inventory, and maintain cleanliness.

children.name: Bartenders
children.description: Mix and serve drinks to patrons, directly or through waitstaff.

children.name: Fast Food and Counter Workers
children.description: Serve food and beverages, often at fast-food or self-service establishments. Take orders, process payments, and handle simple meal assembly.

children.name: Combined Food Preparation and Serving Workers, Including Fast Food
children.description: Perform duties which combine preparing and serving food and nonalcoholic beverages.

children.name: Counter Attendants, Cafeteria, Food Concession, and Coffee Shop
children.description: Serve food to diners at counter or from a steam table.

children.name: Baristas
children.description: Prepare or serve specialty coffee or other beverages. Serve food such as baked goods or sandwiches to patrons.

children.name: Waiters and Waitresses
children.description: Take orders and serve food and beverages to patrons. Provide menu information, address customer needs, and handle payments.

children.name: Waiters and Waitresses
children.description: Take orders and serve food and beverages to patrons at tables in dining establishment.

children.name: Food Servers, Nonrestaurant
children.description: Serve food at locations such as hospitals, hotels, and offices that do not operate as traditional restaurants.

children.name: Food Servers, Nonrestaurant
children.description: Serve food to individuals outside of a restaurant environment, such as in hotel rooms, hospital rooms, residential care facilities, or cars.

children.name: Other Food Preparation and Serving Related Workers
children.description: Other Food Preparation and Serving Related Workers assist in the preparation and serving of food and beverages in various dining establishments such as restaurants, cafeterias, and fast food outlets. They may be responsible for tasks like clearing tables, restocking supplies, operating cash registers, and cleaning kitchen or dining areas.

children.name: Dining Room and Cafeteria Attendants and Bartender Helpers
children.description: Facilitate the dining experience by cleaning tables, restocking supplies, and supporting waitstaff or bartenders.

children.name: Dining Room and Cafeteria Attendants and Bartender Helpers
children.description: Facilitate food service. Clean tables; remove dirty dishes; replace soiled table linens; set tables; replenish supply of clean linens, silverware, glassware, and dishes; supply service bar with food; and serve items such as water, condiments, and coffee to patrons.

children.name: Dishwashers
children.description: Clean dishes, kitchen utensils, and work areas. May also store clean items in designated areas and remove trash.

children.name: Dishwashers
children.description: Clean dishes, kitchen, food preparation equipment, or utensils.

children.name: Hosts and Hostesses, Restaurant, Lounge, and Coffee Shop
children.description: Greet guests, manage waitlists, guide patrons to their seats, and maintain an organized seating chart.

children.name: Hosts and Hostesses, Restaurant, Lounge, and Coffee Shop
children.description: Welcome patrons, seat them at tables or in lounge, and help ensure quality of facilities and service.

children.name: Miscellaneous Food Preparation and Serving Related Workers
children.description: Perform a variety of food service tasks not classified under other categories, such as delivering room service or assisting with catering events.

children.name: Food Preparation and Serving Related Workers, All Other
children.description: All food preparation and serving related workers not listed separately.

name: Building and Grounds Cleaning and Maintenance Occupations
description: Encompasses custodial and housekeeping roles maintaining interior and exterior spaces. Workers clean, repair, and manage areas such as offices, hotels, or grounds, ensuring a safe and sanitary environment.

children.name: Supervisors of Building and Grounds Cleaning and Maintenance Workers
children.description: Supervisors of Building and Grounds Cleaning and Maintenance Workers are responsible for coordinating and managing the work of cleaning and maintenance staff. They assign tasks, ensure compliance with safety standards, inspect work quality, and may handle administrative duties related to scheduling, budgeting, and inventory management.

children.name: First-Line Supervisors of Building and Grounds Cleaning and Maintenance Workers
children.description: Oversee and coordinate janitorial or maintenance personnel. Schedule work shifts, inspect facilities, and ensure safety and cleanliness standards.

children.name: First-Line Supervisors of Housekeeping and Janitorial Workers
children.description: Directly supervise and coordinate work activities of cleaning personnel in hotels, hospitals, offices, and other establishments.

children.name: First-Line Supervisors of Landscaping, Lawn Service, and Groundskeeping Workers
children.description: Directly supervise and coordinate activities of workers engaged in landscaping or groundskeeping activities. Work may involve reviewing contracts to ascertain service, machine, and workforce requirements; answering inquiries from potential customers regarding methods, material, and price ranges; and preparing estimates according to labor, material, and machine costs.

children.name: Building Cleaning and Pest Control Workers
children.description: Building Cleaning and Pest Control Workers perform tasks related to cleaning and maintaining buildings, such as janitorial work, custodial services, and pest control. Their responsibilities may include sweeping, mopping, vacuuming, waste removal, disinfecting surfaces, and implementing pest control measures.

children.name: Building Cleaning Workers
children.description: Clean buildings or private residences. Duties may include mopping, vacuuming, trash disposal, and sanitizing surfaces.

children.name: Janitors and Cleaners, Except Maids and Housekeeping Cleaners
children.description: Keep buildings in clean and orderly condition. Perform heavy cleaning duties, such as cleaning floors, shampooing rugs, washing walls and glass, and removing rubbish. Duties may include tending furnace and boiler, performing routine maintenance activities, notifying management of need for repairs, and cleaning snow or debris from sidewalk.

children.name: Maids and Housekeeping Cleaners
children.description: Perform any combination of light cleaning duties to maintain private households or commercial establishments, such as hotels and hospitals, in a clean and orderly manner. Duties may include making beds, replenishing linens, cleaning rooms and halls, and vacuuming.

children.name: Building Cleaning Workers, All Other
children.description: All building cleaning workers not listed separately.

children.name: Pest Control Workers
children.description: Identify and control pests using chemicals, traps, or natural solutions. Inspect buildings for infestation and recommend prevention measures.

children.name: Pest Control Workers
children.description: Apply or release chemical solutions or toxic gases and set traps to kill or remove pests and vermin that infest buildings and surrounding areas.

children.name: Grounds Maintenance Workers
children.description: Grounds Maintenance Workers perform tasks related to landscaping, lawn care, planting, pruning, irrigation, and maintenance of outdoor areas. They may also operate machinery and equipment, such as mowers, trimmers, and power tools.

children.name: Grounds Maintenance Workers
children.description: Maintain outdoor areas, mow lawns, plant and trim vegetation, clear debris, and keep landscapes looking their best.

children.name: Landscaping and Groundskeeping Workers
children.description: Landscape or maintain grounds of property using hand or power tools or equipment. Workers typically perform a variety of tasks, which may include any combination of the following: sod laying, mowing, trimming, planting, watering, fertilizing, digging, raking, sprinkler installation, and installation of mortarless segmental concrete masonry wall units.

children.name: Pesticide Handlers, Sprayers, and Applicators, Vegetation
children.description: Mix or apply pesticides, herbicides, fungicides, or insecticides through sprays, dusts, vapors, soil incorporation, or chemical application on trees, shrubs, lawns, or crops. Usually requires specific training and state or federal certification.

children.name: Tree Trimmers and Pruners
children.description: Using sophisticated climbing and rigging techniques, cut away dead or excess branches from trees or shrubs to maintain right-of-way for roads, sidewalks, or utilities, or to improve appearance, health, and value of tree. Prune or treat trees or shrubs using handsaws, hand pruners, clippers, and power pruners. Works off the ground in the tree canopy and may use truck-mounted lifts.

children.name: Grounds Maintenance Workers, All Other
children.description: All grounds maintenance workers not listed separately.

name: Personal Care and Service Occupations
description: Provides personal services to clients, such as childcare, fitness instruction, or beauty treatments. Includes hairdressers, childcare workers, fitness trainers, and similar service providers.

children.name: Supervisors of Personal Care and Service Workers
children.description: Supervisors of Personal Care and Service Workers oversee and coordinate the activities of workers providing personal care services to individuals in various settings, such as home care, residential facilities, or healthcare institutions. They may supervise workers such as personal care aides, home health aides, and childcare workers, ensuring the quality of care and adherence to regulations.

children.name: First-Line Supervisors of Gaming Workers
children.description: Supervise and coordinate the activities of gaming service employees, such as dealers and slot supervisors. Ensure compliance with gaming regulations and maintain customer satisfaction.

children.name: Gaming Supervisors
children.description: Supervise and coordinate activities of workers in assigned gaming areas. Circulate among tables and observe operations. Ensure that stations and games are covered for each shift. May explain and interpret operating rules of house to patrons. May plan and organize activities and services for guests in hotels/casinos. May address service complaints.

children.name: Slot Supervisors
children.description: Supervise and coordinate activities of slot department workers to provide service to patrons. Handle and settle complaints of players. Verify and pay off jackpots. Reset slot machines after payoffs. Make repairs or adjustments to slot machines or recommend removal of slot machines for repair. Report hazards and enforce safety rules.

children.name: First-Line Supervisors of Personal Service Workers
children.description: Direct workers providing personal services (e.g., spa, salon, or childcare). Monitor operations, train staff, and handle customer complaints or special requests.

children.name: First-Line Supervisors of Personal Service Workers
children.description: Directly supervise and coordinate activities of personal service workers, such as flight attendants, hairdressers, or caddies.

children.name: Spa Managers
children.description: Plan, direct, or coordinate activities of a spa facility. Coordinate programs, schedule and direct staff, and oversee financial activities.

children.name: Animal Care and Service Workers
children.description: Animal Care and Service Workers provide care, support, and services to animals in a variety of settings, such as animal shelters, zoos, veterinary clinics, and pet care facilities. They may be involved in tasks such as feeding, grooming, training, monitoring health, and ensuring the overall well-being of animals.

children.name: Animal Trainers
children.description: Train animals for riding, harness, security, performance, or obedience, or for assisting persons with disabilities. Accustom animals to human voice and contact, and condition animals to respond to commands. Train animals according to prescribed standards for show or competition. May train animals to carry pack loads or work as part of pack team.

children.name: Animal Caretakers
children.description: Feed, water, groom, bathe, exercise, or otherwise provide care to promote and maintain the well-being of pets and other animals that are not raised for consumption, such as dogs, cats, race horses, ornamental fish or birds, zoo animals, and mice. Work in settings such as kennels, animal shelters, zoos, circuses, and aquariums. May keep records of feedings, treatments, and animals received or discharged. May clean, disinfect, and repair cages, pens, or fish tanks.

children.name: Entertainment Attendants and Related Workers
children.description: This category includes various occupations involved in providing entertainment services and assisting with the operations of entertainment venues. It encompasses workers who support and facilitate the smooth running of events, performances, amusement parks, and other entertainment establishments.

children.name: Gaming Services Workers
children.description: Operate gambling tables, deal cards, or handle slot machines in casinos. Assist patrons, enforce gaming rules, and handle financial transactions.

children.name: Gambling Dealers
children.description: Operate table games. Stand or sit behind table and operate games of chance by dispensing the appropriate number of cards or blocks to players, or operating other gambling equipment. Distribute winnings or collect players' money or chips. May compare the house's hand against players' hands.

children.name: Gambling and Sports Book Writers and Runners
children.description: Post information enabling patrons to wager on various races and sporting events. Assist in the operation of games such as keno and bingo. May operate random number-generating equipment and announce the numbers for patrons. Receive, verify, and record patrons' wagers. Scan and process winning tickets presented by patrons and pay out winnings for those wagers.

children.name: Gambling Service Workers, All Other
children.description: All gambling service workers not listed separately.

children.name: Motion Picture Projectionists
children.description: Operate film or digital projectors, manage reels or digital files, adjust sound and picture quality, and ensure smooth theatrical screenings.

children.name: Motion Picture Projectionists
children.description: Set up and operate motion picture projection and related sound reproduction equipment.

children.name: Ushers, Lobby Attendants, and Ticket Takers
children.description: Greet patrons, take tickets, and direct attendees to seats. May distribute programs, answer questions, or help maintain order before and after events.

children.name: Ushers, Lobby Attendants, and Ticket Takers
children.description: Assist patrons at entertainment events by performing duties, such as collecting admission tickets and passes from patrons, assisting in finding seats, searching for lost articles, and helping patrons locate such facilities as restrooms and telephones.

children.name: Miscellaneous Entertainment Attendants and Related Workers
children.description: Perform event-related tasks not listed under other occupations, such as carnival ride operators, costume characters, or escape room attendants.

children.name: Amusement and Recreation Attendants
children.description: Perform a variety of attending duties at amusement or recreation facility. May schedule use of recreation facilities, maintain and provide equipment to participants of sporting events or recreational pursuits, or operate amusement concessions and rides.

children.name: Costume Attendants
children.description: Select, fit, and take care of costumes for cast members, and aid entertainers. May assist with multiple costume changes during performances.

children.name: Locker Room, Coatroom, and Dressing Room Attendants
children.description: Provide personal items to patrons or customers in locker rooms, dressing rooms, or coatrooms.

children.name: Entertainment Attendants and Related Workers, All Other
children.description: All entertainment attendants and related workers not listed separately.

children.name: Funeral Service Workers
children.description: Funeral Service Workers, includes various professionals involved in providing funeral services and supporting bereaved families. This category typically encompasses funeral directors, morticians, embalmers, and funeral attendants. Funeral service workers are responsible for assisting families in making funeral arrangements, preparing bodies for burial or cremation, organizing memorial services, and providing emotional support to grieving individuals.

children.name: Embalmers
children.description: Prepare bodies for burial or cremation by cleansing and preserving remains. May reconstruct disfigured bodies to restore natural appearance.

children.name: Embalmers
children.description: Prepare bodies for interment in conformity with legal requirements.

children.name: Funeral Attendants
children.description: Assist funeral directors in various tasks, including setting up viewing rooms, arranging flowers, and transporting caskets.

children.name: Funeral Attendants
children.description: Perform a variety of tasks during funeral, such as placing casket in parlor or chapel prior to service, arranging floral offerings or lights around casket, directing or escorting mourners, closing casket, and issuing and storing funeral equipment.

children.name: Morticians, Undertakers, and Funeral Directors
children.description: Coordinate all aspects of funeral services, including embalming, meeting with families to plan services, and handling administrative duties such as records and permits.

children.name: Morticians, Undertakers, and Funeral Arrangers
children.description: Perform various tasks to arrange and direct individual funeral services, such as coordinating transportation of body to mortuary, interviewing family or other authorized person to arrange details, selecting pallbearers, aiding with the selection of officials for religious rites, and providing transportation for mourners.

children.name: Personal Appearance Workers
children.description: The category of Personal Appearance Workers typically includes occupations such as hairstylists, barbers, makeup artists, skincare specialists, and nail technicians. These professionals provide personal grooming services to clients, helping them enhance their appearance.

children.name: Barbers, Hairdressers, Hairstylists and Cosmetologists
children.description: Provide hair, makeup, and related beauty services. Cut, style, and color hair; recommend products; and maintain sanitary work areas.

children.name: Barbers
children.description: Provide barbering services, such as cutting, trimming, shampooing, and styling hair; trimming beards; or giving shaves.

children.name: Hairdressers, Hairstylists, and Cosmetologists
children.description: Provide beauty services, such as cutting, coloring, and styling hair, and massaging and treating scalp. May shampoo hair, apply makeup, dress wigs, remove hair, and provide nail and skincare services.

children.name: Miscellaneous Personal Appearance Workers
children.description: Offer specialized beauty or grooming services not classified under standard roles, potentially including skincare, nail, or spa treatments.

children.name: Makeup Artists, Theatrical and Performance
children.description: Apply makeup to performers to reflect period, setting, and situation of their role.

children.name: Manicurists and Pedicurists
children.description: Clean and shape customers' fingernails and toenails. May polish or decorate nails.

children.name: Shampooers
children.description: Shampoo and rinse customers' hair.

children.name: Skincare Specialists
children.description: Provide skincare treatments to face and body to enhance an individual's appearance. Includes electrologists and laser hair removal specialists.

children.name: Baggage Porters, Bellhops, and Concierges
children.description: The category of Baggage Porters, Bellhops, and Concierges includes occupations that are involved in providing assistance and services to guests in hotels, resorts, and other hospitality establishments.

children.name: Baggage Porters, Bellhops, and Concierges
children.description: Assist hotel, resort, or travel guests by carrying luggage, providing information, making reservations, and handling other customer-service tasks.

children.name: Baggage Porters and Bellhops
children.description: Handle baggage for travelers at transportation terminals or for guests at hotels or similar establishments.

children.name: Concierges
children.description: Assist patrons at hotel, apartment, or office building with personal services. May take messages; arrange or give advice on transportation, business services, or entertainment; or monitor guest requests for housekeeping and maintenance.

children.name: Tour and Travel Guides
children.description: Tour and Travel Guides are professionals who provide guided tours and travel services to individuals or groups visiting various destinations. They provide information about the history, culture, landmarks, and other relevant details of the places being visited.

children.name: Tour and Travel Guides
children.description: Escort individuals or groups on sightseeing tours or through places of interest. Provide historical, cultural, or practical information to enhance the visitor experience.

children.name: Tour Guides and Escorts
children.description: Escort individuals or groups on sightseeing tours or through places of interest, such as industrial establishments, public buildings, and art galleries.

children.name: Travel Guides
children.description: Plan, organize, and conduct long-distance travel, tours, and expeditions for individuals and groups.

children.name: Other Personal Care and Service Workers
children.description: The category of 39-9000 Other Personal Care and Service Workers includes a diverse range of occupations that provide personal care and support services to individuals in various settings. These workers typically assist clients with their daily living activities, promote their well-being, and provide companionship. The category encompasses a wide array of roles, including personal care aides, residential advisors, child and youth workers, recreation workers, and personal trainers. These workers often have direct and regular contact with clients, offering assistance and support in areas such as grooming, hygiene, mobility, meal preparation, and household tasks.

children.name: Childcare Workers
children.description: Attend to children’s basic needs, plan activities, and monitor their safety. May help with homework and implement schedules for meals or playtime.

children.name: Childcare Workers
children.description: Attend to children at schools, businesses, private households, and childcare institutions. Perform a variety of tasks, such as dressing, feeding, bathing, and overseeing play.

children.name: Nannies
children.description: Care for children in private households and provide support and expertise to parents in satisfying children's physical, emotional, intellectual, and social needs. Duties may include meal planning and preparation, laundry and clothing care, organization of play activities and outings, discipline, intellectual stimulation, language activities, and transportation.

children.name: Personal Care Aides
children.description: Assist individuals with daily living activities at home or in care facilities. Duties often include housekeeping, meal preparation, and companionship.

children.name: Personal Care Aides
children.description: Assist the elderly, convalescents, or persons with disabilities with daily living activities at the person's home or in a care facility. Duties performed at a place of residence may include keeping house (making beds, doing laundry, washing dishes) and preparing meals. May provide assistance at non-residential care facilities. May advise families, the elderly, convalescents, and persons with disabilities regarding such things as nutrition, cleanliness, and household activities.

children.name: Recreation and Fitness Workers
children.description: Lead leisure or fitness activities in settings such as parks, recreation facilities, gyms, or community centers. Develop exercise programs and motivate participants.

children.name: Exercise Trainers and Group Fitness Instructors
children.description: Instruct or coach groups or individuals in exercise activities for the primary purpose of personal fitness. Demonstrate techniques and form, observe participants, and explain to them corrective measures necessary to improve their skills. Develop and implement individualized approaches to exercise.

children.name: Recreation Workers
children.description: Conduct recreation activities with groups in public, private, or volunteer agencies or recreation facilities. Organize and promote activities, such as arts and crafts, sports, games, music, dramatics, social recreation, camping, and hobbies, taking into account the needs and interests of individual members.

children.name: Residential Advisors
children.description: Supervise students or residents in group housing facilities, enforcing rules and coordinating social or educational activities.

children.name: Residential Advisors
children.description: Coordinate activities in resident facilities in secondary school and college dormitories, group homes, or similar establishments. Order supplies and determine need for maintenance, repairs, and furnishings. May maintain household records and assign rooms. May assist residents with problem solving or refer them to counseling resources.

children.name: Miscellaneous Personal Care and Service Workers
children.description: Deliver personal care or support services not covered by other roles, e.g., valet parking, spa attendants, or personal organizers.

children.name: Personal Care and Service Workers, All Other
children.description: All personal care and service workers not listed separately.

name: Sales and Related Occupations
description: Focuses on selling goods or services directly to consumers or other businesses. Occupations range from retail sales associates to wholesale sales representatives, often involving customer service and product promotion.

children.name: Supervisors of Sales Workers
children.description: Supervisors of Sales Workers are responsible for overseeing and managing the activities of sales teams within various industries. They play a crucial role in providing guidance, training, and support to sales personnel, monitoring sales performance, and implementing strategies to achieve sales targets.

children.name: First-Line Supervisors of Sales Workers
children.description: Direct and coordinate sales staff activities. Assign tasks, train employees, set sales goals, and monitor performance.

children.name: First-Line Supervisors of Retail Sales Workers
children.description: Directly supervise and coordinate activities of retail sales workers in an establishment or department. Duties may include management functions, such as purchasing, budgeting, accounting, and personnel work, in addition to supervisory duties.

children.name: First-Line Supervisors of Non-Retail Sales Workers
children.description: Directly supervise and coordinate activities of sales workers other than retail sales workers. May perform duties such as budgeting, accounting, and personnel work, in addition to supervisory duties.

children.name: Retail Sales Workers
children.description: Retail Sales Workers are individuals who work in various retail settings, such as department stores, boutiques, and online marketplaces. They are responsible for assisting customers, providing product information, processing sales transactions, and ensuring a positive shopping experience.

children.name: Cashiers
children.description: Handle customer purchases, operate cash registers or other point-of-sale equipment, process payments, and may bag or wrap merchandise.

children.name: Cashiers
children.description: Receive and disburse money in establishments other than financial institutions. May use electronic scanners, cash registers, or related equipment. May process credit or debit card transactions and validate checks.

children.name: Gambling Change Persons and Booth Cashiers
children.description: Exchange coins, tokens, and chips for patrons' money. May issue payoffs and obtain customer's signature on receipt. May operate a booth in the slot machine area and furnish change persons with money bank at the start of the shift, or count and audit money in drawers.

children.name: Counter and Rental Clerks and Parts Salespersons
children.description: Assist customers in finding products, including rentals or parts. Provide product information, manage transactions, and maintain stock.

children.name: Counter and Rental Clerks
children.description: Receive orders, generally in person, for repairs, rentals, and services. May describe available options, compute cost, and accept payment.

children.name: Parts Salespersons
children.description: Sell spare and replacement parts and equipment in repair shop or parts store.

children.name: Retail Salespersons
children.description: Sell merchandise such as clothing, furniture, or electronics. Greet customers, explain features, and ring up purchases.

children.name: Retail Salespersons
children.description: Sell merchandise, such as furniture, motor vehicles, appliances, or apparel to consumers.

children.name: Sales Representatives, Services
children.description: Sales Representatives, Services are professionals who are responsible for selling various services to businesses and individuals. They may work in industries such as advertising, financial services, consulting, and technology. These sales representatives build relationships with clients, identify their needs, and present suitable service solutions.

children.name: Advertising Sales Agents
children.description: Sell or solicit advertising to businesses and individuals. Maintain client accounts, develop ad campaigns, and achieve sales targets.

children.name: Advertising Sales Agents
children.description: Sell or solicit advertising space, time, or media in publications, signage, TV, radio, or Internet establishments or public spaces.

children.name: Insurance Sales Agents
children.description: Contact potential clients, explain various insurance policies, and help customers choose plans that meet their needs.

children.name: Insurance Sales Agents
children.description: Sell life, property, casualty, health, automotive, or other types of insurance. May refer clients to independent brokers, work as an independent broker, or be employed by an insurance company.

children.name: Securities, Commodities, and Financial Services Sales Agents
children.description: Buy and sell stocks, bonds, or other financial instruments. Advise clients on investment strategies and market conditions.

children.name: Securities, Commodities, and Financial Services Sales Agents
children.description: Buy and sell securities or commodities in investment and trading firms, or provide financial services to businesses and individuals. May advise customers about stocks, bonds, mutual funds, commodities, and market conditions.

children.name: Sales Agents, Securities and Commodities
children.description: Buy and sell securities in investment and trading firms and develop and implement financial plans for individuals, businesses, and organizations.

children.name: Sales Agents, Financial Services
children.description: Sell financial services, such as loan, tax, and securities counseling to customers of financial institutions and business establishments.

children.name: Securities and Commodities Traders
children.description: Buy and sell securities and commodities to transfer debt, capital, or risk. Establish and negotiate unit prices and terms of sale.

children.name: Travel Agents
children.description: Plan and sell transportation, lodging, and entertainment activities for clients. Offer advice on destinations, itineraries, and travel costs.

children.name: Travel Agents
children.description: Plan and sell transportation and accommodations for customers. Determine destination, modes of transportation, travel dates, costs, and accommodations required. May also describe, plan, and arrange itineraries and sell tour packages. May assist in resolving clients' travel problems.

children.name: Miscellaneous Sales Representatives, Services
children.description: Sell services (e.g., digital marketing, consulting) not categorized under other sales roles. May create client proposals and follow up on leads.

children.name: Sales Representatives, Services, All Other
children.description: All services sales representatives not listed separately.

children.name: Energy Brokers
children.description: Buy or sell energy products on the behalf of residential or commercial customers or utilities. Negotiate and oversee contracts for energy sales.

children.name: Sales Representatives, Wholesale and Manufacturing
children.description: Sales Representatives, Wholesale and Manufacturing are professionals who are responsible for selling goods and products to businesses (wholesale) or retailers (manufacturing). They work in various industries such as manufacturing, wholesale trade, and distribution. These sales representatives build relationships with clients, showcase product features, negotiate contracts, and close sales deals.

children.name: Sales Representatives, Wholesale and Manufacturing
children.description: Sell goods for wholesalers or manufacturers to businesses, government agencies, or other organizations. Negotiate prices, explain product features, and maintain customer relationships.

children.name: Sales Representatives, Wholesale and Manufacturing, Technical and Scientific Products
children.description: Sell goods for wholesalers or manufacturers where technical or scientific knowledge is required in such areas as biology, engineering, chemistry, and electronics, normally obtained from at least 2 years of postsecondary education.

children.name: Solar Sales Representatives and Assessors
children.description: Contact new or existing customers to determine their solar equipment needs, suggest systems or equipment, or estimate costs.

children.name: Sales Representatives, Wholesale and Manufacturing, Except Technical and Scientific Products
children.description: Sell goods for wholesalers or manufacturers to businesses or groups of individuals. Work requires substantial knowledge of items sold.

children.name: Other Sales and Related Workers
children.description: Other Sales and Related Workers include a diverse range of occupations that are involved in sales and related activities, but are not classified under the specific subcategories within the sales occupation group. These occupations may include sales support roles, retail sales support, sales coordinators, sales assistants, and other sales-related positions.

children.name: Models, Demonstrators, and Product Promoters
children.description: Display and promote products at events or retail locations. Interact with customers, answer questions, and encourage product sales.

children.name: Demonstrators and Product Promoters
children.description: Demonstrate merchandise and answer questions for the purpose of creating public interest in buying the product. May sell demonstrated merchandise.

children.name: Models
children.description: Model garments or other apparel and accessories for prospective buyers at fashion shows, private showings, or retail establishments. May pose for photos to be used in magazines or advertisements. May pose as subject for paintings, sculptures, and other types of artistic expression.

children.name: Real Estate Brokers and Sales Agents
children.description: Assist clients in buying, selling, and renting properties. Conduct property showings, prepare contracts, and negotiate terms of sale or lease.

children.name: Real Estate Brokers
children.description: Operate real estate office, or work for commercial real estate firm, overseeing real estate transactions. Other duties usually include selling real estate or renting properties and arranging loans.

children.name: Real Estate Sales Agents
children.description: Rent, buy, or sell property for clients. Perform duties such as study property listings, interview prospective clients, accompany clients to property site, discuss conditions of sale, and draw up real estate contracts. Includes agents who represent buyer.

children.name: Sales Engineers
children.description: Sell complex scientific or technical products to businesses, leveraging engineering or technical knowledge to demonstrate product benefits and functionalities.

children.name: Sales Engineers
children.description: Sell business goods or services, the selling of which requires a technical background equivalent to a baccalaureate degree in engineering.

children.name: Telemarketers
children.description: Solicit sales or donations over the phone. Follow scripts, answer questions, record customer details, and process payment information.

children.name: Telemarketers
children.description: Solicit donations or orders for goods or services over the telephone.

children.name: Miscellaneous Sales and Related Workers
children.description: Perform sales-related duties not classified under other specific occupations, such as door-to-door sales or demonstration merchandising.

children.name: Door-to-Door Sales Workers, News and Street Vendors, and Related Workers
children.description: Sell goods or services door-to-door or on the street.

children.name: Sales and Related Workers, All Other
children.description: All sales and related workers not listed separately.

children.name: Supervisors of Office and Administrative Support Workers
children.description: Supervisors of Office and Administrative Support Workers are responsible for overseeing and managing the daily operations of administrative support staff within an organization. They provide guidance, assign tasks, ensure efficient workflow, and may also be involved in evaluating employee performance and training.

children.name: First-Line Supervisors of Office and Administrative Support Workers
children.description: Oversee the work of office and administrative support staff. Assign tasks, train employees, ensure compliance with policies, and manage workflow.

children.name: First-Line Supervisors of Office and Administrative Support Workers
children.description: Directly supervise and coordinate the activities of clerical and administrative support workers.

children.name: Communications Equipment Operators
children.description: Communications Equipment Operators typically work in industries such as telecommunications, broadcasting, or emergency services. They operate and monitor various communication equipment, such as switchboards, radio systems, or dispatch consoles. Their responsibilities may include answering and transferring calls, transmitting messages, monitoring communication channels, and providing support during emergencies.

children.name: Switchboard Operators, Including Answering Service
children.description: Operate telephone switchboards, route calls, provide information, and record messages. May assist with clerical tasks.

children.name: Switchboard Operators, Including Answering Service
children.description: Operate telephone business systems equipment or switchboards to relay incoming, outgoing, and interoffice calls. May supply information to callers and record messages.

children.name: Telephone Operators
children.description: Help callers with directory assistance, handle emergency calls, or support specialized telephone systems.

children.name: Telephone Operators
children.description: Provide information by accessing alphabetical, geographical, or other directories. Assist customers with special billing requests, such as charges to a third party and credits or refunds for incorrectly dialed numbers or bad connections. May handle emergency calls and assist children or people with physical disabilities to make telephone calls.

children.name: Miscellaneous Communications Equipment Operators
children.description: Operate or maintain communications devices not included in other categories, possibly handling specialized telecommunication systems.

children.name: Communications Equipment Operators, All Other
children.description: All communications equipment operators not listed separately.

children.name: Financial Clerks
children.description: Financial Clerks perform various clerical and administrative tasks related to financial transactions and records. They work in financial institutions, insurance companies, and other businesses where financial activities are conducted. Some common occupations within this category include billing and posting clerks, payroll clerks, and procurement clerks.

children.name: Bill and Account Collectors
children.description: Locate and notify customers of overdue payments, negotiate payment arrangements, and maintain financial records.

children.name: Bill and Account Collectors
children.description: Locate and notify customers of delinquent accounts by mail, telephone, or personal visit to solicit payment. Duties include receiving payment and posting amount to customer's account, preparing statements to credit department if customer fails to respond, initiating repossession proceedings or service disconnection, and keeping records of collection and status of accounts.

children.name: Billing and Posting Clerks
children.description: Compile and record bills for services rendered or goods sold. Verify accuracy and post transactions to customer accounts.

children.name: Billing and Posting Clerks
children.description: Compile, compute, and record billing, accounting, statistical, and other numerical data for billing purposes. Prepare billing invoices for services rendered or for delivery or shipment of goods.

children.name: Statement Clerks
children.description: Prepare and distribute bank statements to customers, answer inquiries, and reconcile discrepancies in records and accounts.

children.name: Billing, Cost, and Rate Clerks
children.description: Compile data, compute fees and charges, and prepare invoices for billing purposes. Duties include computing costs and calculating rates for goods, services, and shipment of goods; posting data; and keeping other relevant records. May involve use of computer or typewriter, calculator, and adding and bookkeeping machines.

children.name: Bookkeeping, Accounting, and Auditing Clerks
children.description: Compute, classify, and record financial data. Maintain financial records, verify transactions, and reconcile accounts.

children.name: Bookkeeping, Accounting, and Auditing Clerks
children.description: Compute, classify, and record numerical data to keep financial records complete. Perform any combination of routine calculating, posting, and verifying duties to obtain primary financial data for use in maintaining accounting records. May also check the accuracy of figures, calculations, and postings pertaining to business transactions recorded by other workers.

children.name: Gaming Cage Workers
children.description: Handle cash transactions in casinos, exchange tokens or chips for cash, and balance cash drawers and transactions.

children.name: Gambling Cage Workers
children.description: In a gambling establishment, conduct financial transactions for patrons. Accept patron's credit application and verify credit references to provide check-cashing authorization or to establish house credit accounts. May reconcile daily summaries of transactions to balance books. May sell gambling chips, tokens, or tickets to patrons, or to other workers for resale to patrons. May convert gambling chips, tokens, or tickets to currency upon patron's request. May use a cash register or computer to record transaction.

children.name: Payroll and Timekeeping Clerks
children.description: Compile and record employee time data. Calculate wages, deductions, and ensure employees are paid accurately and on time.

children.name: Payroll and Timekeeping Clerks
children.description: Compile and record employee time and payroll data. May compute employees' time worked, production, and commission. May compute and post wages and deductions, or prepare paychecks.

children.name: Procurement Clerks
children.description: Compile information and records to draw up purchase orders for procurement of materials and services. Track deliveries and maintain vendor data.

children.name: Procurement Clerks
children.description: Compile information and records to draw up purchase orders for procurement of materials and services.

children.name: Tellers
children.description: Receive and pay out money at a financial institution. Track transactions, record deposits, handle withdrawals, and maintain account balances.

children.name: Tellers
children.description: Receive and pay out money. Keep records of money and negotiable instruments involved in a financial institution's various transactions.

children.name: Miscellaneous Financial Clerks
children.description: Perform financial tasks not categorized under other titles, possibly including specialized billing or claims.

children.name: Financial Clerks, All Other
children.description: All financial clerks not listed separately.

children.name: Information and Record Clerks
children.description: Information and Record Clerks are responsible for maintaining and organizing information, records, and documents in various settings such as libraries, archives, hospitals, and government agencies. They may perform tasks such as data entry, recordkeeping, information retrieval, and assisting users in accessing information.

children.name: Brokerage Clerks
children.description: Assist in securities trading offices by recording and processing stock transactions, verifying trade details, and maintaining client records.

children.name: Brokerage Clerks
children.description: Perform duties related to the purchase, sale, or holding of securities. Duties include writing orders for stock purchases or sales, computing transfer taxes, verifying stock transactions, accepting and delivering securities, tracking stock price fluctuations, computing equity, distributing dividends, and keeping records of daily transactions and holdings.

children.name: Correspondence Clerks
children.description: Compose and respond to business correspondence. Review mail requests, direct inquiries, and file outgoing/incoming letters.

children.name: Correspondence Clerks
children.description: Compose letters or electronic correspondence in reply to requests for merchandise, damage claims, credit and other information, delinquent accounts, incorrect billings, or unsatisfactory services. Duties may include gathering data to formulate reply and preparing correspondence.

children.name: Court, Municipal, and License Clerks
children.description: Perform clerical duties in courts or government offices. Manage records, process licenses, file legal documents, and provide information to the public.

children.name: Court, Municipal, and License Clerks
children.description: Perform clerical duties for courts of law, municipalities, or governmental licensing agencies and bureaus. May prepare docket of cases to be called; secure information for judges and court; prepare draft agendas or bylaws for town or city council; answer official correspondence; keep fiscal records and accounts; issue licenses or permits; and record data, administer tests, or collect fees.

children.name: Court Clerks
children.description: Perform clerical duties in court of law; prepare docket of cases to be called; secure information for judges; and contact witnesses, attorneys, and litigants to obtain information for court.

children.name: Municipal Clerks
children.description: Draft agendas and bylaws for town or city council; record minutes of council meetings; answer official correspondence; keep fiscal records and accounts; and prepare reports on civic needs.

children.name: License Clerks
