children.description: Issue licenses or permits to qualified applicants. Obtain necessary information, record data, advise applicants on requirements, collect fees, and issue licenses. May conduct oral, written, visual, or performance testing.

children.name: Credit Authorizers, Checkers, and Clerks
children.description: Investigate credit history, verify financial data, and authorize credit limits for customers or businesses.

children.name: Credit Authorizers, Checkers, and Clerks
children.description: Authorize credit charges against customers' accounts. Investigate history and credit standing of individuals or business establishments applying for credit. May interview applicants to obtain personal and financial data, determine credit worthiness, process applications, and notify customers of acceptance or rejection of credit.

children.name: Credit Authorizers
children.description: Authorize credit charges against customers' accounts.

children.name: Credit Checkers
children.description: Investigate history and credit standing of individuals or business establishments applying for credit. Telephone or write to credit departments of business and service establishments to obtain information about applicant's credit standing.

children.name: Customer Service Representatives
children.description: Interact with customers, answer questions about products or services, process orders or returns, and handle complaints or billing issues.

children.name: Customer Service Representatives
children.description: Interact with customers to provide basic or scripted information in response to routine inquiries about products and services. May handle and resolve general complaints. Excludes individuals whose duties are primarily installation, sales, repair, and technical support.

children.name: Patient Representatives
children.description: Assist patients in obtaining services, understanding policies and making health care decisions.

children.name: Eligibility Interviewers, Government Programs
children.description: Determine eligibility for government aid, benefits, or programs by interviewing applicants, reviewing documentation, and updating records.

children.name: Eligibility Interviewers, Government Programs
children.description: Determine eligibility of persons applying to receive assistance from government programs and agency resources, such as welfare, unemployment benefits, social security, and public housing.

children.name: File Clerks
children.description: Maintain and organize paper and electronic records. Retrieve documents for staff, track file locations, and update records management systems.

children.name: File Clerks
children.description: File correspondence, cards, invoices, receipts, and other records in alphabetical or numerical order or according to the filing system used. Locate and remove material from file when requested.

children.name: Hotel, Motel, and Resort Desk Clerks
children.description: Greet and register guests, assign rooms, manage reservations, issue room keys, and process payments. Respond to customer service requests.

children.name: Hotel, Motel, and Resort Desk Clerks
children.description: Accommodate hotel, motel, and resort patrons by registering and assigning rooms to guests, issuing room keys or cards, transmitting and receiving messages, keeping records of occupied rooms and guests' accounts, making and confirming reservations, and presenting statements to and collecting payments from departing guests.

children.name: Interviewers, Except Eligibility and Loan
children.description: Ask questions to gather information, often for surveys, market research, or medical histories. Record responses and compile data.

children.name: Interviewers, Except Eligibility and Loan
children.description: Interview persons by telephone, mail, in person, or by other means for the purpose of completing forms, applications, or questionnaires. Ask specific questions, record answers, and assist persons with completing form. May sort, classify, and file forms.

children.name: Library Assistants, Clerical
children.description: Help librarians by organizing materials, shelving books, assisting patrons in locating resources, and performing other clerical duties.

children.name: Library Assistants, Clerical
children.description: Compile records, and sort, shelve, issue, and receive library materials such as books, electronic media, pictures, cards, slides and microfilm. Locate library materials for loan and replace material in shelving area, stacks, or files according to identification number and title. Register patrons to permit them to borrow books, periodicals, and other library materials.

children.name: Loan Interviewers and Clerks
children.description: Gather financial data from loan applicants, process applications, verify credit information, and prepare loan paperwork for review by loan officers.

children.name: Loan Interviewers and Clerks
children.description: Interview loan applicants to elicit information; investigate applicants' backgrounds and verify references; prepare loan request papers; and forward findings, reports, and documents to appraisal department. Review loan papers to ensure completeness, and complete transactions between loan establishment, borrowers, and sellers upon approval of loan.

children.name: New Accounts Clerks
children.description: Interview prospective banking customers, gather personal information, open accounts, and explain account services or policies.

children.name: New Accounts Clerks
children.description: Interview persons desiring to open accounts in financial institutions. Explain account services available to prospective customers and assist them in preparing applications.

children.name: Order Clerks
children.description: Receive and process incoming orders for goods or services. Verify order details, maintain logs, and coordinate shipping or fulfillment.

children.name: Order Clerks
children.description: Receive and process incoming orders for materials, merchandise, classified ads, or services such as repairs, installations, or rental of facilities. Generally receives orders via mail, phone, fax, or other electronic means. Duties include informing customers of receipt, prices, shipping dates, and delays; preparing contracts; and handling complaints.

children.name: Human Resources Assistants, Except Payroll and Timekeeping
children.description: Support HR departments by maintaining employee records, scheduling interviews, and processing paperwork related to hiring, performance, or termination.

children.name: Human Resources Assistants, Except Payroll and Timekeeping
children.description: Compile and keep personnel records. Record data for each employee, such as address, weekly earnings, absences, amount of sales or production, supervisory reports, and date of and reason for termination. May prepare reports for employment records, file employment records, or search employee files and furnish information to authorized persons.

children.name: Receptionists and Information Clerks
children.description: Receive and direct visitors, answer telephones, schedule appointments, and provide information about an organization’s services.

children.name: Receptionists and Information Clerks
children.description: Answer inquiries and provide information to the general public, customers, visitors, and other interested parties regarding activities conducted at establishment and location of departments, offices, and employees within the organization.

children.name: Reservation and Transportation Ticket Agents and Travel Clerks
children.description: Make and confirm reservations for transportation or lodging. May issue tickets, provide itinerary information, and assist travelers with changes.

children.name: Reservation and Transportation Ticket Agents and Travel Clerks
children.description: Make and confirm reservations for transportation or lodging, or sell transportation tickets. May check baggage and direct passengers to designated concourse, pier, or track; deliver tickets and contact individuals and groups to inform them of package tours; or provide tourists with travel or transportation information.

children.name: Miscellaneous Information and Record Clerks
children.description: Occupations involving records and information processing not included under other titles. May handle specialized data management, archival tasks, or administrative recordkeeping.

children.name: Information and Record Clerks, All Other
children.description: All information and record clerks not listed separately.

children.name: Material Recording, Scheduling, Dispatching, and Distributing Workers
children.description: Material Recording, Scheduling, Dispatching, and Distributing Workers are responsible for tracking, organizing, and coordinating the movement of goods, materials, and resources within various industries. They may perform tasks such as inventory control, order processing, scheduling, and logistics coordination.

children.name: Cargo and Freight Agents
children.description: Coordinate and track shipments of goods, arrange transportation, handle paperwork, and ensure timely delivery of cargo.

children.name: Cargo and Freight Agents
children.description: Expedite and route movement of incoming and outgoing cargo and freight shipments in airline, train, and trucking terminals and shipping docks. Take orders from customers and arrange pickup of freight and cargo for delivery to loading platform. Prepare and examine bills of lading to determine shipping charges and tariffs.

children.name: Freight Forwarders
children.description: Research rates, routings, or modes of transport for shipment of products. Maintain awareness of regulations affecting the international movement of cargo. Make arrangements for additional services, such as storage or inland transportation.

children.name: Couriers and Messengers
children.description: Transport documents or packages between offices or businesses. Plan routes, obtain signatures, and track deliveries.

children.name: Couriers and Messengers
children.description: Pick up and deliver messages, documents, packages, and other items between offices or departments within an establishment or directly to other business concerns, traveling by foot, bicycle, motorcycle, automobile, or public conveyance.

children.name: Dispatchers
children.description: Schedule and dispatch workers, work crews, or service vehicles for tasks including emergency response, shipping, or repairs. Maintain logs, handle calls, and track operations.

children.name: Public Safety Telecommunicators
children.description: Operate telephone, radio, or other communication systems to receive and communicate requests for emergency assistance at 9-1-1 public safety answering points and emergency operations centers. Take information from the public and other sources regarding crimes, threats, disturbances, acts of terrorism, fires, medical emergencies, and other public safety matters. May coordinate and provide information to law enforcement and emergency response personnel. May access sensitive databases and other information sources as needed. May provide additional instructions to callers based on knowledge of and certification in law enforcement, fire, or emergency medical procedures.

children.name: Dispatchers, Except Police, Fire, and Ambulance
children.description: Schedule and dispatch workers, work crews, equipment, or service vehicles for conveyance of materials, freight, or passengers, or for normal installation, service, or emergency repairs rendered outside the place of business. Duties may include using radio, telephone, or computer to transmit assignments and compiling statistics and reports on work progress.

children.name: Meter Readers, Utilities
children.description: Read utility meters (e.g., gas, water, or electricity), record usage, and check for irregularities or needed maintenance.

children.name: Meter Readers, Utilities
children.description: Read meter and record consumption of electricity, gas, water, or steam.

children.name: Postal Service Workers
children.description: Sort, process, and deliver mail. Sell postal products and provide customer service in post offices.

children.name: Postal Service Clerks
children.description: Perform any combination of tasks in a United States Postal Service (USPS) post office, such as receive letters and parcels; sell postage and revenue stamps, postal cards, and stamped envelopes; fill out and sell money orders; place mail in pigeon holes of mail rack or in bags; and examine mail for correct postage. Includes postal service clerks employed by USPS contractors.

children.name: Postal Service Mail Carriers
children.description: Sort and deliver mail for the United States Postal Service (USPS). Deliver mail on established route by vehicle or on foot. Includes postal service mail carriers employed by USPS contractors.

children.name: Postal Service Mail Sorters, Processors, and Processing Machine Operators
children.description: Prepare incoming and outgoing mail for distribution for the United States Postal Service (USPS). Examine, sort, and route mail. Load, operate, and occasionally adjust and repair mail processing, sorting, and canceling machinery. Keep records of shipments, pouches, and sacks, and perform other duties related to mail handling within the postal service. Includes postal service mail sorters and processors employed by USPS contractors.

children.name: Production, Planning, and Expediting Clerks
children.description: Coordinate and expedite the flow of work and materials within or between departments according to production schedules.

children.name: Production, Planning, and Expediting Clerks
children.description: Coordinate and expedite the flow of work and materials within or between departments of an establishment according to production schedule. Duties include reviewing and distributing production, work, and shipment schedules; conferring with department supervisors to determine progress of work and completion dates; and compiling reports on progress of work, inventory levels, costs, and production problems.

children.name: Shipping, Receiving, and Traffic Clerks
children.description: Verify and record incoming or outgoing shipments, prepare items for shipment, and coordinate with carriers. Maintain logs and update shipping records.

children.name: Shipping, Receiving, and Inventory Clerks
children.description: Verify and maintain records on incoming and outgoing shipments involving inventory. Duties include verifying and recording incoming merchandise or material and arranging for the transportation of products. May prepare items for shipment.

children.name: Stock Clerks and Order Fillers
children.description: Receive, store, and issue merchandise or materials. Track inventory, fill orders, and maintain stockroom organization.

children.name: Stock Clerks and Order Fillers
children.description: Receive, store, and issue sales floor merchandise, materials, equipment, and other items from stockroom, warehouse, or storage yard to fill shelves, racks, tables, or customers' orders. May mark prices on merchandise and set up sales displays.

children.name: Stock Clerks, Sales Floor
children.description: Receive, store, and issue sales floor merchandise. Stock shelves, racks, cases, bins, and tables with merchandise and arrange merchandise displays to attract customers. May periodically take physical count of stock or check and mark merchandise.

children.name: Marking Clerks
children.description: Print and attach price tickets to articles of merchandise using one or several methods, such as marking price on tickets by hand or using ticket-printing machine.

children.name: Stock Clerks- Stockroom, Warehouse, or Storage Yard
children.description: Receive, store, and issue materials, equipment, and other items from stockroom, warehouse, or storage yard. Keep records and compile stock reports.

children.name: Order Fillers, Wholesale and Retail Sales
children.description: Fill customers' mail and telephone orders from stored merchandise in accordance with specifications on sales slips or order forms. Duties include computing prices of items, completing order receipts, keeping records of out-going orders, and requisitioning additional materials, supplies, and equipment.

children.name: Weighers, Measurers, Checkers, and Samplers, Recordkeeping
children.description: Weigh, measure, and check raw materials or products to ensure adherence to standards. Keep relevant records of materials tested or measured.

children.name: Weighers, Measurers, Checkers, and Samplers, Recordkeeping
children.description: Weigh, measure, and check materials, supplies, and equipment for the purpose of keeping relevant records. Duties are primarily clerical by nature. Includes workers who collect and keep record of samples of products or materials.

children.name: Secretaries and Administrative Assistants
children.description: Secretaries and Administrative Assistants provide administrative support to organizations and individuals. They perform various tasks, including managing correspondence, scheduling appointments, organizing files, and assisting in office operations.

children.name: Secretaries and Administrative Assistants
children.description: Perform routine clerical and administrative duties such as scheduling appointments, organizing files, and preparing correspondence.

children.name: Executive Secretaries and Executive Administrative Assistants
children.description: Provide high-level administrative support by conducting research, preparing statistical reports, and handling information requests, as well as performing routine administrative functions such as preparing correspondence, receiving visitors, arranging conference calls, and scheduling meetings. May also train and supervise lower-level clerical staff.

children.name: Legal Secretaries and Administrative Assistants
children.description: Perform secretarial duties using legal terminology, procedures, and documents. Prepare legal papers and correspondence, such as summonses, complaints, motions, and subpoenas. May also assist with legal research.

children.name: Medical Secretaries and Administrative Assistants
children.description: Perform secretarial duties using specific knowledge of medical terminology and hospital, clinic, or laboratory procedures. Duties may include scheduling appointments, billing patients, and compiling and recording medical charts, reports, and correspondence.

children.name: Secretaries and Administrative Assistants, Except Legal, Medical, and Executive
children.description: Perform routine administrative functions such as drafting correspondence, scheduling appointments, organizing and maintaining paper and electronic files, or providing information to callers.

children.name: Other Office and Administrative Support Workers
children.description: This category includes a wide range of occupations that provide administrative support and perform various clerical tasks within an organization. It encompasses roles such as data entry clerks, mail clerks, office clerks, receptionists, and customer service representatives.

children.name: Computer Operators
children.description: Monitor and control electronic computer systems. Handle hardware or software malfunctions, load peripheral equipment, and oversee system performance.

children.name: Computer Operators
children.description: Monitor and control electronic computer and peripheral electronic data processing equipment to process business, scientific, engineering, and other data according to operating instructions. Monitor and respond to operating and error messages. May enter commands at a computer terminal and set controls on computer and peripheral devices.

children.name: Data Entry and Information Processing Workers
children.description: Input information into computerized databases, spreadsheets, or other systems. Verify accuracy of data and troubleshoot minor input problems.

children.name: Data Entry Keyers
children.description: Operate data entry device, such as keyboard or photo composing perforator. Duties may include verifying data and preparing materials for printing.

children.name: Word Processors and Typists
children.description: Use word processor, computer, or typewriter to type letters, reports, forms, or other material from rough draft, corrected copy, or voice recording. May perform other clerical duties as assigned.

children.name: Desktop Publishers
children.description: Use computer software to format and combine text, data, and graphics into page layouts for print or online publication.

children.name: Desktop Publishers
children.description: Format typescript and graphic elements using computer software to produce publication-ready material.

children.name: Insurance Claims and Policy Processing Clerks
children.description: Process insurance applications, changes, or claims. Organize policy details, review claims for completeness, and forward to appropriate departments.

children.name: Insurance Claims and Policy Processing Clerks
children.description: Process new insurance policies, modifications to existing policies, and claims forms. Obtain information from policyholders to verify the accuracy and completeness of information on claims forms, applications and related documents, and company records. Update existing policies and company records to reflect changes requested by policyholders and insurance company representatives.

children.name: Insurance Claims Clerks
children.description: Obtain information from insured or designated persons for purpose of settling claim with insurance carrier.

children.name: Insurance Policy Processing Clerks
children.description: Process applications for, changes to, reinstatement of, and cancellation of insurance policies. Duties include reviewing insurance applications to ensure that all questions have been answered, compiling data on insurance policy changes, changing policy records to conform to insured party's specifications, compiling data on lapsed insurance policies to determine automatic reinstatement according to company policies, canceling insurance policies as requested by agents, and verifying the accuracy of insurance company records.

children.name: Mail Clerks and Mail Machine Operators, Except Postal Service
children.description: Prepare incoming and outgoing mail for distribution. Operate mail-processing machines or sort mail by hand.

children.name: Mail Clerks and Mail Machine Operators, Except Postal Service
children.description: Prepare incoming and outgoing mail for distribution. Time-stamp, open, read, sort, and route incoming mail; and address, seal, stamp, fold, stuff, and affix postage to outgoing mail or packages. Duties may also include keeping necessary records and completed forms.

children.name: Office Clerks, General
children.description: Perform a variety of administrative tasks, such as answering phones, filing records, and assisting with data entry or scheduling.

children.name: Office Clerks, General
children.description: Perform duties too varied and diverse to be classified in any specific office clerical occupation, requiring knowledge of office systems and procedures. Clerical duties may be assigned in accordance with the office procedures of individual establishments and may include a combination of answering telephones, bookkeeping, typing or word processing, office machine operation, and filing.

children.name: Office Machine Operators, Except Computer
children.description: Operate machines that duplicate, scan, or bind documents. Ensure equipment is maintained and troubleshoot minor mechanical issues.

children.name: Office Machine Operators, Except Computer
children.description: Operate one or more of a variety of office machines, such as photocopying, photographic, and duplicating machines, or other office machines.

children.name: Proofreaders and Copy Markers
children.description: Examine written text for spelling, punctuation, and grammatical errors. Mark corrections and verify revisions.

children.name: Proofreaders and Copy Markers
children.description: Read transcript or proof type setup to detect and mark for correction any grammatical, typographical, or compositional errors. Excludes workers whose primary duty is editing copy. Includes proofreaders of braille.

children.name: Statistical Assistants
children.description: Compile and compute statistical data under the guidance of statisticians. Prepare tables, charts, or reports summarizing analysis results.

children.name: Statistical Assistants
children.description: Compile and compute data according to statistical formulas for use in statistical studies. May perform actuarial computations and compile charts and graphs for use by actuaries. Includes actuarial clerks.

children.name: Bioinformatics Technicians
children.description: Apply principles and methods of bioinformatics to assist scientists in areas such as pharmaceuticals, medical technology, biotechnology, computational biology, proteomics, computer information science, biology and medical informatics. Apply bioinformatics tools to visualize, analyze, manipulate or interpret molecular data. May build and maintain databases for processing and analyzing genomic or other biological information.

children.name: Miscellaneous Office and Administrative Support Workers
children.description: Provide a range of administrative services not covered by other standard office occupations, potentially including specialized clerical tasks or recordkeeping.

children.name: Office and Administrative Support Workers, All Other
children.description: All office and administrative support workers not listed separately.

name: Farming, Fishing, and Forestry Occupations
description: Concerned with planting, growing, and harvesting crops, raising livestock, catching fish, or managing forest resources. Includes farmers, ranchers, fishers, loggers, and related roles in agricultural or natural environments.

children.name: Supervisors of Farming, Fishing, and Forestry Workers
children.description: This category includes supervisors who oversee and coordinate the activities of workers engaged in farming, fishing, and forestry operations. They ensure that tasks are carried out efficiently, adhere to safety regulations, and manage the overall operations of farms, fisheries, or forestry sites.

children.name: First-Line Supervisors of Farming, Fishing, and Forestry Workers
children.description: Coordinate and direct the activities of agricultural, fishing, or forestry workers. Assign tasks, monitor progress, and ensure compliance with safety and environmental regulations.

children.name: First-Line Supervisors of Farming, Fishing, and Forestry Workers
children.description: Directly supervise and coordinate the activities of agricultural, forestry, aquacultural, and related workers.

children.name: First-Line Supervisors of Logging Workers
children.description: Directly supervise and coordinate activities of logging workers.

children.name: First-Line Supervisors of Aquacultural Workers
children.description: Directly supervise and coordinate activities of aquacultural workers.

children.name: First-Line Supervisors of Agricultural Crop and Horticultural Workers
children.description: Directly supervise and coordinate activities of agricultural crop or horticultural workers.

children.name: First-Line Supervisors of Animal Husbandry and Animal Care Workers
children.description: Directly supervise and coordinate activities of animal husbandry or animal care workers.

children.name: Agricultural Workers
children.description: This category includes supervisors who oversee and coordinate the activities of workers engaged in farming, fishing, and forestry operations. They ensure that tasks are carried out efficiently, adhere to safety regulations, and manage the overall operations of farms, fisheries, or forestry sites.

children.name: Agricultural Inspectors
children.description: Inspect agricultural commodities or facilities, ensuring compliance with regulations and quality standards. Identify and document violations.

children.name: Agricultural Inspectors
children.description: Inspect agricultural commodities, processing equipment, and facilities, and fish and logging operations, to ensure compliance with regulations and laws governing health, quality, and safety.

children.name: Animal Breeders
children.description: Select and breed animals according to genetic principles and knowledge of offspring characteristics. Keep records on breeding schedules and pedigrees.

children.name: Animal Breeders
children.description: Select and breed animals according to their genealogy, characteristics, and offspring. May require knowledge of artificial insemination techniques and equipment use. May involve keeping records on heats, birth intervals, or pedigree.

children.name: Graders and Sorters, Agricultural Products
children.description: Grade, sort, or classify unprocessed food and other agricultural products by size, weight, or condition.

children.name: Graders and Sorters, Agricultural Products
children.description: Grade, sort, or classify unprocessed food and other agricultural products by size, weight, color, or condition.

children.name: Miscellaneous Agricultural Workers
children.description: Perform farming or agricultural tasks not covered by other occupations, possibly planting, harvesting, or managing specialized livestock.

children.name: Agricultural Equipment Operators
children.description: Drive and control equipment to support agricultural activities such as tilling soil; planting, cultivating, and harvesting crops; feeding and herding livestock; or removing animal waste. May perform tasks such as crop baling or hay bucking. May operate stationary equipment to perform post-harvest tasks such as husking, shelling, threshing, and ginning.

children.name: Farmworkers and Laborers, Crop, Nursery, and Greenhouse
children.description: Manually plant, cultivate, and harvest vegetables, fruits, nuts, horticultural specialties, and field crops. Use hand tools, such as shovels, trowels, hoes, tampers, pruning hooks, shears, and knives. Duties may include tilling soil and applying fertilizers; transplanting, weeding, thinning, or pruning crops; applying pesticides; or cleaning, grading, sorting, packing, and loading harvested products. May construct trellises, repair fences and farm buildings, or participate in irrigation activities.

children.name: Nursery Workers
children.description: Work in nursery facilities or at customer location planting, cultivating, harvesting, and transplanting trees, shrubs, or plants.

children.name: Farmworkers and Laborers, Crop
children.description: Manually plant, cultivate, and harvest vegetables, fruits, nuts and field crops. Use hand tools, such as shovels, trowels, hoes, tampers, pruning hooks, shears, and knives. Duties may include tilling soil and applying fertilizers; transplanting, weeding, thinning, or pruning crops; applying pesticides; cleaning, packing, and loading harvested products. May construct trellises, repair fences and farm buildings, or participate in irrigation activities.

children.name: Farmworkers, Farm, Ranch, and Aquacultural Animals
children.description: Attend to live farm, ranch, open range or aquacultural animals that may include cattle, sheep, swine, goats, horses and other equines, poultry, rabbits, finfish, shellfish, and bees. Attend to animals produced for animal products, such as meat, fur, skins, feathers, eggs, milk, and honey. Duties may include feeding, watering, herding, grazing, milking, castrating, branding, de-beaking, weighing, catching, and loading animals. May maintain records on animals; examine animals to detect diseases and injuries; assist in birth deliveries; and administer medications, vaccinations, or insecticides as appropriate. May clean and maintain animal housing areas. Includes workers who shear wool from sheep and collect eggs in hatcheries.

children.name: Agricultural Workers, All Other
children.description: All agricultural workers not listed separately.

children.name: Fishing and Hunting Workers
children.description: This category includes workers involved in fishing and hunting activities. Fishing workers may engage in various tasks related to commercial or recreational fishing, such as operating fishing vessels, setting nets or lines, and processing or preserving fish. Hunting workers may be involved in activities related to game hunting or wildlife management.

children.name: Fishers and Related Fishing Workers
children.description: Catch and gather fish or other aquatic species. Maintain fishing gear, navigate vessels, and store catch properly.

children.name: Fishers and Related Fishing Workers
children.description: Use nets, fishing rods, traps, or other equipment to catch and gather fish or other aquatic animals from rivers, lakes, or oceans, for human consumption or other uses. May haul game onto ship.

children.name: Hunters and Trappers
children.description: Trap and hunt wild animals for food, pelts, or other products. Use knowledge of wildlife habits, tracking techniques, and environmental regulations.

children.name: Hunters and Trappers
children.description: Hunt and trap wild animals for human consumption, fur, feed, bait, or other purposes.

children.name: Forest, Conservation, and Logging Workers
children.description: This category includes workers involved in various activities related to forestry, conservation, and logging. It encompasses a range of roles, such as forest workers engaged in planting, maintaining, and harvesting trees; conservation workers involved in preserving and managing natural resources; and logging workers responsible for cutting and processing timber.

children.name: Forest and Conservation Workers
children.description: Develop, maintain, and protect forests by planting seedlings, controlling insects and diseases, and assisting with fire prevention measures.

children.name: Forest and Conservation Workers
children.description: Under supervision, perform manual labor necessary to develop, maintain, or protect areas such as forests, forested areas, woodlands, wetlands, and rangelands through such activities as raising and transporting seedlings; combating insects, pests, and diseases harmful to plant life; and building structures to control water, erosion, and leaching of soil. Includes forester aides, seedling pullers, tree planters, and gatherers of nontimber forestry products such as pine straw.

children.name: Logging Workers
children.description: Fell, process, and transport timber. Operate machinery such as harvesters and loaders, and follow safety protocols when working in forests.

children.name: Fallers
children.description: Use axes or chainsaws to fell trees using knowledge of tree characteristics and cutting techniques to control direction of fall and minimize tree damage.

children.name: Logging Equipment Operators
children.description: Drive logging tractor or wheeled vehicle equipped with one or more accessories, such as bulldozer blade, frontal shear, grapple, logging arch, cable winches, hoisting rack, or crane boom, to fell tree; to skid, load, unload, or stack logs; or to pull stumps or clear brush. Includes operating stand-alone logging machines, such as log chippers.

children.name: Log Graders and Scalers
children.description: Grade logs or estimate the marketable content or value of logs or pulpwood in sorting yards, millpond, log deck, or similar locations. Inspect logs for defects or measure logs to determine volume.

children.name: Logging Workers, All Other
children.description: All logging workers not listed separately.

name: Construction and Extraction Occupations
description: Involves building, repairing, or demolishing structures and extracting natural resources. Includes carpenters, electricians, miners, plumbers, and other trades focused on infrastructure and resource excavation.

children.name: Supervisors of Construction and Extraction Workers
children.description: This category includes supervisors who oversee construction and extraction activities in various industries. They are responsible for managing and coordinating the work of construction and extraction workers, ensuring compliance with safety regulations, and overseeing the progress of projects. The category encompasses supervisors in fields such as construction, mining, oil and gas extraction, and more.

children.name: First-Line Supervisors of Construction Trades and Extraction Workers
children.description: Plan, schedule, and coordinate the work of construction or extraction crews. Monitor progress, enforce safety regulations, and resolve on-site issues.

children.name: First-Line Supervisors of Construction Trades and Extraction Workers
children.description: Directly supervise and coordinate activities of construction or extraction workers.

children.name: Solar Energy Installation Managers
children.description: Direct work crews installing residential or commercial solar photovoltaic or thermal systems.

children.name: Construction Trades Workers
children.description: This category includes various skilled workers involved in construction activities. It encompasses a wide range of occupations such as carpenters, electricians, plumbers, masons, painters, and other tradespeople. These workers perform specialized tasks related to construction, renovation, repair, and maintenance of buildings and structures.

children.name: Boilermakers
children.description: Construct, assemble, and repair boilers, vats, or other large vessels. Use welding or riveting skills to join parts and ensure structural integrity.

children.name: Boilermakers
children.description: Construct, assemble, maintain, and repair stationary steam boilers and boiler house auxiliaries. Align structures or plate sections to assemble boiler frame tanks or vats, following blueprints. Work involves use of hand and power tools, plumb bobs, levels, wedges, dogs, or turnbuckles. Assist in testing assembled vessels. Direct cleaning of boilers and boiler furnaces. Inspect and repair boiler fittings, such as safety valves, regulators, automatic-control mechanisms, water columns, and auxiliary machines.

children.name: Brickmasons, Blockmasons, and Stonemasons
children.description: Build walls, walkways, and other structures using bricks, blocks, or stone. Follow blueprints, mix mortar, and ensure alignment and structural soundness.

children.name: Brickmasons and Blockmasons
children.description: Lay and bind building materials, such as brick, structural tile, concrete block, cinder block, glass block, and terra-cotta block, with mortar and other substances, to construct or repair walls, partitions, arches, sewers, and other structures.

children.name: Stonemasons
children.description: Build stone structures, such as piers, walls, and abutments. Lay walks, curbstones, or special types of masonry for vats, tanks, and floors.

children.name: Carpenters
children.description: Construct, install, or repair frameworks and structures. Measure, cut, and shape wood or other materials using hand and power tools.

children.name: Carpenters
children.description: Construct, erect, install, or repair structures and fixtures made of wood and comparable materials, such as concrete forms; building frameworks, including partitions, joists, studding, and rafters; and wood stairways, window and door frames, and hardwood floors. May also install cabinets, siding, drywall, and batt or roll insulation. Includes brattice builders who build doors or brattices (ventilation walls or partitions) in underground passageways.

children.name: Construction Carpenters
children.description: Construct, erect, install, and repair structures and fixtures of wood, plywood, and wallboard, using carpenter's hand tools and power tools.

children.name: Rough Carpenters
children.description: Build rough wooden structures, such as concrete forms, scaffolds, tunnel, bridge, or sewer supports, billboard signs, and temporary frame shelters, according to sketches, blueprints, or oral instructions.

children.name: Carpet, Floor, and Tile Installers and Finishers
children.description: Install and finish carpets, hardwood, tile, or other flooring materials. Prepare surfaces, align materials, and apply adhesives or finishes.

children.name: Carpet Installers
children.description: Lay and install carpet from rolls or blocks on floors. Install padding and trim flooring materials.

children.name: Floor Layers, Except Carpet, Wood, and Hard Tiles
children.description: Apply blocks, strips, or sheets of shock-absorbing, sound-deadening, or decorative coverings to floors.

children.name: Floor Sanders and Finishers
children.description: Scrape and sand wooden floors to smooth surfaces using floor scraper and floor sanding machine, and apply coats of finish.

children.name: Tile and Stone Setters
children.description: Apply hard tile, stone, and comparable materials to walls, floors, ceilings, countertops, and roof decks.

children.name: Cement Masons, Concrete Finishers, and Terrazzo Workers
children.description: Pour, level, and finish concrete for various projects, such as sidewalks or floors. May also install and finish terrazzo surfaces.

children.name: Cement Masons and Concrete Finishers
children.description: Smooth and finish surfaces of poured concrete, such as floors, walks, sidewalks, roads, or curbs using a variety of hand and power tools. Align forms for sidewalks, curbs, or gutters; patch voids; and use saws to cut expansion joints.

children.name: Terrazzo Workers and Finishers
children.description: Apply a mixture of cement, sand, pigment, or marble chips to floors, stairways, and cabinet fixtures to fashion durable and decorative surfaces.

children.name: Construction Laborers
children.description: Perform tasks involving physical labor at construction sites, operate hand or power tools, and assist other craft workers.

children.name: Construction Laborers
children.description: Perform tasks involving physical labor at construction sites. May operate hand and power tools of all types: air hammers, earth tampers, cement mixers, small mechanical hoists, surveying and measuring equipment, and a variety of other equipment and instruments. May clean and prepare sites, dig trenches, set braces to support the sides of excavations, erect scaffolding, and clean up rubble, debris, and other waste materials. May assist other craft workers.

children.name: Construction Equipment Operators
children.description: Operate machinery such as bulldozers, excavators, or loaders to move earth and materials, clear land, and assist in building projects.

children.name: Paving, Surfacing, and Tamping Equipment Operators
children.description: Operate equipment used for applying concrete, asphalt, or other materials to road beds, parking lots, or airport runways and taxiways or for tamping gravel, dirt, or other materials. Includes concrete and asphalt paving machine operators, form tampers, tamping machine operators, and stone spreader operators.

children.name: Pile Driver Operators
children.description: Operate pile drivers mounted on skids, barges, crawler treads, or locomotive cranes to drive pilings for retaining walls, bulkheads, and foundations of structures such as buildings, bridges, and piers.

children.name: Operating Engineers and Other Construction Equipment Operators
children.description: Operate one or several types of power construction equipment, such as motor graders, bulldozers, scrapers, compressors, pumps, derricks, shovels, tractors, or front-end loaders to excavate, move, and grade earth, erect structures, or pour concrete or other hard surface pavement. May repair and maintain equipment in addition to other duties.

children.name: Drywall Installers, Ceiling Tile Installers, and Tapers
children.description: Install wallboard and apply tape or compound to seams and corners for finishing. May also install ceiling tiles in buildings.

children.name: Drywall and Ceiling Tile Installers
children.description: Apply plasterboard or other wallboard to ceilings or interior walls of buildings. Apply or mount acoustical tiles or blocks, strips, or sheets of shock-absorbing materials to ceilings and walls of buildings to reduce or reflect sound. Materials may be of decorative quality. Includes lathers who fasten wooden, metal, or rockboard lath to walls, ceilings, or partitions of buildings to provide support base for plaster, fireproofing, or acoustical material.

children.name: Tapers
children.description: Seal joints between plasterboard or other wallboard to prepare wall surface for painting or papering.

children.name: Electricians
children.description: Install, maintain, and repair electrical wiring, lighting, and control systems. Diagnose issues, ensure compliance with codes, and follow safety protocols.

children.name: Electricians
children.description: Install, maintain, and repair electrical wiring, equipment, and fixtures. Ensure that work is in accordance with relevant codes. May install or service street lights, intercom systems, or electrical control systems.

children.name: Glaziers
children.description: Install glass in windows, skylights, and other fixtures in buildings or vehicles. Measure and cut glass, seal edges, and secure frames.

children.name: Glaziers
children.description: Install glass in windows, skylights, store fronts, and display cases, or on surfaces, such as building fronts, interior walls, ceilings, and tabletops.

children.name: Insulation Workers
children.description: Line and cover structures with insulating materials to control or maintain temperatures. May apply insulating materials to pipes, ductwork, or other mechanical systems.

children.name: Insulation Workers, Floor, Ceiling, and Wall
children.description: Line and cover structures with insulating materials. May work with batt, roll, or blown insulation materials.

children.name: Insulation Workers, Mechanical
children.description: Apply insulating materials to pipes or ductwork, or other mechanical systems in order to help control and maintain temperature.

children.name: Painters and Paperhangers
children.description: Apply paint, stain, varnish, or wallpaper to buildings, equipment, or other structures. Prepare surfaces by cleaning or sanding, and mix materials to achieve desired finishes.

children.name: Painters, Construction and Maintenance
children.description: Paint walls, equipment, buildings, bridges, and other structural surfaces, using brushes, rollers, and spray guns. May remove old paint to prepare surface prior to painting. May mix colors or oils to obtain desired color or consistency.

children.name: Paperhangers
children.description: Cover interior walls or ceilings of rooms with decorative wallpaper or fabric, or attach advertising posters on surfaces such as walls and billboards. May remove old materials or prepare surfaces to be papered.

children.name: Pipelayers, Plumbers, Pipefitters, and Steamfitters
children.description: Lay pipe for storm or sanitation sewers, water mains, or gas lines. Install and repair plumbing fixtures, pipe systems, or steam systems.

children.name: Pipelayers
children.description: Lay pipe for storm or sanitation sewers, drains, and water mains. Perform any combination of the following tasks: grade trenches or culverts, position pipe, or seal joints.

children.name: Plumbers, Pipefitters, and Steamfitters
children.description: Assemble, install, alter, and repair pipelines or pipe systems that carry water, steam, air, or other liquids or gases. May install heating and cooling equipment and mechanical control systems. Includes sprinkler fitters.

children.name: Pipe Fitters and Steamfitters
children.description: Lay out, assemble, install, or maintain pipe systems, pipe supports, or related hydraulic or pneumatic equipment for steam, hot water, heating, cooling, lubricating, sprinkling, or industrial production or processing systems.

children.name: Plumbers
children.description: Assemble, install, or repair pipes, fittings, or fixtures of heating, water, or drainage systems, according to specifications or plumbing codes.

children.name: Plasterers and Stucco Masons
children.description: Apply plaster or stucco to walls and ceilings, forming smooth or textured surfaces. May also install prefabricated exterior insulation systems.

children.name: Plasterers and Stucco Masons
children.description: Apply interior or exterior plaster, cement, stucco, or similar materials. May also set ornamental plaster.

children.name: Reinforcing Iron and Rebar Workers
children.description: Position and secure steel bars or mesh in concrete forms to reinforce concrete structures. Cut, bend, or weld rebar as necessary.

children.name: Reinforcing Iron and Rebar Workers
children.description: Position and secure steel bars or mesh in concrete forms in order to reinforce concrete. Use a variety of fasteners, rod-bending machines, blowtorches, and hand tools. Includes rod busters.

children.name: Roofers
children.description: Cover roofs of structures with shingles, asphalt, or other materials. Install insulation layers, apply waterproofing, and ensure correct sealing to prevent leaks.

children.name: Roofers
children.description: Cover roofs of structures with shingles, slate, asphalt, aluminum, wood, or related materials. May spray roofs, sidings, and walls with material to bind, seal, insulate, or soundproof sections of structures.

children.name: Sheet Metal Workers
children.description: Fabricate, assemble, and install products made from thin metal sheets, such as ducts or roofing panels. Use technical drawings, cut metal, and secure seams.

children.name: Sheet Metal Workers
children.description: Fabricate, assemble, install, and repair sheet metal products and equipment, such as ducts, control boxes, drainpipes, and furnace casings. Work may involve any of the following: setting up and operating fabricating machines to cut, bend, and straighten sheet metal; shaping metal over anvils, blocks, or forms using hammer; operating soldering and welding equipment to join sheet metal parts; or inspecting, assembling, and smoothing seams and joints of burred surfaces. Includes sheet metal duct installers who install prefabricated sheet metal ducts used for heating, air conditioning, or other purposes.

children.name: Structural Iron and Steel Workers
children.description: Raise, place, and unite iron or steel girders, columns, and other structural members to form frameworks for buildings, bridges, and other structures.

children.name: Structural Iron and Steel Workers
children.description: Raise, place, and unite iron or steel girders, columns, and other structural members to form completed structures or structural frameworks. May erect metal storage tanks and assemble prefabricated metal buildings.

children.name: Solar Photovoltaic Installers
children.description: Assemble, install, and maintain solar photovoltaic systems on roofs or other structures. Ensure safe handling of electrical wiring and compliance with building codes.

children.name: Solar Photovoltaic Installers
children.description: Assemble, install, or maintain solar photovoltaic (PV) systems on roofs or other structures in compliance with site assessment and schematics. May include measuring, cutting, assembling, and bolting structural framing and solar modules. May perform minor electrical work such as current checks.

children.name: Helpers, Construction Trades
children.description: This category includes workers who assist skilled tradespeople in various construction trades. They provide support and assistance in tasks such as carrying materials, cleaning work areas, operating machinery, and performing other duties as directed by the skilled trades workers. Helpers work under the supervision of more experienced tradespeople and contribute to the overall progress of construction projects.

children.name: Helpers, Construction Trades
children.description: Assist skilled construction trades workers by supplying or holding materials or tools, cleaning job sites, and performing basic tasks under the direction of more experienced craft workers.

children.name: Helpers--Brickmasons, Blockmasons, Stonemasons, and Tile and Marble Setters
children.description: Help brickmasons, blockmasons, stonemasons, or tile and marble setters by performing duties requiring less skill. Duties include using, supplying, or holding materials or tools, and cleaning work area and equipment.

children.name: Helpers--Carpenters
children.description: Help carpenters by performing duties requiring less skill. Duties include using, supplying, or holding materials or tools, and cleaning work area and equipment.

children.name: Helpers--Electricians
children.description: Help electricians by performing duties requiring less skill. Duties include using, supplying, or holding materials or tools, and cleaning work area and equipment.

children.name: Helpers--Painters, Paperhangers, Plasterers, and Stucco Masons
children.description: Help painters, paperhangers, plasterers, or stucco masons by performing duties requiring less skill. Duties include using, supplying, or holding materials or tools, and cleaning work area and equipment.

children.name: Helpers--Pipelayers, Plumbers, Pipefitters, and Steamfitters
children.description: Help plumbers, pipefitters, steamfitters, or pipelayers by performing duties requiring less skill. Duties include using, supplying, or holding materials or tools, and cleaning work area and equipment.

children.name: Helpers--Roofers
children.description: Help roofers by performing duties requiring less skill. Duties include using, supplying, or holding materials or tools, and cleaning work area and equipment.

children.name: Helpers, Construction Trades, All Other
children.description: All construction trades helpers not listed separately.

children.name: Other Construction and Related Workers
children.description: This category includes a diverse range of construction and related workers who perform various tasks that support construction projects but do not fall into other specific construction trades categories. It may include workers such as highway maintenance workers, roustabouts, elevator installers and repairers, and other construction-related roles that are not classified elsewhere.

children.name: Construction and Building Inspectors
children.description: Inspect buildings, highways, and other structures to ensure compliance with building codes and regulations. Review structural quality, safety, and overall integrity of construction projects.

children.name: Construction and Building Inspectors
children.description: Inspect structures using engineering skills to determine structural soundness and compliance with specifications, building codes, and other regulations. Inspections may be general in nature or may be limited to a specific area, such as electrical systems or plumbing.

children.name: Elevator Installers and Repairers
children.description: Assemble, install, and repair elevators, escalators, and similar systems. Read blueprints, conduct routine maintenance, and troubleshoot mechanical or electrical malfunctions.

children.name: Elevator and Escalator Installers and Repairers
children.description: Assemble, install, repair, or maintain electric or hydraulic freight or passenger elevators, escalators, or dumbwaiters.

children.name: Fence Erectors
children.description: Build and repair fences, gates, and related enclosures. Measure property lines, dig postholes, and set fence posts in concrete or other materials.

children.name: Fence Erectors
children.description: Erect and repair fences and fence gates, using hand and power tools.

children.name: Hazardous Materials Removal Workers
children.description: Identify, remove, package, transport, or dispose of hazardous substances (like asbestos or lead). Follow strict safety protocols to protect health and the environment.

children.name: Hazardous Materials Removal Workers
children.description: Identify, remove, pack, transport, or dispose of hazardous materials, including asbestos, lead-based paint, waste oil, fuel, transmission fluid, radioactive materials, or contaminated soil. Specialized training and certification in hazardous materials handling or a confined entry permit are generally required. May operate earth-moving equipment or trucks.

children.name: Highway Maintenance Workers
children.description: Maintain highways, roads, and airport runways. Patch potholes, clear drains, remove snow, and set up traffic control devices.

children.name: Highway Maintenance Workers
children.description: Maintain highways, municipal and rural roads, airport runways, and rights-of-way. Duties include patching broken or eroded pavement and repairing guard rails, highway markers, and snow fences. May also mow or clear brush from along road, or plow snow from roadway.

children.name: Rail-Track Laying and Maintenance Equipment Operators
children.description: Operate machinery to lay, repair, or remove railroad tracks. Measure and cut rails, align track sections, and ensure proper alignment and safety.

children.name: Rail-Track Laying and Maintenance Equipment Operators
children.description: Lay, repair, and maintain track for standard or narrow-gauge railroad equipment used in regular railroad service or in plant yards, quarries, sand and gravel pits, and mines. Includes ballast cleaning machine operators and railroad bed tamping machine operators.

children.name: Septic Tank Servicers and Sewer Pipe Cleaners
children.description: Clean and repair septic tanks, sewer lines, or drains. Locate problem areas, operate pumping equipment, and perform routine system maintenance.

children.name: Septic Tank Servicers and Sewer Pipe Cleaners
children.description: Clean and repair septic tanks, sewer lines, or drains. May patch walls and partitions of tank, replace damaged drain tile, or repair breaks in underground piping.

children.name: Miscellaneous Construction and Related Workers
children.description: Carry out construction-related tasks not categorized under specific trades. May include highway flagging, site preparation, or specialized tasks such as chimney repair.

children.name: Segmental Pavers
children.description: Lay out, cut, and place segmental paving units. Includes installers of bedding and restraining materials for the paving units.

children.name: Construction and Related Workers, All Other
children.description: All construction and related workers not listed separately.

children.name: Solar Thermal Installers and Technicians
children.description: Install or repair solar energy systems designed to collect, store, and circulate solar-heated water for residential, commercial or industrial use.

children.name: Weatherization Installers and Technicians
children.description: Perform a variety of activities to weatherize homes and make them more energy efficient. Duties include repairing windows, insulating ducts, and performing heating, ventilating, and air-conditioning (HVAC) work. May perform energy audits and advise clients on energy conservation measures.

children.name: Extraction Workers
children.description: This category includes workers involved in extracting natural resources from the earth. It encompasses various occupations such as mining machine operators, oil and gas extraction workers, quarrying workers, and other related roles. These workers are primarily engaged in extracting minerals, metals, oil, gas, and other valuable resources from the ground.

children.name: Derrick, Rotary Drill, and Service Unit Operators, Oil, Gas, and Mining
children.description: Operate derricks and drilling equipment to extract oil, gas, or minerals from the earth. Monitor pressure gauges, maintain equipment, and manage the drilling process.

children.name: Derrick Operators, Oil and Gas
children.description: Rig derrick equipment and operate pumps to circulate mud or fluid through drill hole.

children.name: Rotary Drill Operators, Oil and Gas
children.description: Set up or operate a variety of drills to remove underground oil and gas, or remove core samples for testing during oil and gas exploration.

children.name: Service Unit Operators, Oil and Gas
children.description: Operate equipment to increase oil flow from producing wells or to remove stuck pipe, casing, tools, or other obstructions from drilling wells. Includes fishing-tool technicians.

children.name: Earth Drillers, Except Oil and Gas
children.description: Operate drilling equipment to drill holes for utility lines, foundation supports, or geological exploration. Monitor equipment performance, remove earth or rock, and ensure site safety.

children.name: Earth Drillers, Except Oil and Gas
children.description: Operate a variety of drills such as rotary, churn, and pneumatic to tap sub-surface water and salt deposits, to remove core samples during mineral exploration or soil testing, and to facilitate the use of explosives in mining or construction. May use explosives. Includes horizontal and earth boring machine operators.

children.name: Explosives Workers, Ordnance Handling Experts, and Blasters
children.description: Handle explosives for construction, mining, or demolition. Assess rock or other material, set charges, and detonate explosives following strict safety protocols.

children.name: Explosives Workers, Ordnance Handling Experts, and Blasters
children.description: Place and detonate explosives to demolish structures or to loosen, remove, or displace earth, rock, or other materials. May perform specialized handling, storage, and accounting procedures. Includes seismograph shooters.

children.name: Mining Machine Operators
children.description: Operate self-propelled machines to extract coal, ore, or other materials from mines. Monitor equipment gauges, manage conveyor systems, and ensure efficient extraction.

children.name: Continuous Mining Machine Operators
children.description: Operate self-propelled mining machines that rip coal, metal and nonmetal ores, rock, stone, or sand from the mine face and load it onto conveyors, shuttle cars, or trucks in a continuous operation.

children.name: Mine Cutting and Channeling Machine Operators
children.description: Operate machinery such as longwall shears, plows, and cutting machines to cut or channel along the face or seams of coal mines, stone quarries, or other mining surfaces to facilitate blasting, separating, or removing minerals or materials from mines or from the Earth's surface. Includes shale planers.

children.name: Underground Mining Machine Operators, All Other
children.description: All underground mining machine operators not listed separately.

children.name: Rock Splitters, Quarry
children.description: Separate blocks of rough dimension stone from quarry mass using drills, wedges, or other tools. Check for quality, measure, and mark cutting lines.

children.name: Rock Splitters, Quarry
children.description: Separate blocks of rough dimension stone from quarry mass using jackhammers, wedges, or chop saws.

children.name: Roof Bolters, Mining
children.description: Operate machinery to install roof support bolts in underground mines to prevent roof collapses. Monitor and test the stability of installed bolts.

children.name: Roof Bolters, Mining
children.description: Operate machinery to install roof support bolts in underground mine.

children.name: Roustabouts, Oil and Gas
children.description: Assemble or repair oil field equipment using hand and power tools. Perform basic maintenance, transport materials, and maintain safety standards on oil rigs or fields.

children.name: Roustabouts, Oil and Gas
children.description: Assemble or repair oil field equipment using hand and power tools. Perform other tasks as needed.

children.name: Helpers—Extraction Workers
children.description: Assist more experienced workers in oil, gas, or mining operations. Haul materials, operate simple equipment, and clean worksites under close supervision.

children.name: Helpers--Extraction Workers
children.description: Help extraction craft workers, such as earth drillers, blasters and explosives workers, derrick operators, and mining machine operators, by performing duties requiring less skill. Duties include supplying equipment or cleaning work area.

children.name: Miscellaneous Extraction Workers
children.description: Perform extraction tasks not elsewhere classified, such as specialized drilling or rare mineral sampling in mines or quarries.

children.name: Extraction Workers, All Other
children.description: All extraction workers not listed separately.

name: Installation, Maintenance, and Repair Occupations
description: Covers roles setting up, troubleshooting, and fixing equipment, machines, and systems. Occupations include automotive mechanics, HVAC installers, and general maintenance technicians working across various industries.

children.name: Supervisors of Installation, Maintenance, and Repair Workers
children.description: This category includes supervisors who oversee and coordinate the work of installation, maintenance, and repair workers across various industries. They are responsible for managing teams, assigning tasks, ensuring compliance with safety regulations, and maintaining the efficiency of installation and repair processes. Supervisors in this category may work in fields such as construction, manufacturing, telecommunications, utilities, and transportation.

children.name: First-Line Supervisors of Mechanics, Installers, and Repairers
children.description: Direct and coordinate maintenance or repair staff. Assign tasks, schedule work, ensure compliance with safety regulations, and track work progress.

children.name: First-Line Supervisors of Mechanics, Installers, and Repairers
children.description: Directly supervise and coordinate the activities of mechanics, installers, and repairers. May also advise customers on recommended services. Excludes team or work leaders.

children.name: Electrical and Electronic Equipment Mechanics, Installers, and Repairers
children.description: This category includes workers who install, maintain, and repair electrical and electronic equipment across various industries. They may work on equipment such as electrical systems, telecommunications equipment, computer systems, and audiovisual systems. Workers in this category are skilled in diagnosing and fixing electrical and electronic issues, reading technical diagrams and manuals, and using specialized tools and equipment.

children.name: Computer, Automated Teller, and Office Machine Repairers
children.description: Install, maintain, and repair business machines such as computers, ATMs, copiers, or printers. Diagnose hardware problems, replace parts, and test functionality.

children.name: Computer, Automated Teller, and Office Machine Repairers
children.description: Repair, maintain, or install computers, word processing systems, automated teller machines, and electronic office machines, such as duplicating and fax machines.

children.name: Radio and Telecommunications Equipment Installers and Repairers
children.description: Install and maintain radio or telecommunications equipment (cell towers, broadcast transmitters, etc.). Diagnose signal issues, update equipment, and perform routine inspections.

children.name: Radio, Cellular, and Tower Equipment Installers and Repairers
children.description: Repair, install, or maintain mobile or stationary radio transmitting, broadcasting, and receiving equipment, and two-way radio communications systems used in cellular telecommunications, mobile broadband, ship-to-shore, aircraft-to-ground communications, and radio equipment in service and emergency vehicles. May test and analyze network coverage.

children.name: Radio Mechanics
children.description: Test or repair mobile or stationary radio transmitting and receiving equipment and two-way radio communications systems used in ship-to-shore communications and found in service and emergency vehicles.

children.name: Telecommunications Equipment Installers and Repairers, Except Line Installers
children.description: Install, set up, rearrange, or remove switching, distribution, routing, and dialing equipment used in central offices or headends. Service or repair telephone, cable television, Internet, and other communications equipment on customers' property. May install communications equipment or communications wiring in buildings.

children.name: Miscellaneous Electrical and Electronic Equipment Mechanics, Installers, and Repairers
children.description: Service and repair a wide range of electrical or electronic devices not classified under standard categories. Could include security systems, AV equipment, or specialized industrial gear.

children.name: Avionics Technicians
children.description: Install, inspect, test, adjust, or repair avionics equipment, such as radar, radio, navigation, and missile control systems in aircraft or space vehicles.

children.name: Electric Motor, Power Tool, and Related Repairers
children.description: Repair, maintain, or install electric motors, wiring, or switches.

children.name: Electrical and Electronics Installers and Repairers, Transportation Equipment
children.description: Install, adjust, or maintain mobile electronics communication equipment, including sound, sonar, security, navigation, and surveillance systems on trains, watercraft, or other mobile equipment.

children.name: Electrical and Electronics Repairers, Commercial and Industrial Equipment
children.description: Repair, test, adjust, or install electronic equipment, such as industrial controls, transmitters, and antennas.

children.name: Electrical and Electronics Repairers, Powerhouse, Substation, and Relay
children.description: Inspect, test, repair, or maintain electrical equipment in generating stations, substations, and in-service relays.

children.name: Electronic Equipment Installers and Repairers, Motor Vehicles
children.description: Install, diagnose, or repair communications, sound, security, or navigation equipment in motor vehicles.

children.name: Audiovisual Equipment Installers and Repairers
children.description: Install, repair, or adjust audio or television receivers, stereo systems, camcorders, video systems, or other electronic entertainment equipment in homes or other venues. May perform routine maintenance.

children.name: Security and Fire Alarm Systems Installers
children.description: Install, program, maintain, and repair security and fire alarm wiring and equipment. Ensure that work is in accordance with relevant codes.

children.name: Vehicle and Mobile Equipment Mechanics, Installers, and Repairers
children.description: This category includes workers who repair, maintain, and install various types of vehicles and mobile equipment, such as cars, trucks, motorcycles, aircraft, boats, and industrial equipment. They are responsible for diagnosing mechanical issues, performing repairs and replacements, conducting regular maintenance, and ensuring vehicles and equipment are in safe working condition.

children.name: Aircraft Mechanics and Service Technicians
children.description: Diagnose, adjust, repair, or overhaul aircraft engines and assemblies. Perform routine inspections, maintain logbooks, and comply with FAA regulations.

children.name: Aircraft Mechanics and Service Technicians
children.description: Diagnose, adjust, repair, or overhaul aircraft engines and assemblies, such as hydraulic and pneumatic systems.

children.name: Automotive Technicians and Repairers
children.description: Inspect, maintain, and repair cars or light trucks. Diagnose problems using computerized equipment, replace parts, and test vehicles for performance and safety.

children.name: Automotive Body and Related Repairers
children.description: Repair and refinish automotive vehicle bodies and straighten vehicle frames.

children.name: Automotive Glass Installers and Repairers
children.description: Replace or repair broken windshields and window glass in motor vehicles.

children.name: Automotive Service Technicians and Mechanics
children.description: Diagnose, adjust, repair, or overhaul automotive vehicles.

children.name: Automotive Master Mechanics
children.description: Repair automobiles, trucks, buses, and other vehicles. Master mechanics repair virtually any part on the vehicle or specialize in the transmission system.

children.name: Automotive Specialty Technicians
children.description: Repair only one system or component on a vehicle, such as brakes, suspension, or radiator.

children.name: Bus and Truck Mechanics and Diesel Engine Specialists
children.description: Repair and maintain buses, trucks, or other diesel-powered vehicles. Perform engine diagnostics, replace faulty components, and ensure vehicles meet regulations.

children.name: Bus and Truck Mechanics and Diesel Engine Specialists
children.description: Diagnose, adjust, repair, or overhaul buses and trucks, or maintain and repair any type of diesel engines. Includes mechanics working primarily with automobile or marine diesel engines.

children.name: Heavy Vehicle and Mobile Equipment Service Technicians and Mechanics
children.description: Service and repair heavy machinery used in construction, farming, or rail transport. Troubleshoot mechanical or electrical issues, replace parts, and confirm safe operation.

children.name: Farm Equipment Mechanics and Service Technicians
children.description: Diagnose, adjust, repair, or overhaul farm machinery and vehicles, such as tractors, harvesters, dairy equipment, and irrigation systems.

children.name: Mobile Heavy Equipment Mechanics, Except Engines
children.description: Diagnose, adjust, repair, or overhaul mobile mechanical, hydraulic, and pneumatic equipment, such as cranes, bulldozers, graders, and conveyors, used in construction, logging, and mining.

children.name: Rail Car Repairers
children.description: Diagnose, adjust, repair, or overhaul railroad rolling stock, mine cars, or mass transit rail cars.

children.name: Small Engine Mechanics
children.description: Repair and service engines in lawnmowers, motorcycles, motorboats, or other small engine equipment. Identify problems, test, and replace worn parts.

children.name: Motorboat Mechanics and Service Technicians
children.description: Repair and adjust electrical and mechanical equipment of inboard or inboard-outboard boat engines.

children.name: Motorcycle Mechanics
children.description: Diagnose, adjust, repair, or overhaul motorcycles, scooters, mopeds, dirt bikes, or similar motorized vehicles.

children.name: Outdoor Power Equipment and Other Small Engine Mechanics
children.description: Diagnose, adjust, repair, or overhaul small engines used to power lawn mowers, chain saws, recreational sporting equipment, and related equipment.

children.name: Miscellaneous Vehicle and Mobile Equipment Mechanics, Installers, and Repairers
children.description: Handle vehicle or mobile equipment maintenance tasks not included under other categories. May service specialized machinery, like locomotives or farm equipment.

children.name: Bicycle Repairers
children.description: Repair and service bicycles.

children.name: Recreational Vehicle Service Technicians
children.description: Diagnose, inspect, adjust, repair, or overhaul recreational vehicles including travel trailers. May specialize in maintaining gas, electrical, hydraulic, plumbing, or chassis/towing systems as well as repairing generators, appliances, and interior components. Includes workers who perform customized van conversions.

children.name: Tire Repairers and Changers
children.description: Repair and replace tires.

children.name: Other Installation, Maintenance, and Repair Occupations
children.description: This category includes a wide range of workers involved in installation, maintenance, and repair activities across various industries. It encompasses occupations that are not classified under more specific categories but still contribute to the maintenance and functioning of equipment, machinery, and infrastructure. Examples of occupations in this category may include industrial machinery mechanics, commercial divers, signal and track switch repairers, and locksmiths.

children.name: Control and Valve Installers and Repairers
children.description: Install or repair mechanical regulating devices like valves, governors, or traps that control flow of gases or liquids in pipelines or mains.

children.name: Mechanical Door Repairers
children.description: Install, service, or repair automatic door mechanisms and hydraulic doors. Includes garage door mechanics.

children.name: Control and Valve Installers and Repairers, Except Mechanical Door
children.description: Install, repair, and maintain mechanical regulating and controlling devices, such as electric meters, gas regulators, thermostats, safety and flow valves, and other mechanical governors.

children.name: Heating, Air Conditioning, and Refrigeration Mechanics and Installers
children.description: Install, maintain, and repair heating, ventilation, air conditioning, and refrigeration systems. Test for leaks, connect wiring, and comply with HVAC codes.

children.name: Heating, Air Conditioning, and Refrigeration Mechanics and Installers
children.description: Install or repair heating, central air conditioning, HVAC, or refrigeration systems, including oil burners, hot-air furnaces, and heating stoves.

children.name: Heating and Air Conditioning Mechanics and Installers
children.description: Install, service, or repair heating and air conditioning systems in residences or commercial establishments.

children.name: Refrigeration Mechanics and Installers
children.description: Install and repair industrial and commercial refrigerating systems.

children.name: Home Appliance Repairers
children.description: Diagnose and fix problems with household appliances—like washers, ovens, or refrigerators. Disassemble units, replace parts, and reassemble to working condition.

children.name: Home Appliance Repairers
children.description: Repair, adjust, or install all types of electric or gas household appliances, such as refrigerators, washers, dryers, and ovens.

children.name: Industrial Machinery Installation, Repair, and Maintenance Workers
children.description: Maintain and repair factory equipment or industrial machinery. Perform preventative maintenance, troubleshoot failures, and ensure machinery is safe and efficient.

children.name: Industrial Machinery Mechanics
children.description: Repair, install, adjust, or maintain industrial production and processing machinery or refinery and pipeline distribution systems. May also install, dismantle, or move machinery and heavy equipment according to plans.

children.name: Maintenance Workers, Machinery
children.description: Lubricate machinery, change parts, or perform other routine machinery maintenance.

children.name: Millwrights
children.description: Install, dismantle, or move machinery and heavy equipment according to layout plans, blueprints, or other drawings.

children.name: Refractory Materials Repairers, Except Brickmasons
children.description: Build or repair equipment such as furnaces, kilns, cupolas, boilers, converters, ladles, soaking pits, and ovens, using refractory materials.

children.name: Line Installers and Repairers
children.description: Install and maintain electrical, telecommunications, or cable lines. Climb poles, use testing equipment, and ensure continuity of service.
