children.name: Electrical Power-Line Installers and Repairers
children.description: Install or repair cables or wires used in electrical power or distribution systems. May erect poles and light or heavy duty transmission towers.

children.name: Telecommunications Line Installers and Repairers
children.description: Install and repair telecommunications cable, including fiber optics.

children.name: Precision Instrument and Equipment Repairers
children.description: Calibrate, maintain, or repair specialized instruments like musical devices, medical equipment, or watch components. May use microscopes or other detailed precision tools.

children.name: Camera and Photographic Equipment Repairers
children.description: Repair and adjust cameras and photographic equipment, including commercial video and motion picture camera equipment.

children.name: Medical Equipment Repairers
children.description: Test, adjust, or repair biomedical or electromedical equipment.

children.name: Musical Instrument Repairers and Tuners
children.description: Repair percussion, stringed, reed, or wind instruments. May specialize in one area, such as piano tuning.

children.name: Watch and Clock Repairers
children.description: Repair, clean, and adjust mechanisms of timing instruments, such as watches and clocks. Includes watchmakers, watch technicians, and mechanical timepiece repairers.

children.name: Precision Instrument and Equipment Repairers, All Other
children.description: All precision instrument and equipment repairers not listed separately.

children.name: Maintenance and Repair Workers, General
children.description: Keep machines, mechanical equipment, or buildings in good working order. Perform minor electrical or plumbing repairs, basic carpentry, and routine facility maintenance.

children.name: Maintenance and Repair Workers, General
children.description: Perform work involving the skills of two or more maintenance or craft occupations to keep machines, mechanical equipment, or the structure of a building in repair. Duties may involve pipe fitting; HVAC maintenance; insulating; welding; machining; carpentry; repairing electrical or mechanical equipment; installing, aligning, and balancing new equipment; and repairing buildings, floors, or stairs.

children.name: Wind Turbine Service Technicians
children.description: Inspect, diagnose, and repair wind turbines. Climb turbine towers, troubleshoot electrical or mechanical failures, and ensure safety protocols are followed.

children.name: Wind Turbine Service Technicians
children.description: Inspect, diagnose, adjust, or repair wind turbines. Perform maintenance on wind turbine equipment including resolving electrical, mechanical, and hydraulic malfunctions.

children.name: Miscellaneous Installation, Maintenance, and Repair Workers
children.description: Perform installation or repair tasks not falling under standard categories, possibly including locksmiths, riggers, or maintenance workers in specialized environments.

children.name: Coin, Vending, and Amusement Machine Servicers and Repairers
children.description: Install, service, adjust, or repair coin, vending, or amusement machines including video games, juke boxes, pinball machines, or slot machines.

children.name: Commercial Divers
children.description: Work below surface of water, using surface-supplied air or scuba equipment to inspect, repair, remove, or install equipment and structures. May use a variety of power and hand tools, such as drills, sledgehammers, torches, and welding equipment. May conduct tests or experiments, rig explosives, or photograph structures or marine life.

children.name: Fabric Menders, Except Garment
children.description: Repair tears, holes, and other defects in fabrics, such as draperies, linens, parachutes, and tents.

children.name: Locksmiths and Safe Repairers
children.description: Repair and open locks, make keys, change locks and safe combinations, and install and repair safes.

children.name: Manufactured Building and Mobile Home Installers
children.description: Move or install mobile homes or prefabricated buildings.

children.name: Riggers
children.description: Set up or repair rigging for construction projects, manufacturing plants, logging yards, ships and shipyards, or for the entertainment industry.

children.name: Signal and Track Switch Repairers
children.description: Install, inspect, test, maintain, or repair electric gate crossings, signals, signal equipment, track switches, section lines, or intercommunications systems within a railroad system.

children.name: Helpers--Installation, Maintenance, and Repair Workers
children.description: Help installation, maintenance, and repair workers in maintenance, parts replacement, and repair of vehicles, industrial machinery, and electrical and electronic equipment. Perform duties such as furnishing tools, materials, and supplies to other workers; cleaning work area, machines, and tools; and holding materials or tools for other workers.

children.name: Installation, Maintenance, and Repair Workers, All Other
children.description: All installation, maintenance, and repair workers not listed separately.

children.name: Geothermal Technicians
children.description: Perform technical activities at power plants or individual installations necessary for the generation of power from geothermal energy sources. Monitor and control operating activities at geothermal power generation facilities and perform maintenance and repairs as necessary. Install, test, and maintain residential and commercial geothermal heat pumps.

name: Production Occupations
description: Involve manufacturing and processing goods. Workers operate machinery, assemble products, inspect output, and ensure quality in industries such as food processing, metal fabrication, and electronics.

children.name: Supervisors of Production Workers
children.description: This category includes supervisors who oversee and coordinate the activities of production workers in various industries. They are responsible for ensuring the efficient operation of production processes, maintaining quality standards, and managing the workforce. Supervisors in this category may work in manufacturing plants, factories, or production facilities across different sectors.

children.name: First-Line Supervisors of Production and Operating Workers
children.description: Oversee and coordinate the operations of production workers in manufacturing plants. Schedule tasks, monitor workflow, and meet production goals.

children.name: First-Line Supervisors of Production and Operating Workers
children.description: Directly supervise and coordinate the activities of production and operating workers, such as inspectors, precision workers, machine setters and operators, assemblers, fabricators, and plant and system operators. Excludes team or work leaders.

children.name: Assemblers and Fabricators
children.description: Assemblers and Fabricators are responsible for assembling and constructing various products and components. They work in industries such as manufacturing, electronics, automotive, and aerospace, where they use tools, machines, and manual labor to assemble parts, perform quality control, and ensure products meet specifications.

children.name: Aircraft Structure, Surfaces, Rigging, and Systems Assemblers
children.description: Assemble, fit, and install parts of aircraft frames, control systems, or surfaces. Use hand tools, read blueprints, and inspect finished components for accuracy.

children.name: Aircraft Structure, Surfaces, Rigging, and Systems Assemblers
children.description: Assemble, fit, fasten, and install parts of airplanes, space vehicles, or missiles, such as tails, wings, fuselage, bulkheads, stabilizers, landing gear, rigging and control equipment, or heating and ventilating systems.

children.name: Electrical, Electronics, and Electromechanical Assemblers
children.description: Assemble or modify electrical or electronic equipment. May connect wires, mount components, or solder parts onto circuit boards.

children.name: Coil Winders, Tapers, and Finishers
children.description: Wind wire coils used in electrical components, such as resistors and transformers, and in electrical equipment and instruments, such as field cores, bobbins, armature cores, electrical motors, generators, and control equipment.

children.name: Electrical and Electronic Equipment Assemblers
children.description: Assemble or modify electrical or electronic equipment, such as computers, test equipment telemetering systems, electric motors, and batteries.

children.name: Electromechanical Equipment Assemblers
children.description: Assemble or modify electromechanical equipment or devices, such as servomechanisms, gyros, dynamometers, magnetic drums, tape drives, brakes, control linkage, actuators, and appliances.

children.name: Engine and Other Machine Assemblers
children.description: Construct, fit, or assemble engines or machinery for vehicles, generators, or industrial equipment. Follow technical diagrams and test final products.

children.name: Engine and Other Machine Assemblers
children.description: Construct, assemble, or rebuild machines, such as engines, turbines, and similar equipment used in such industries as construction, extraction, textiles, and paper manufacturing.

children.name: Structural Metal Fabricators and Fitters
children.description: Fabricate, position, align, and fit metal parts to form structural frameworks. Weld, bolt, or rivet sections, and measure for accuracy.

children.name: Structural Metal Fabricators and Fitters
children.description: Fabricate, position, align, and fit parts of structural metal products.

children.name: Miscellaneous Assemblers and Fabricators
children.description: Combine parts or pieces to form products in manufacturing not categorized under other assembler/fabricator roles. May involve operating machines or using hand tools.

children.name: Fiberglass Laminators and Fabricators
children.description: Laminate layers of fiberglass on molds to form boat decks and hulls, bodies for golf carts, automobiles, or other products.

children.name: Team Assemblers
children.description: Work as part of a team having responsibility for assembling an entire product or component of a product. Team assemblers can perform all tasks conducted by the team in the assembly process and rotate through all or most of them, rather than being assigned to a specific task on a permanent basis. May participate in making management decisions affecting the work. Includes team leaders who work as part of the team.

children.name: Timing Device Assemblers and Adjusters
children.description: Perform precision assembling, adjusting, or calibrating, within narrow tolerances, of timing devices such as digital clocks or timing devices with electrical or electronic components.

children.name: Assemblers and Fabricators, All Other
children.description: All assemblers and fabricators not listed separately.

children.name: Food Processing Workers
children.description: Food Processing Workers are involved in various tasks related to the processing, packaging, and preparation of food products. They work in food processing plants, factories, and facilities where they handle ingredients, operate machinery, monitor production processes, and ensure food safety and quality standards are met.

children.name: Bakers
children.description: Mix and prepare dough, shape and bake bread, pastries, or other baked goods. Adhere to recipes, maintain cleanliness, and meet food safety standards.

children.name: Bakers
children.description: Mix and bake ingredients to produce breads, rolls, cookies, cakes, pies, pastries, or other baked goods.

children.name: Butchers and Other Meat, Poultry, and Fish Processing Workers
children.description: Slaughter, cut, trim, or prepare meat for sale or further processing. Follow sanitation standards and use specialized cutting equipment.

children.name: Butchers and Meat Cutters
children.description: Cut, trim, or prepare consumer-sized portions of meat for use or sale in retail establishments.

children.name: Meat, Poultry, and Fish Cutters and Trimmers
children.description: Use hands or hand tools to perform routine cutting and trimming of meat, poultry, and seafood.

children.name: Slaughterers and Meat Packers
children.description: Perform nonroutine or precision functions involving the preparation of large portions of meat. Work may include specialized slaughtering tasks, cutting standard or premium cuts of meat for marketing, making sausage, or wrapping meats. Work typically occurs in slaughtering, meat packing, or wholesale establishments.

children.name: Miscellaneous Food Processing Workers
children.description: Perform food processing tasks not classified under other specific occupations. May include dehydrating, canning, or specialized packaging.

children.name: Food and Tobacco Roasting, Baking, and Drying Machine Operators and Tenders
children.description: Operate or tend food or tobacco roasting, baking, or drying equipment, including hearth ovens, kiln driers, roasters, char kilns, and vacuum drying equipment.

children.name: Food Batchmakers
children.description: Set up and operate equipment that mixes or blends ingredients used in the manufacturing of food products. Includes candy makers and cheese makers.

children.name: Food Cooking Machine Operators and Tenders
children.description: Operate or tend cooking equipment, such as steam cooking vats, deep fry cookers, pressure cookers, kettles, and boilers, to prepare food products.

children.name: Food Processing Workers, All Other
children.description: All food processing workers not listed separately.

children.name: Metal Workers and Plastic Workers
children.description: Metal Workers and Plastic Workers include a range of occupations involved in working with metal and plastic materials. This category encompasses various roles such as metal fabricators, welders, machinists, tool and die makers, plastic molders, and extrusion operators. These workers use specialized tools, machines, and techniques to shape, join, and finish metal and plastic materials for various applications in industries such as manufacturing, construction, and automotive.

children.name: Computer Control Programmers and Operators
children.description: Develop or operate computer-controlled machines or robots to perform machining or processing tasks on metal or plastic. Troubleshoot code or mechanical issues.

children.name: Computer-Controlled Machine Tool Operators, Metal and Plastic
children.description: Operate computer-controlled machines or robots to perform one or more machine functions on metal or plastic work pieces.

children.name: Computer Numerically Controlled Machine Tool Programmers, Metal and Plastic
children.description: Develop programs to control machining or processing of metal or plastic parts by automatic machine tools, equipment, or systems.

children.name: Forming Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders, Metal and Plastic
children.description: Operate or set up machines that shape or form metal or plastic materials. Monitor processes, adjust speeds, and inspect finished parts for compliance.

children.name: Extruding and Drawing Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders, Metal and Plastic
children.description: Set up, operate, or tend machines to extrude or draw thermoplastic or metal materials into tubes, rods, hoses, wire, bars, or structural shapes.

children.name: Forging Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders, Metal and Plastic
children.description: Set up, operate, or tend forging machines to taper, shape, or form metal or plastic parts.

children.name: Rolling Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders, Metal and Plastic
children.description: Set up, operate, or tend machines to roll steel or plastic forming bends, beads, knurls, rolls, or plate, or to flatten, temper, or reduce gauge of material.

children.name: Machine Tool Cutting Setters, Operators, and Tenders, Metal and Plastic
children.description: Set up or operate machine tools like lathes, milling machines, or grinders to shape metal or plastic parts. Inspect products for precision and follow safety guidelines.

children.name: Cutting, Punching, and Press Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders, Metal and Plastic
children.description: Set up, operate, or tend machines to saw, cut, shear, slit, punch, crimp, notch, bend, or straighten metal or plastic material.

children.name: Drilling and Boring Machine Tool Setters, Operators, and Tenders, Metal and Plastic
children.description: Set up, operate, or tend drilling machines to drill, bore, ream, mill, or countersink metal or plastic work pieces.

children.name: Grinding, Lapping, Polishing, and Buffing Machine Tool Setters, Operators, and Tenders, Metal and Plastic
children.description: Set up, operate, or tend grinding and related tools that remove excess material or burrs from surfaces, sharpen edges or corners, or buff, hone, or polish metal or plastic work pieces.

children.name: Lathe and Turning Machine Tool Setters, Operators, and Tenders, Metal and Plastic
children.description: Set up, operate, or tend lathe and turning machines to turn, bore, thread, form, or face metal or plastic materials, such as wire, rod, or bar stock.

children.name: Milling and Planing Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders, Metal and Plastic
children.description: Set up, operate, or tend milling or planing machines to mill, plane, shape, groove, or profile metal or plastic work pieces.

children.name: Machinists
children.description: Set up and operate a variety of machine tools to produce precision parts. Interpret blueprints, measure tolerances, and maintain equipment.

children.name: Machinists
children.description: Set up and operate a variety of machine tools to produce precision parts and instruments out of metal. Includes precision instrument makers who fabricate, modify, or repair mechanical instruments. May also fabricate and modify parts to make or repair machine tools or maintain industrial machines, applying knowledge of mechanics, mathematics, metal properties, layout, and machining procedures.

children.name: Metal Furnace Operators, Tenders, Pourers, and Casters
children.description: Operate furnaces to melt or refine metal before casting. Control temperature, pour molten metal, and oversee cooling and shaping.

children.name: Metal-Refining Furnace Operators and Tenders
children.description: Operate or tend furnaces, such as gas, oil, coal, electric-arc or electric induction, open-hearth, or oxygen furnaces, to melt and refine metal before casting or to produce specified types of steel.

children.name: Pourers and Casters, Metal
children.description: Operate hand-controlled mechanisms to pour and regulate the flow of molten metal into molds to produce castings or ingots.

children.name: Model Makers and Patternmakers, Metal and Plastic
children.description: Create or adapt prototypes, patterns, and models used in metal or plastic manufacturing. Use precision tools and computer-aided design (CAD) for complex shapes.

children.name: Model Makers, Metal and Plastic
children.description: Set up and operate machines, such as lathes, milling and engraving machines, and jig borers to make working models of metal or plastic objects. Includes template makers.

children.name: Patternmakers, Metal and Plastic
children.description: Lay out, machine, fit, and assemble castings and parts to metal or plastic foundry patterns, core boxes, or match plates.

children.name: Molders and Molding Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders, Metal and Plastic
children.description: Operate equipment to form metal or plastic into desired shapes. Prepare molds, regulate temperatures, and monitor production for defects.

children.name: Foundry Mold and Coremakers
children.description: Make or form wax or sand cores or molds used in the production of metal castings in foundries.

children.name: Molding, Coremaking, and Casting Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders, Metal and Plastic
children.description: Set up, operate, or tend metal or plastic molding, casting, or coremaking machines to mold or cast metal or thermoplastic parts or products.

children.name: Multiple Machine Tool Setters, Operators, and Tenders, Metal and Plastic
children.description: Set up, operate, or tend more than one type of cutting or forming machine tool. Switch between machines to maintain throughput, ensuring quality and consistency.

children.name: Multiple Machine Tool Setters, Operators, and Tenders, Metal and Plastic
children.description: Set up, operate, or tend more than one type of cutting or forming machine tool or robot.

children.name: Tool and Die Makers
children.description: Produce and repair dies, jigs, fixtures, or specialized tools used in manufacturing. Use precision instruments and follow engineering specifications.

children.name: Tool and Die Makers
children.description: Analyze specifications, lay out metal stock, set up and operate machine tools, and fit and assemble parts to make and repair dies, cutting tools, jigs, fixtures, gauges, and machinists' hand tools.

children.name: Welding, Soldering, and Brazing Workers
children.description: Join metal parts together or repair them using welding, soldering, or brazing equipment. Inspect welds, maintain equipment, and follow safety measures.

children.name: Welders, Cutters, Solderers, and Brazers
children.description: Use hand-welding, flame-cutting, hand-soldering, or brazing equipment to weld or join metal components or to fill holes, indentations, or seams of fabricated metal products.

children.name: Welders, Cutters, and Welder Fitters
children.description: Use hand-welding or flame-cutting equipment to weld or join metal components or to fill holes, indentations, or seams of fabricated metal products.

children.name: Solderers and Brazers
children.description: Braze or solder together components to assemble fabricated metal parts, using soldering iron, torch, or welding machine and flux.

children.name: Welding, Soldering, and Brazing Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders
children.description: Set up, operate, or tend welding, soldering, or brazing machines or robots that weld, braze, solder, or heat treat metal products, components, or assemblies. Includes workers who operate laser cutters or laser-beam machines.

children.name: Miscellaneous Metal Workers and Plastic Workers
children.description: Carry out metal- or plastic-working processes not specifically classified under other job titles. May include finishing, polishing, or specialized shaping tasks.

children.name: Heat Treating Equipment Setters, Operators, and Tenders, Metal and Plastic
children.description: Set up, operate, or tend heating equipment, such as heat-treating furnaces, flame-hardening machines, induction machines, soaking pits, or vacuum equipment to temper, harden, anneal, or heat treat metal or plastic objects.

children.name: Layout Workers, Metal and Plastic
children.description: Lay out reference points and dimensions on metal or plastic stock or workpieces, such as sheets, plates, tubes, structural shapes, castings, or machine parts, for further processing. Includes shipfitters.

children.name: Plating Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders, Metal and Plastic
children.description: Set up, operate, or tend plating machines to coat metal or plastic products with chromium, zinc, copper, cadmium, nickel, or other metal to protect or decorate surfaces. Typically, the product being coated is immersed in molten metal or an electrolytic solution.

children.name: Tool Grinders, Filers, and Sharpeners
children.description: Perform precision smoothing, sharpening, polishing, or grinding of metal objects.

children.name: Metal Workers and Plastic Workers, All Other
children.description: All metal workers and plastic workers not listed separately.

children.name: Printing Workers
children.description: Printing Workers are involved in various tasks related to the printing industry, including operating printing presses, preparing materials for printing, performing quality checks, and maintaining printing equipment. This category encompasses roles such as prepress technicians, press operators, bindery workers, and finishing workers. Printing workers may be employed in commercial printing companies, publishing houses, packaging companies, or specialized printing shops.

children.name: Printing Workers
children.description: Operate and maintain printing presses or digital printing equipment, set up print jobs, and handle tasks like color management, binding, and finishing.

children.name: Prepress Technicians and Workers
children.description: Format and proof text and images submitted by designers and clients into finished pages that can be printed. Includes digital and photo typesetting. May produce printing plates.

children.name: Printing Press Operators
children.description: Set up and operate digital, letterpress, lithographic, flexographic, gravure, or other printing machines. Includes short-run offset printing presses.

children.name: Print Binding and Finishing Workers
children.description: Bind books and other publications or finish printed products by hand or machine. May set up binding and finishing machines.

children.name: Textile, Apparel, and Furnishings Workers
children.description: Occupations within the category "51-6000 Textile, Apparel, and Furnishings Workers" typically involve various processes related to the production of clothing, textiles, and furnishings. This includes but is not limited to sewing, upholstering, tailoring, and weaving.

children.name: Laundry and Dry-Cleaning Workers
children.description: Operate washing or dry-cleaning machines to clean garments or other articles. Sort items, treat stains, and press or fold finished laundry.

children.name: Laundry and Dry-Cleaning Workers
children.description: Operate or tend washing or dry-cleaning machines to wash or dry-clean industrial or household articles, such as cloth garments, suede, leather, furs, blankets, draperies, linens, rugs, and carpets. Includes spotters and dyers of these articles.

children.name: Pressers, Textile, Garment, and Related Materials
children.description: Press or shape garments using hand irons or pressing machines. Smooth or finish fabrics for sale or further processing.

children.name: Pressers, Textile, Garment, and Related Materials
children.description: Press or shape articles by hand or machine.

children.name: Sewing Machine Operators
children.description: Operate sewing machines to stitch, join, or hem fabrics, garments, or non-garment items. Follow patterns and check finished seams.

children.name: Sewing Machine Operators
children.description: Operate or tend sewing machines to join, reinforce, decorate, or perform related sewing operations in the manufacture of garment or nongarment products.

children.name: Shoe and Leather Workers
children.description: Construct, decorate, or repair leather products such as shoes, handbags, or saddles. Cut, stitch, and finish materials following patterns or designs.

children.name: Shoe and Leather Workers and Repairers
children.description: Construct, decorate, or repair leather and leather-like products, such as luggage, shoes, and saddles. May use hand tools.

children.name: Shoe Machine Operators and Tenders
children.description: Operate or tend a variety of machines to join, decorate, reinforce, or finish shoes and shoe parts.

children.name: Tailors, Dressmakers, and Sewers
children.description: Customize or sew garments, measure clients, alter clothing, and design or repair various apparel items.

children.name: Sewers, Hand
children.description: Sew, join, reinforce, or finish, usually with needle and thread, a variety of manufactured items. Includes weavers and stitchers.

children.name: Tailors, Dressmakers, and Custom Sewers
children.description: Design, make, alter, repair, or fit garments.

children.name: Textile Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders
children.description: Operate machines that weave, knit, or otherwise process textiles. Monitor operations, handle thread or fabric changes, and clear machine jams.

children.name: Textile Bleaching and Dyeing Machine Operators and Tenders
children.description: Operate or tend machines to bleach, shrink, wash, dye, or finish textiles or synthetic or glass fibers.

children.name: Textile Cutting Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders
children.description: Set up, operate, or tend machines that cut textiles.

children.name: Textile Knitting and Weaving Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders
children.description: Set up, operate, or tend machines that knit, loop, weave, or draw in textiles.

children.name: Textile Winding, Twisting, and Drawing Out Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders
children.description: Set up, operate, or tend machines that wind or twist textiles; or draw out and combine sliver, such as wool, hemp, or synthetic fibers. Includes slubber machine and drawing frame operators.

children.name: Miscellaneous Textile, Apparel, and Furnishings Workers
children.description: Perform textile- or furnishings-related tasks not classified elsewhere, possibly involving specialized finishing, drapery work, or craft-based textile production.

children.name: Extruding and Forming Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders, Synthetic and Glass Fibers
children.description: Set up, operate, or tend machines that extrude and form continuous filaments from synthetic materials, such as liquid polymer, rayon, and fiberglass.

children.name: Fabric and Apparel Patternmakers
children.description: Draw and construct sets of precision master fabric patterns or layouts. May also mark and cut fabrics and apparel.

children.name: Upholsterers
children.description: Make, repair, or replace upholstery for household furniture or transportation vehicles.

children.name: Textile, Apparel, and Furnishings Workers, All Other
children.description: All textile, apparel, and furnishings workers not listed separately.

children.name: Woodworkers
children.description: The "51-7000 Woodworkers" occupational category typically includes jobs that involve working with wood to create various types of products. This can range from furniture to musical instruments and more.

children.name: Cabinetmakers and Bench Carpenters
children.description: Build and repair wooden cabinets, furniture, or fixtures. Read blueprints, measure and cut wood, assemble components, and finish surfaces.

children.name: Cabinetmakers and Bench Carpenters
children.description: Cut, shape, and assemble wooden articles or set up and operate a variety of woodworking machines, such as power saws, jointers, and mortisers to surface, cut, or shape lumber or to fabricate parts for wood products.

children.name: Furniture Finishers
children.description: Shape, finish, or refinish new or repaired furniture. Remove old finishes, apply stains or sealers, and polish surfaces for desired appearance.

children.name: Furniture Finishers
children.description: Shape, finish, and refinish damaged, worn, or used furniture or new high-grade furniture to specified color or finish.

children.name: Model Makers and Patternmakers, Wood
children.description: Plan, lay out, and construct wooden precision models or patterns for use in manufacturing. Operate tools and machinery to shape wood according to specs.

children.name: Model Makers, Wood
children.description: Construct full-size and scale wooden precision models of products. Includes wood jig builders and loft workers.

children.name: Patternmakers, Wood
children.description: Plan, lay out, and construct wooden unit or sectional patterns used in forming sand molds for castings.

children.name: Woodworking Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders
children.description: Set up and operate machines such as saws, molders, or sanders to cut and shape wood. Monitor operation, adjust settings, and ensure correct dimensions.

children.name: Sawing Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders, Wood
children.description: Set up, operate, or tend wood sawing machines. May operate computer numerically controlled (CNC) equipment. Includes lead sawyers.

children.name: Woodworking Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders, Except Sawing
children.description: Set up, operate, or tend woodworking machines, such as drill presses, lathes, shapers, routers, sanders, planers, and wood nailing machines. May operate computer numerically controlled (CNC) equipment.

children.name: Miscellaneous Woodworkers
children.description: Perform specialized or various woodworking duties not specified under other job titles, potentially including custom carving, lathe work, or wood pattern finishing.

children.name: Woodworkers, All Other
children.description: All woodworkers not listed separately.

children.name: Plant and System Operators
children.description: The "51-8000 Plant and System Operators" occupational category typically involves jobs that control and operate industrial plants or systems, such as power plants, water treatment facilities, or chemical processing plants.

children.name: Power Plant Operators, Distributors, and Dispatchers
children.description: Control or operate machinery that generates electric power. Monitor instruments, regulate power flows, and manage distribution to meet demand.

children.name: Nuclear Power Reactor Operators
children.description: Operate or control nuclear reactors. Move control rods, start and stop equipment, monitor and adjust controls, and record data in logs. Implement emergency procedures when needed. May respond to abnormalities, determine cause, and recommend corrective action.

children.name: Power Distributors and Dispatchers
children.description: Coordinate, regulate, or distribute electricity or steam.

children.name: Power Plant Operators
children.description: Control, operate, or maintain machinery to generate electric power. Includes auxiliary equipment operators.

children.name: Stationary Engineers and Boiler Operators
children.description: Operate and maintain stationary engines, boilers, or other mechanical equipment. Adjust controls, perform inspections, and ensure safe pressure and temperature levels.

children.name: Stationary Engineers and Boiler Operators
children.description: Operate or maintain stationary engines, boilers, or other mechanical equipment to provide utilities for buildings or industrial processes. Operate equipment such as steam engines, generators, motors, turbines, and steam boilers.

children.name: Water and Wastewater Treatment Plant and System Operators
children.description: Run or control treatment processes to purify water or treat sewage. Monitor operating conditions, record test results, and adjust equipment to meet standards.

children.name: Water and Wastewater Treatment Plant and System Operators
children.description: Operate or control an entire process or system of machines, often through the use of control boards, to transfer or treat water or wastewater.

children.name: Miscellaneous Plant and System Operators
children.description: Oversee or operate specialized plant systems not under other classifications—e.g., nuclear reactor operators or specific chemical processing systems.

children.name: Chemical Plant and System Operators
children.description: Control or operate entire chemical processes or system of machines.

children.name: Gas Plant Operators
children.description: Distribute or process gas for utility companies and others by controlling compressors to maintain specified pressures on main pipelines.

children.name: Petroleum Pump System Operators, Refinery Operators, and Gaugers
children.description: Operate or control petroleum refining or processing units. May specialize in controlling manifold and pumping systems, gauging or testing oil in storage tanks, or regulating the flow of oil into pipelines.

children.name: Plant and System Operators, All Other
children.description: All plant and system operators not listed separately.

children.name: Biofuels Processing Technicians
children.description: Calculate, measure, load, mix, and process refined feedstock with additives in fermentation or reaction process vessels and monitor production process. Perform, and keep records of, plant maintenance, repairs, and safety inspections.

children.name: Methane/Landfill Gas Generation System Technicians
children.description: Monitor, operate, and maintain landfill gas collection system components and environmental monitoring and control systems.

children.name: Biomass Plant Technicians
children.description: Control and monitor biomass plant activities and perform maintenance as needed.

children.name: Hydroelectric Plant Technicians
children.description: Monitor and control activities associated with hydropower generation. Operate plant equipment, such as turbines, pumps, valves, gates, fans, electric control boards, and battery banks. Monitor equipment operation and performance and make necessary adjustments to ensure optimal performance. Perform equipment maintenance and repair as necessary.

children.name: Other Production Occupations
children.description: The category "51-9000 Other Production Occupations" involves a wide array of jobs that generally revolve around producing, processing, or preparing consumer goods in various industries, such as food processing, manufacturing, and more.

children.name: Chemical Processing Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders
children.description: Operate or tend equipment that processes chemicals. Observe gauges, take samples, and regulate flow, temperature, or pressure.

children.name: Chemical Equipment Operators and Tenders
children.description: Operate or tend equipment to control chemical changes or reactions in the processing of industrial or consumer products. Equipment used includes devulcanizers, steam-jacketed kettles, and reactor vessels.

children.name: Separating, Filtering, Clarifying, Precipitating, and Still Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders
children.description: Set up, operate, or tend continuous flow or vat-type equipment; filter presses; shaker screens; centrifuges; condenser tubes; precipitating, fermenting, or evaporating tanks; scrubbing towers; or batch stills. These machines extract, sort, or separate liquids, gases, or solids from other materials to recover a refined product. Includes dairy processing equipment operators.

children.name: Crushing, Grinding, Polishing, Mixing, and Blending Workers
children.description: Set up, operate, or tend machines that crush, grind, or blend materials (e.g., coal, glass, spices). Verify consistency and quality of output.

children.name: Crushing, Grinding, and Polishing Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders
children.description: Set up, operate, or tend machines to crush, grind, or polish materials, such as coal, glass, grain, stone, food, or rubber.

children.name: Grinding and Polishing Workers, Hand
children.description: Grind, sand, or polish, using hand tools or hand-held power tools, a variety of metal, wood, stone, clay, plastic, or glass objects. Includes chippers, buffers, and finishers.

children.name: Mixing and Blending Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders
children.description: Set up, operate, or tend machines to mix or blend materials, such as chemicals, tobacco, liquids, color pigments, or explosive ingredients.

children.name: Cutting Workers
children.description: Use hand or machine cutters to trim, cut, or slice materials (fabric, paper, metal) for further processing. Follow patterns or templates.

children.name: Cutters and Trimmers, Hand
children.description: Use hand tools or hand-held power tools to cut and trim a variety of manufactured items, such as carpet, fabric, stone, glass, or rubber.

children.name: Cutting and Slicing Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders
children.description: Set up, operate, or tend machines that cut or slice materials, such as glass, stone, cork, rubber, tobacco, food, paper, or insulating material.

children.name: Extruding, Forming, Pressing, and Compacting Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders
children.description: Operate equipment that extrudes or forms materials such as clay, glass, or rubber into shapes. Adjust settings, remove finished products, and inspect for defects.

children.name: Extruding, Forming, Pressing, and Compacting Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders
children.description: Set up, operate, or tend machines, such as glass-forming machines, plodder machines, and tuber machines, to shape and form products such as glassware, food, rubber, soap, brick, tile, clay, wax, tobacco, or cosmetics.

children.name: Furnace, Kiln, Oven, Drier, and Kettle Operators and Tenders
children.description: Operate heating equipment used in manufacturing. Control temperature, feed raw materials, and monitor the process to ensure proper treatment or drying.

children.name: Furnace, Kiln, Oven, Drier, and Kettle Operators and Tenders
children.description: Operate or tend heating equipment other than basic metal, plastic, or food processing equipment. Includes activities such as annealing glass, drying lumber, curing rubber, removing moisture from materials, or boiling soap.

children.name: Inspectors, Testers, Sorters, Samplers, and Weighers
children.description: Examine products or materials for defects, measure weights, and ensure items meet specifications. Record findings and recommend adjustments.

children.name: Inspectors, Testers, Sorters, Samplers, and Weighers
children.description: Inspect, test, sort, sample, or weigh nonagricultural raw materials or processed, machined, fabricated, or assembled parts or products for defects, wear, and deviations from specifications. May use precision measuring instruments and complex test equipment.

children.name: Jewelers and Precious Stone and Metal Workers
children.description: Design, fabricate, adjust, or repair jewelry and precious metal pieces. Cut and set gemstones, solder metal parts, and polish final products.

children.name: Jewelers and Precious Stone and Metal Workers
children.description: Design, fabricate, adjust, repair, or appraise jewelry, gold, silver, other precious metals, or gems.

children.name: Jewelers
children.description: Fabricate and repair jewelry articles. Make models or molds to create jewelry items.

children.name: Gem and Diamond Workers
children.description: Fabricate, finish, or evaluate the quality of gems and diamonds used in jewelry or industrial tools.

children.name: Precious Metal Workers
children.description: Cast, anneal, solder, hammer, or shape gold, silver, pewter or other metals to form jewelry or other metal items such as goblets or candlesticks.

children.name: Medical, Dental, and Ophthalmic Laboratory Technicians
children.description: Construct, fit, or repair medical devices such as dentures, eyeglasses, or prosthetics. Use specialized machinery, molds, or measuring equipment.

children.name: Dental Laboratory Technicians
children.description: Construct and repair full or partial dentures or dental appliances.

children.name: Medical Appliance Technicians
children.description: Construct, maintain, or repair medical supportive devices such as braces, orthotics and prosthetic devices, joints, arch supports, and other surgical and medical appliances.

children.name: Ophthalmic Laboratory Technicians
children.description: Cut, grind, and polish eyeglasses, contact lenses, or other precision optical elements. Assemble and mount lenses into frames or process other optical elements. Includes precision lens polishers or grinders, centerer-edgers, and lens mounters.

children.name: Packaging and Filling Machine Operators and Tenders
children.description: Run machines that prepare and package products for shipping. Fill containers, seal packages, label items, and ensure quality control.

children.name: Packaging and Filling Machine Operators and Tenders
children.description: Operate or tend machines to prepare industrial or consumer products for storage or shipment. Includes cannery workers who pack food products.

children.name: Painting Workers
children.description: Paint or coat a variety of products, including vehicles, furniture, or machinery. May use spray guns, rollers, or brushes.

children.name: Coating, Painting, and Spraying Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders
children.description: Set up, operate, or tend machines to coat or paint any of a wide variety of products, including glassware, cloth, ceramics, metal, plastic, paper, or wood, with lacquer, silver, copper, rubber, varnish, glaze, enamel, oil, or rust-proofing materials.

children.name: Painters, Transportation Equipment
children.description: Operate or tend painting machines to paint surfaces of transportation equipment, such as automobiles, buses, trucks, trains, boats, and airplanes. Includes painters in auto body repair facilities.

children.name: Painting, Coating, and Decorating Workers
children.description: Paint, coat, or decorate articles, such as furniture, glass, plateware, pottery, jewelry, toys, books, or leather.

children.name: Semiconductor Processors
children.description: Perform tasks in the manufacturing of electronic semiconductors. Monitor equipment, measure chemical solutions, and inspect wafers for defects.

children.name: Semiconductor Processing Technicians
children.description: Perform any or all of the following functions in the manufacture of electronic semiconductors: load semiconductor material into furnace; saw formed ingots into segments; load individual segment into crystal growing chamber and monitor controls; locate crystal axis in ingot using x-ray equipment and saw ingots into wafers; and clean, polish, and load wafers into series of special purpose furnaces, chemical baths, and equipment used to form circuitry and change conductive properties.

children.name: Photographic Process Workers and Processing Machine Operators
children.description: Develop film or operate digital printing equipment. Adjust chemical mixes, maintain darkroom or digital lab equipment, and oversee final print quality.

children.name: Photographic Process Workers and Processing Machine Operators
children.description: Perform work involved in developing and processing photographic images from film or digital media. May perform precision tasks such as editing photographic negatives and prints.

children.name: Miscellaneous Production Workers
children.description: Engage in diverse production roles not classified under a specific category, such as tire builders, fabricated metal workers, or factory line positions handling specialized tasks.

children.name: Adhesive Bonding Machine Operators and Tenders
children.description: Operate or tend bonding machines that use adhesives to join items for further processing or to form a completed product. Processes include joining veneer sheets into plywood; gluing paper; or joining rubber and rubberized fabric parts, plastic, simulated leather, or other materials.

children.name: Cleaning, Washing, and Metal Pickling Equipment Operators and Tenders
children.description: Operate or tend machines to wash or clean products, such as barrels or kegs, glass items, tin plate, food, pulp, coal, plastic, or rubber, to remove impurities.

children.name: Cooling and Freezing Equipment Operators and Tenders
children.description: Operate or tend equipment such as cooling and freezing units, refrigerators, batch freezers, and freezing tunnels, to cool or freeze products, food, blood plasma, and chemicals.

children.name: Etchers and Engravers
children.description: Engrave or etch metal, wood, rubber, or other materials. Includes such workers as etcher-circuit processors, pantograph engravers, and silk screen etchers.

children.name: Molders, Shapers, and Casters, Except Metal and Plastic
children.description: Mold, shape, form, cast, or carve products such as food products, figurines, tile, pipes, and candles consisting of clay, glass, plaster, concrete, stone, or combinations of materials.

children.name: Stone Cutters and Carvers, Manufacturing
children.description: Cut or carve stone according to diagrams and patterns.

children.name: Glass Blowers, Molders, Benders, and Finishers
children.description: Shape molten glass according to patterns.

children.name: Potters, Manufacturing
children.description: Operate production machines such as pug mill, jigger machine, or potter's wheel to process clay in manufacture of ceramic, pottery and stoneware products.

children.name: Molding and Casting Workers
children.description: Perform a variety of duties such as mixing materials, assembling mold parts, filling molds, and stacking molds to mold and cast a wide range of products.

children.name: Paper Goods Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders
children.description: Set up, operate, or tend paper goods machines that perform a variety of functions, such as converting, sawing, corrugating, banding, wrapping, boxing, stitching, forming, or sealing paper or paperboard sheets into products.

children.name: Tire Builders
children.description: Operate machines to build tires.

children.name: Helpers--Production Workers
children.description: Help production workers by performing duties requiring less skill. Duties include supplying or holding materials or tools, and cleaning work area and equipment.

children.name: Production Workers, All Other
children.description: All production workers not listed separately.

children.name: Recycling and Reclamation Workers
children.description: Prepare and sort materials or products for recycling. Identify and remove hazardous substances. Dismantle components of products such as appliances.

children.name: Supervisors of Transportation and Material Moving Workers
children.description: The "53-1000 Supervisors of Transportation and Material Moving Workers" category includes occupations that involve the supervision of the transportation of goods and people, as well as the movement of materials within warehouses, storage yards, or construction sites.

children.name: Aircraft Cargo Handling Supervisors
children.description: Coordinate and supervise workers who load and unload aircraft cargo. Oversee cargo handling equipment, verify load weights, and ensure compliance with flight safety procedures.

children.name: Aircraft Cargo Handling Supervisors
children.description: Supervise and coordinate the activities of ground crew in the loading, unloading, securing, and staging of aircraft cargo or baggage. May determine the quantity and orientation of cargo and compute aircraft center of gravity. May accompany aircraft as member of flight crew and monitor and handle cargo in flight, and assist and brief passengers on safety and emergency procedures. Includes loadmasters.

children.name: First-Line Supervisors of Helpers, Laborers, and Material Movers, Hand
children.description: Direct and coordinate the activities of workers who move freight or stock by hand. Assign tasks, schedule shifts, and enforce safety protocols.

children.name: First-Line Supervisors of Helpers, Laborers, and Material Movers, Hand
children.description: Directly supervise and coordinate the activities of helpers, laborers, or material movers.

children.name: Recycling Coordinators
children.description: Supervise curbside and drop-off recycling programs for municipal governments or private firms.

children.name: First-Line Supervisors of Transportation and Material-Moving Machine and Vehicle Operators
children.description: Supervise and schedule machine or vehicle operators (e.g., crane, forklift, or truck drivers). Ensure correct loading, adherence to regulations, and on-time deliveries.

children.name: First-Line Supervisors of Transportation and Material-Moving Machine and Vehicle Operators
children.description: Directly supervise and coordinate activities of transportation and material-moving machine and vehicle operators and helpers.

children.name: Air Transportation Workers
children.description: The "53-2000 Air Transportation Workers" category encompasses a variety of occupations that deal with the operation and facilitation of air travel. This includes jobs such as pilots, flight attendants, and air traffic controllers, among others. Workers in this field typically require specialized training and certification due to the high level of responsibility and the technical knowledge required.

children.name: Aircraft Pilots and Flight Engineers
children.description: Fly and navigate airplanes or helicopters. Monitor instruments, communicate with air traffic control, and ensure passenger and aircraft safety.

children.name: Airline Pilots, Copilots, and Flight Engineers
children.description: Pilot and navigate the flight of fixed-wing aircraft, usually on scheduled air carrier routes, for the transport of passengers and cargo. Requires Federal Air Transport certificate and rating for specific aircraft type used. Includes regional, national, and international airline pilots and flight instructors of airline pilots.

children.name: Commercial Pilots
children.description: Pilot and navigate the flight of fixed-wing aircraft on nonscheduled air carrier routes, or helicopters. Requires Commercial Pilot certificate. Includes charter pilots with similar certification, and air ambulance and air tour pilots. Excludes regional, national, and international airline pilots.

children.name: Air Traffic Controllers and Airfield Operations Specialists
children.description: Coordinate safe takeoffs and landings of aircraft. Issue landing and takeoff instructions, manage runway traffic, and ensure minimal risks at airports.

children.name: Air Traffic Controllers
children.description: Control air traffic on and within vicinity of airport, and movement of air traffic between altitude sectors and control centers, according to established procedures and policies. Authorize, regulate, and control commercial airline flights according to government or company regulations to expedite and ensure flight safety.

children.name: Airfield Operations Specialists
children.description: Ensure the safe takeoff and landing of commercial and military aircraft. Duties include coordination between air-traffic control and maintenance personnel, dispatching, using airfield landing and navigational aids, implementing airfield safety procedures, monitoring and maintaining flight records, and applying knowledge of weather information.

children.name: Flight Attendants
children.description: Provide personal services to ensure the safety and comfort of airline passengers. Demonstrate emergency equipment usage, serve refreshments, and respond to passenger requests.

children.name: Flight Attendants
children.description: Monitor safety of the aircraft cabin. Provide services to airline passengers, explain safety information, serve food and beverages, and respond to emergency incidents.

children.name: Ambulance Drivers and Attendants, Except Emergency Medical Technicians
children.description: Drive ambulances to transport sick or injured persons. Follow instructions from dispatchers, assist paramedics as needed, and ensure safe transport to medical facilities.

children.name: Ambulance Drivers and Attendants, Except Emergency Medical Technicians
children.description: Drive ambulance or assist ambulance driver in transporting sick, injured, or convalescent persons. Assist in lifting patients.

children.name: Bus Drivers
children.description: Operate buses to transport passengers along scheduled routes or on chartered trips. Maintain schedules, collect fares, and comply with traffic laws and safety regulations.

children.name: Bus Drivers, Transit and Intercity
children.description: Drive bus or motor coach, including regular route operations, charters, and private carriage. May assist passengers with baggage. May collect fares or tickets.

children.name: Bus Drivers, School or Special Client
children.description: Transport students or special clients, such as the elderly or persons with disabilities. Ensure adherence to safety rules. May assist passengers in boarding or exiting.

children.name: Driver/Sales Workers and Truck Drivers
children.description: Transport goods or passengers, often operating large trucks or delivery vehicles. May also handle sales, load/unload cargo, track inventory, and ensure accurate deliveries.

children.name: Driver/Sales Workers
children.description: Drive truck or other vehicle over established routes or within an established territory and sell or deliver goods, such as food products, including restaurant take-out items, or pick up or deliver items such as commercial laundry. May also take orders, collect payment, or stock merchandise at point of delivery.

children.name: Heavy and Tractor-Trailer Truck Drivers
children.description: Drive a tractor-trailer combination or a truck with a capacity of at least 26,001 pounds Gross Vehicle Weight (GVW). May be required to unload truck. Requires commercial drivers' license. Includes tow truck drivers.

children.name: Light Truck Drivers
children.description: Drive a light vehicle, such as a truck or van, with a capacity of less than 26,001 pounds Gross Vehicle Weight (GVW), primarily to pick up merchandise or packages from a distribution center and deliver. May load and unload vehicle.

children.name: Taxi Drivers and Chauffeurs
children.description: Drive automobiles or limousines to transport passengers. Collect fares, assist with luggage, and follow local driving regulations.

children.name: Taxi Drivers and Chauffeurs
children.description: Drive automobiles, vans, or limousines to transport passengers. May occasionally carry cargo. Includes hearse drivers.

children.name: Miscellaneous Motor Vehicle Operators
children.description: Operate specialized motor vehicles, not included under other standard driver categories, possibly including shuttle or vehicle test drivers.

children.name: Motor Vehicle Operators, All Other
children.description: All motor vehicle operators not listed separately.

children.name: Motor Vehicle Operators
children.description: The "53-3000 Motor Vehicle Operators" category includes a range of occupations involving the operation of motor vehicles to transport people and goods. This category includes jobs such as bus drivers, taxi drivers, truck drivers, ambulance drivers, and more. Each of these jobs requires specific skills, certifications, and knowledge about safety regulations.

children.name: Rail Transportation Workers
children.description: The "53-4000 Rail Transportation Workers" category includes occupations that involve the operation and maintenance of trains and rail systems. This includes roles such as locomotive engineers, conductors, and yardmasters, among others. These workers ensure the safe and efficient transportation of passengers and goods via rail systems.

children.name: Locomotive Engineers and Operators
children.description: Drive locomotives to transport passengers or freight. Monitor instruments, interpret signals, and oversee safe train operation.

children.name: Locomotive Engineers
children.description: Drive electric, diesel-electric, steam, or gas-turbine-electric locomotives to transport passengers or freight. Interpret train orders, electronic or manual signals, and railroad rules and regulations.

children.name: Locomotive Firers
children.description: Monitor locomotive instruments and watch for dragging equipment, obstacles on rights-of-way, and train signals during run. Watch for and relay traffic signals from yard workers to yard engineer in railroad yard.

children.name: Rail Yard Engineers, Dinkey Operators, and Hostlers
children.description: Drive switching or other locomotive or dinkey engines within railroad yard, industrial plant, quarry, construction project, or similar location.

children.name: Railroad Brake, Signal, and Switch Operators
children.description: Operate track switches, couple or uncouple cars, or assist in controlling train movement. Monitor signals, follow dispatchers’ instructions, and maintain safety.

children.name: Railroad Brake, Signal, and Switch Operators
children.description: Operate railroad track switches. Couple or uncouple rolling stock to make up or break up trains. Signal engineers by hand or flagging. May inspect couplings, air hoses, journal boxes, and hand brakes.

children.name: Railroad Conductors and Yardmasters
children.description: Coordinate train crew activities, manage railcars, and operate within rail yards to ensure safe train assembly and movement.

children.name: Railroad Conductors and Yardmasters
children.description: Coordinate activities of switch-engine crew within railroad yard, industrial plant, or similar location. Conductors coordinate activities of train crew on passenger or freight trains. Yardmasters review train schedules and switching orders and coordinate activities of workers engaged in railroad traffic operations, such as the makeup or breakup of trains and yard switching.

children.name: Subway and Streetcar Operators
children.description: Drive electric-powered streetcars or subways. Follow schedules, stop at designated stations, operate doors, and ensure passenger safety.

children.name: Subway and Streetcar Operators
children.description: Operate subway or elevated suburban trains with no separate locomotive, or electric-powered streetcar, to transport passengers. May handle fares.

children.name: Miscellaneous Rail Transportation Workers
children.description: Perform tasks in rail transportation not covered by other job titles. Might include specialized signaling, track inspection, or passenger assistance roles.

children.name: Rail Transportation Workers, All Other
children.description: All rail transportation workers not listed separately.

children.name: Water Transportation Workers
children.description: The "53-5000 Water Transportation Workers" category encompasses occupations that involve the operation and maintenance of vessels that transport passengers and cargo over water. This includes roles such as ship captains, mates, sailors, marine oilers, and ship engineers. These workers are responsible for managing the vessel, ensuring the safety of passengers and cargo, and maintaining the ship's equipment and structures.

children.name: Sailors and Marine Oilers
children.description: Stand watch, handle lines, or maintain decks on ships or other water vessels. Lubricate machinery, repair cables, and manage onboard tasks for efficient operation.

children.name: Sailors and Marine Oilers
children.description: Stand watch to look for obstructions in path of vessel, measure water depth, turn wheel on bridge, or use emergency equipment as directed by captain, mate, or pilot. Break out, rig, overhaul, and store cargo-handling gear, stationary rigging, and running gear. Perform a variety of maintenance tasks to preserve the painted surface of the ship and to maintain line and ship equipment. Must hold government-issued certification and tankerman certification when working aboard liquid-carrying vessels. Includes able seamen and ordinary seamen.

children.name: Ship and Boat Captains and Operators
children.description: Command water vessels like tugboats, ferries, or cargo ships. Navigate routes, supervise crew, and ensure safe loading and unloading of cargo or passengers.

children.name: Captains, Mates, and Pilots of Water Vessels
children.description: Command or supervise operations of ships and water vessels, such as tugboats and ferryboats. Required to hold license issued by U.S. Coast Guard.

children.name: Ship and Boat Captains
children.description: Command vessels in oceans, bays, lakes, rivers, or coastal waters.

children.name: Mates- Ship, Boat, and Barge
children.description: Supervise or coordinate activities of crew aboard ships, boats, barges, or dredges.

children.name: Pilots, Ship
children.description: Command ships to steer them into and out of harbors, estuaries, straits, or sounds, or on rivers, lakes, or bays. Must be licensed by U.S. Coast Guard with limitations indicating class and tonnage of vessels for which license is valid and route and waters that may be piloted.

children.name: Motorboat Operators
children.description: Operate small motor-driven boats. May assist in navigational activities.

children.name: Ship Engineers
children.description: Operate and maintain engines and related systems aboard ships. Monitor machinery, troubleshoot issues, and oversee repairs to ensure vessel safety.

children.name: Ship Engineers
children.description: Supervise and coordinate activities of crew engaged in operating and maintaining engines, boilers, deck machinery, and electrical, sanitary, and refrigeration equipment aboard ship.

children.name: Other Transportation Workers
children.description: The "53-6000 Other Transportation Workers" category includes a variety of occupations that involve transportation services not classified in other categories. This includes roles such as parking lot attendants, automotive and watercraft service attendants, transportation inspectors, freight and cargo inspectors, and bridge and lock tenders.

children.name: Bridge and Lock Tenders
children.description: Operate and monitor drawbridges, locks, or similar mechanisms to allow boat traffic. Communicate with vessel operators and manage signals or gates.

children.name: Bridge and Lock Tenders
children.description: Operate and tend bridges, canal locks, and lighthouses to permit marine passage on inland waterways, near shores, and at danger points in waterway passages. May supervise such operations. Includes drawbridge operators, lock operators, and slip bridge operators.

children.name: Parking Lot Attendants
children.description: Park or retrieve vehicles for customers at parking facilities. Collect fees, provide directions, and maintain orderly traffic flow.

children.name: Parking Attendants
children.description: Park vehicles or issue tickets for customers in a parking lot or garage. May park or tend vehicles in environments such as a car dealership or rental car facility. May collect fee.

children.name: Automotive and Watercraft Service Attendants
children.description: Provide fueling, cleaning, or routine maintenance for cars or boats. May check fluid levels, wash vehicles, and offer basic customer service.

children.name: Automotive and Watercraft Service Attendants
children.description: Service automobiles, buses, trucks, boats, and other automotive or marine vehicles with fuel, lubricants, and accessories. Collect payment for services and supplies. May lubricate vehicle, change motor oil, refill antifreeze, or replace lights or other accessories, such as windshield wiper blades or fan belts. May repair or replace tires.

children.name: Traffic Technicians
children.description: Collect and analyze traffic data, set up traffic counters, evaluate patterns, and suggest traffic flow improvements.

children.name: Traffic Technicians
children.description: Conduct field studies to determine traffic volume, speed, effectiveness of signals, adequacy of lighting, and other factors influencing traffic conditions, under direction of traffic engineer.

children.name: Transportation Inspectors
children.description: Examine transportation equipment (aircraft, ships, or railcars) to ensure compliance with regulations. Check safety devices, review documentation, and investigate accidents.

children.name: Transportation Inspectors
children.description: Inspect equipment or goods in connection with the safe transport of cargo or people. Includes rail transportation inspectors, such as freight inspectors, rail inspectors, and other inspectors of transportation vehicles not elsewhere classified.

children.name: Aviation Inspectors
children.description: Inspect aircraft, maintenance procedures, air navigational aids, air traffic controls, and communications equipment to ensure conformance with Federal safety regulations.

children.name: Transportation Vehicle, Equipment and Systems Inspectors, Except Aviation
children.description: Inspect and monitor transportation equipment, vehicles, or systems to ensure compliance with regulations and safety standards.

children.name: Freight and Cargo Inspectors
children.description: Inspect the handling, storage, and stowing of freight and cargoes.

children.name: Transportation Attendants, Except Flight Attendants
children.description: Provide services to ensure passenger comfort or safety on trains, ships, or buses. Greet passengers, check tickets, and offer basic assistance.

children.name: Passenger Attendants
children.description: Provide services to ensure the safety of passengers aboard ships, buses, trains, or within the station or terminal. Perform duties such as explaining the use of safety equipment, serving meals or beverages, or answering questions related to travel.

children.name: Miscellaneous Transportation Workers
children.description: Occupations in transportation support not classified elsewhere. May include auto transporters, people who pilot specialized vehicles, or traffic escorts.

children.name: Transportation Workers, All Other
children.description: All transportation workers not listed separately.

children.name: Material Moving Workers
children.description: The "53-7000 Material Moving Workers" category covers occupations that involve moving freight, stock, or other materials or helping others to move materials. This includes roles such as conveyor operators, crane and tower operators, dredge operators, hoist and winch operators, industrial truck and tractor operators, cleaners of vehicles and equipment, laborers and freight, stock, and material movers, hand packers, and packagers.

children.name: Conveyor Operators and Tenders
children.description: Control conveyor systems to move materials or products. Adjust speeds, distribute loads, and clear jams to maintain safe, efficient flow.

children.name: Conveyor Operators and Tenders
children.description: Control or tend conveyors or conveyor systems that move materials or products to and from stockpiles, processing stations, departments, or vehicles. May control speed and routing of materials or products.

children.name: Crane and Tower Operators
children.description: Operate mechanical cranes or towers to lift, move, and position loads. Calculate load weights, follow signals, and monitor equipment performance.

children.name: Crane and Tower Operators
children.description: Operate mechanical boom and cable or tower and cable equipment to lift and move materials, machines, or products in many directions.

children.name: Dredge, Excavating, and Loading Machine Operators
children.description: Use machinery to scoop or scrape earth, sand, gravel, or other materials. Dredge waterways or load trucks in construction or mining.

children.name: Dredge Operators
children.description: Operate dredge to remove sand, gravel, or other materials in order to excavate and maintain navigable channels in waterways.

children.name: Excavating and Loading Machine and Dragline Operators
children.description: Operate or tend machinery equipped with scoops, shovels, or buckets, to excavate and load loose materials.

children.name: Loading Machine Operators, Underground Mining
children.description: Operate underground loading machine to load coal, ore, or rock into shuttle or mine car or onto conveyors. Loading equipment may include power shovels, hoisting engines equipped with cable-drawn scraper or scoop, or machines equipped with gathering arms and conveyor.

children.name: Hoist and Winch Operators
children.description: Operate hoists or winches to move loads vertically. Work with riggers or crane operators, follow signals, and keep logs of materials moved.

children.name: Hoist and Winch Operators
children.description: Operate or tend hoists or winches to lift and pull loads using power-operated cable equipment.

children.name: Industrial Truck and Tractor Operators
children.description: Drive industrial trucks or tractors equipped with forklifts, booms, or other devices to move materials in warehouses or construction sites.

children.name: Industrial Truck and Tractor Operators
children.description: Operate industrial trucks or tractors equipped to move materials around a warehouse, storage yard, factory, construction site, or similar location.

children.name: Laborers and Material Movers, Hand
children.description: Manually move freight, stock, or other materials. May load or unload trucks, carry items, or sort shipments in warehouses or production facilities.

children.name: Cleaners of Vehicles and Equipment
children.description: Wash or otherwise clean vehicles, machinery, and other equipment. Use such materials as water, cleaning agents, brushes, cloths, and hoses.

children.name: Laborers and Freight, Stock, and Material Movers, Hand
children.description: Manually move freight, stock, luggage, or other materials, or perform other general labor. Includes all manual laborers not elsewhere classified.

children.name: Machine Feeders and Offbearers
children.description: Feed materials into or remove materials from machines or equipment that is automatic or tended by other workers.

children.name: Packers and Packagers, Hand
children.description: Pack or package by hand a wide variety of products and materials.

children.name: Pumping Station Operators
children.description: Tend and maintain pumps for transferring materials like oil, gas, or water. Monitor pressure gauges, regulate flow, and perform routine maintenance.

children.name: Gas Compressor and Gas Pumping Station Operators
children.description: Operate steam-, gas-, electric motor-, or internal combustion-engine driven compressors. Transmit, compress, or recover gases, such as butane, nitrogen, hydrogen, and natural gas.

children.name: Pump Operators, Except Wellhead Pumpers
children.description: Tend, control, or operate power-driven, stationary, or portable pumps and manifold systems to transfer gases, oil, other liquids, slurries, or powdered materials to and from various vessels and processes.

children.name: Wellhead Pumpers
children.description: Operate power pumps and auxiliary equipment to produce flow of oil or gas from wells in oil field.

children.name: Refuse and Recyclable Material Collectors
children.description: Collect and transport garbage or recyclable materials from homes and businesses. Operate trucks or equipment, follow routes, and ensure safe disposal.

children.name: Refuse and Recyclable Material Collectors
children.description: Collect and dump refuse or recyclable materials from containers into truck. May drive truck.

children.name: Mine Shuttle Car Operators
children.description: Operate diesel or electric-powered shuttle cars in underground mines to transport coal or ore. Maneuver in tight spaces and maintain safety.

children.name: Mine Shuttle Car Operators
children.description: Operate diesel or electric-powered shuttle car in underground mine to transport materials from working face to mine cars or conveyor.

children.name: Tank Car, Truck, and Ship Loaders
children.description: Load and unload chemicals or bulk solids into or from tank cars, trucks, or ships. Use pumps, hoses, or conveyor belts and adhere to safety and environmental rules.

children.name: Tank Car, Truck, and Ship Loaders
children.description: Load and unload chemicals and bulk solids, such as coal, sand, and grain, into or from tank cars, trucks, or ships, using material moving equipment. May perform a variety of other tasks relating to shipment of products. May gauge or sample shipping tanks and test them for leaks.

children.name: Miscellaneous Material Moving Workers
children.description: Conduct specialized material-moving duties not included in other categories, such as rigging, logging yard operations, or forklift duties in unique settings.

children.name: Material Moving Workers, All Other
children.description: All material moving workers not listed separately.

name: Military Specific Occupations
description: Encompasses all roles specific to the armed forces, including enlisted and officer positions. Individuals in these occupations perform national defense duties, from combat operations to specialized tactical support.

children.name: Military Officer Special and Tactical Operations Leaders
children.description: The "55-1000 Military Officer Special and Tactical Operations Leaders" category includes roles focused on leading operations and units in the U.S. Armed Forces. These include high-level leaders in special operations, such as those within the Army Special Forces, Navy SEALs, Air Force Special Operations, Marine Corps Special Operations, and other similar groups. It's important to note that military pay is not determined in the same way as civilian pay. It's primarily based on rank and years of service, and it includes allowances for housing, food, and other benefits.

children.name: Military Officer Special and Tactical Operations Leaders
children.description: Lead units in specialized military operations (infantry, special forces, or tactical teams). Plan missions, oversee personnel, coordinate logistics, and manage training.

children.name: Air Crew Officers
children.description: Perform and direct in-flight duties to ensure the successful completion of combat, reconnaissance, transport, and search and rescue missions. Duties include operating aircraft communications and radar equipment, such as establishing satellite linkages and jamming enemy communications capabilities; operating aircraft weapons and defensive systems; conducting preflight, in-flight, and postflight inspections of onboard equipment; and directing cargo and personnel drops.

children.name: Aircraft Launch and Recovery Officers
children.description: Plan and direct the operation and maintenance of catapults, arresting gear, and associated mechanical, hydraulic, and control systems involved primarily in aircraft carrier takeoff and landing operations. Duties include supervision of readiness and safety of arresting gear, launching equipment, barricades, and visual landing aid systems; planning and coordinating the design, development, and testing of launch and recovery systems; preparing specifications for catapult and arresting gear installations; evaluating design proposals; determining handling equipment needed for new aircraft; preparing technical data and instructions for operation of landing aids; and training personnel in carrier takeoff and landing procedures.

children.name: Armored Assault Vehicle Officers
children.description: Direct the operation of tanks, light armor, and amphibious assault vehicle units during combat situations on land or in aquatic environments. Duties include directing crew members in the operation of targeting and firing systems; coordinating the operation of advanced onboard communications and navigation equipment; directing the transport of personnel and equipment during combat; formulating and implementing battle plans, including the tactical employment of armored vehicle units; and coordinating with infantry, artillery, and air support units.

children.name: Artillery and Missile Officers
children.description: Manage personnel and weapons operations to destroy enemy positions, aircraft, and vessels.
